nodes.text: Crohn disease with bilious vomiting and distention suggests small-bowel obstruction from inflammatory or fibrotic narrowing.
Obtain CT with IV contrast; provide bowel rest, IV fluids, and nasogastric decompression.
**Inflammatory narrowing without abscess or perforation:** consider IV corticosteroids with gastroenterology and surgical monitoring.
**Persistent fibrotic stricture without ischemia:** consider selected endoscopic dilation, stricturoplasty, or resection.
**Ischemia, perforation, or peritonitis:** urgent surgical exploration.
After obstruction resolves, optimize Crohn maintenance treatment; medications do not reverse established fibrosis.

acne-vulgaris.name: Acne vulgaris
acne-vulgaris.scope: Comedonal, inflammatory, and nodulocystic acne, topical retinoids, benzoyl peroxide, oral antibiotics, isotretinoin, photosensitivity counseling
acne-vulgaris.core: Open or closed comedones with variable inflammatory papules, pustules, or nodules reflect pilosebaceous inflammation; severity and scarring determine treatment intensity.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Pubertal androgen activity, family history, occlusive products, friction
Exogenous androgens, glucocorticoids, lithium may provoke eruptions; irregular menses/hirsutism suggests androgen excess

rows.label: Clues
items: Face, chest, back commonly involved; mixed lesion types distinguish acne from monomorphic drug eruptions
Deep painful nodules, scars, or substantial psychosocial impairment justify early treatment escalation
Rapid virilization or severe sudden adult onset → assess endocrine/tumor cause

rows.label: Pathophys
items: **Androgens (testosterone, DHT) → sebum** + follicular hyperkeratinization + Cutibacterium acnes-driven inflammation
Topical retinoids normalize follicular shedding; benzoyl peroxide is bactericidal without antibiotic resistance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical morphology**; no routine culture or hormone testing for typical adolescent acne
Hyperandrogenic findings → pregnancy test and targeted testosterone/DHEAS evaluation
Before isotretinoin → pregnancy assessment when applicable, baseline lipids and liver enzymes; monitor during treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Combine topical mechanisms** and match intensity below; improvement requires weeks, maintenance prevents relapse
★ **Antibiotics require the topical backbone below**; never antibiotic monotherapy; limit systemic course
Adult hormonally driven acne → combined contraceptive or spironolactone when suitable; avoid spironolactone in pregnancy
★ Isotretinoin → **strict pregnancy prevention/testing**; avoid pregnancy during treatment and 1 month afterward
Pregnancy → azelaic acid/benzoyl peroxide options; avoid retinoids and tetracyclines

rows.label: Complications
items: Permanent scars, postinflammatory hyperpigmentation, depression; assess suicidal symptoms when present
Doxycycline → esophagitis/photosensitivity; isotretinoin → cheilitis, hypertriglyceridemia, hepatotoxicity
Avoid simultaneous isotretinoin + tetracycline because intracranial hypertension risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Noncomedogenic skin products, sunscreen**, gentle cleansing; avoid picking lesions
Doxycycline: water and remain upright; retinoids: gradual introduction to reduce irritation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Rosacea: flushing/telangiectasia without comedones
Folliculitis: monomorphic follicular pustules, often pruritic
Perioral dermatitis: periorificial papules, vermilion sparing, steroid exposure

acute-coronary-syndromes.name: Acute coronary syndromes
acute-coronary-syndromes.scope: Unstable angina, NSTEMI, STEMI, cardiac biomarkers, risk stratification (HEART/TIMI), antiplatelet and anticoagulation, reperfusion
acute-coronary-syndromes.core: Acute myocardial ischemia from coronary plaque disruption: distinguish occlusive infarction needing immediate reperfusion from non-ST-elevation syndromes needing risk-guided invasive management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CKD, age, premature family CAD
Cocaine/stimulants, anemia, tachyarrhythmia may provoke ischemia; distinguish supply-demand injury from plaque rupture

rows.label: Clues
items: Pressure with arm/jaw radiation, diaphoresis, nausea; older adults/diabetes may have dyspnea or epigastric pain alone
Inferior MI with hypotension, clear lungs, raised JVP → suspect RV infarction
★ New murmur, pulmonary edema, shock after MI → **mechanical complication**, urgent echo
Unexplained crash/syncope + ischemic ECG → primary MI; troponin over trauma imaging

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Platelet activation and thrombin-mediated clot reduce coronary perfusion; necrosis releases troponin
Type 2 MI: oxygen mismatch without acute atherothrombosis; treat precipitating cause

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG within 10 minutes**, repeat if nondiagnostic; serial high-sensitivity troponin using validated pathway
Posterior suspicion → V7–V9; inferior MI → right-sided leads; new LBBB alone insufficient for STEMI
★ **Do not wait for troponin before STEMI reperfusion**; bedside echo if diagnosis/complications uncertain
HEART ≤3 + negative serial troponins → low risk; TIMI/GRACE stratifies NSTE-ACS
STE: **V1–V6 → LAD**; **II, III, aVF + bradycardia → RCA**; I, aVL → circumflex

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Chewed aspirin**, P2Y12 inhibitor, anticoagulant such as heparin, high-intensity atorvastatin; oxygen only if hypoxemic
Nitroglycerin (**venodilation** → ↓preload) for pain unless hypotension, RV infarction, recent PDE5 inhibitor; avoid NSAIDs
★ STEMI → **primary PCI** within 90 minutes at PCI center, ≤120 minutes including transfer
IF PCI delay >120 minutes, symptoms <12 hours, no contraindication → fibrinolysis promptly, then transfer

rows.label: Complications
items: VT/VF, AV block, HF, cardiogenic shock; free-wall rupture
Later aneurysm/thrombus, embolism, Dressler syndrome; antithrombotics → bleeding
Post-MI murmur: **papillary rupture** → apical, no O₂ step-up; **septal rupture** → left sternal, RA→RV step-up

rows.label: Prevention
items: DAPT usually 12 months after ACS unless bleeding risk changes plan; cardiac rehabilitation, smoking cessation
ACE inhibitor/ARB for LV dysfunction; beta-blocker when stable, avoid in shock or acute decompensation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Aortic dissection: abrupt tearing pain/pulse deficit; anticoagulation or lysis dangerous
Pericarditis: positional pleuritic pain, diffuse changes
PE: hypoxemia, thrombotic risk, RV strain

table.title: Syndrome branches
rows: Urgent catheterization if unstable; otherwise risk-guided angiography
Regional ST elevation or occlusion equivalent
Prior intracranial hemorrhage, active bleeding, suspected dissection
Stress or perfusion testing within 72 hours

acute-kidney-injury.name: Acute kidney injury
acute-kidney-injury.core: Abrupt loss of renal filtration: separate impaired perfusion, parenchymal injury, and urinary obstruction before treating the cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Volume depletion, sepsis, cirrhosis, low-output heart failure (prerenal despite overload); baseline CKD increases vulnerability
NSAIDs constrict afferent arterioles; ACE inhibitors/ARBs reduce efferent tone during hypoperfusion
Aminoglycosides, pigment (dipstick blood, few RBCs), prolonged ischemia → tubular damage; antibiotics/PPIs → tubulointerstitial inflammation

rows.label: Clues
items: Oliguria, edema, uremic nausea; urine output may remain normal
AIN: fever, rash, eosinophilia sometimes present; classic triad often absent
★ Pulmonary edema, severe hyperkalemia, encephalopathy, pericarditis → **urgent renal support**
Anuria despite patent catheter after pelvic surgery + hydronephrosis → ureteral injury/ligation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced glomerular pressure, tubular epithelial injury, or backpressure → declining GFR

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ AKI: creatinine ↑≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 h, ≥1.5-fold within 7 days, or oliguria
Oliguria criterion: urine <0.5 mL/kg/h for ≥6 h; trend creatinine, electrolytes, fluid balance
★ **Urinalysis + microscopy**, medication review; bladder scan → renal ultrasound if obstruction possible
FeNa unreliable with diuretics, CKD, early obstruction; urine eosinophils neither sensitive nor specific
Unexplained persistent injury or suspected glomerulonephritis → nephrology, possible kidney biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe hyperkalemia → **IV calcium**, insulin/dextrose; refractory electrolyte disturbance → dialysis
Hypovolemia (postoperative oliguria, high urine specific gravity) → saline bolus; congestion → loop diuretic; no reflex fluids in overload
Stop nephrotoxins, all NSAIDs including celecoxib (intra-articular steroid for joint pain); persistent AIN → glucocorticoids; renal-dose drugs
★ Obstruction → **catheter or ureteral decompression**; monitor postobstructive diuresis
Dialysis: refractory acidosis, hyperkalemia, intoxication, overload, symptomatic uremia; no isolated creatinine threshold

rows.label: Complications
items: Arrhythmias, acidosis, volume overload; subsequent CKD
Recovery diuresis → dehydration and electrolyte losses

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain perfusion during illness; review nephrotoxic combinations and monitor renal function
Contrast in high-risk CKD → **periprocedural IV isotonic saline**; diuretics, mannitol, metformin stop don't protect
ACR now limits contrast prophylaxis mainly to eGFR <30; older exam questions may expect wider hydration

rows.label: Mimics
items: CKD: longstanding abnormalities, small echogenic kidneys, chronic anemia
Trimethoprim effect: creatinine rise without true GFR decline

acute-kidney-injury.evidence: Not checked online; established KDIGO diagnostic criteria and renal teaching.

acute-leukemias.name: Acute leukemias
acute-leukemias.scope: Acute myeloid leukemia, acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, bone marrow biopsy, Auer rods
acute-leukemias.core: Rapid marrow replacement produces cytopenias and circulating immature cells; acute promyelocytic leukemia with coagulopathy demands immediate treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors

rows.label: Clues

items: Clonal immature myeloid or lymphoid expansion displaces normal hematopoiesis
Blast differentiation arrest; cell turnover predisposes to urate/phosphate release

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC/differential and smear → bone marrow biopsy**, flow cytometry, cytogenetics
Usually ≥20% marrow/blood blasts; defining genetic abnormalities permit some AML diagnoses below threshold
BMP, uric acid, LDH, coagulation profile; lumbar puncture for ALL CNS evaluation after stabilization

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected APL → **ATRA immediately**, then arsenic trioxide-based regimen; correct coagulopathy aggressively
Febrile neutropenia → IV cefepime; symptomatic cytopenias → blood-product support
AML → cytarabine/daunorubicin; less-fit adults → azacitidine/venetoclax; selected patients → allogeneic transplant
ALL → vincristine/steroid/asparaginase-based chemotherapy + intrathecal methotrexate; BCR-ABL-positive → add imatinib
★ Tumor-lysis prevention → hydration/allopurinol; high risk → **rasburicase**, contraindicated with G6PD deficiency

rows.label: Complications
items: Leukostasis: respiratory distress/confusion → urgent cytoreduction; tumor lysis → AKI, arrhythmias
Treatment → opportunistic infection, infertility, cardiomyopathy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Leukemoid reaction: mature neutrophilia with toxic granulation, reactive trigger
Aplastic anemia: hypocellular marrow without blast expansion

acute-rheumatic-fever.name: Acute rheumatic fever
acute-rheumatic-fever.scope: Post-streptococcal sequela, revised Jones criteria (carditis, migratory polyarthritis, chorea), ASO titers, penicillin and prophylaxis
acute-rheumatic-fever.core: Immune-mediated illness weeks after group A streptococcal infection, featuring migratory arthritis, carditis, or chorea; prevent recurrent valve injury with antibiotic prophylaxis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: School-aged children, crowding, limited access to care, prior rheumatic fever; higher-risk endemic populations

rows.label: Clues
items: Migratory large-joint inflammation, new mitral regurgitation murmur, tachycardia out of proportion to fever
★ **Sydenham chorea**: involuntary movements, emotional lability, milkmaid grip; may appear months later
Erythema marginatum: evanescent nonpruritic rings; painless subcutaneous nodules over extensor surfaces

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Molecular mimicry with streptococcal antigens → valve, joint, **basal ganglia** inflammation; not direct cardiac infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Initial episode: **2 major or 1 major + 2 minor**, plus preceding GAS evidence
ASO/anti-DNase B rise or positive throat testing supports prior infection; titers do not prove active infection
★ **Doppler echocardiography for all suspected cases**; subclinical valvulitis counts as carditis
Isolated chorea or indolent carditis can establish diagnosis despite absent contemporaneous GAS evidence
High-risk populations use broader joint criteria and lower inflammatory cutoffs; avoid counting one feature twice

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Penicillin eradication** even if throat culture negative; naproxen or aspirin for arthritis
Carditis with heart failure → diuresis and cardiology care; severe chorea → valproate or carbamazepine
Severe carditis may receive glucocorticoids; anti-inflammatory drugs do not replace recurrence prophylaxis

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic rheumatic valve disease: mitral stenosis/regurgitation, atrial fibrillation, embolism, heart failure
Recurrent attacks accelerate permanent valvular damage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Treat GAS pharyngitis promptly; secondary benzathine penicillin usually every 4 weeks
No carditis: ≥5 years and through age 21; resolved carditis: ≥10 years and through 21
Residual valve disease: continue ≥10 years and through age 40; selected patients lifelong

rows.label: Mimics
items: Septic arthritis: one persistently inflamed joint, positive aspirate
Poststreptococcal reactive arthritis: less migratory, poorer NSAID response
Endocarditis: bacteremia, vegetations, persistent systemic infection

acute-rhinosinusitis.name: Acute rhinosinusitis
acute-rhinosinusitis.scope: Common cold, viral rhinosinusitis, acute bacterial rhinosinusitis criteria, symptomatic therapy, antibiotic stewardship
acute-rhinosinusitis.core: Acute nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, and facial pressure usually reflect a self-limited viral infection; duration and course identify likely bacterial disease.

rows.label: Dx

Suspected orbital/intracranial extension → contrast CT; MRI for intracranial definition
Refractory or unusual infection → ENT evaluation; routine nasal swab cultures unhelpful

items: ★ Viral illness → **saline irrigation, acetaminophen/NSAID**, oral pseudoephedrine (not young children); no antibiotics
Intranasal fluticasone for associated allergic inflammation; topical oxymetazoline at most 3 days
★ Uncomplicated bacterial illness + reliable follow-up → **watchful waiting** or antibiotics
Antibiotic choice: amoxicillin-clavulanate, usually 5–7 days in adults; penicillin allergy → doxycycline
Complication → admission, IV ampicillin-sulbactam, urgent ENT/ophthalmology; avoid empiric azithromycin because resistance

rows.label: Complications
items: Orbital cellulitis or abscess, cavernous sinus thrombosis, meningitis, intracranial abscess
Unnecessary antibiotics → diarrhea, C difficile, resistance

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hand hygiene, smoking avoidance, control allergic rhinitis
Sterile/distilled or previously boiled water for nasal irrigation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Allergic rhinitis: itching, sneezing, watery discharge without fever
Migraine: episodic disabling headache, photophobia, nausea
Dental infection: focal tooth pain, unilateral maxillary symptoms

table.title: Bacterial patterns
rows: Initial improvement → new fever or worsening symptoms

adult-immunizations.name: Adult immunizations
adult-immunizations.scope: Routine adult vaccines, immunocompromised and HIV, pregnancy, live-vaccine contraindications, chronic medical conditions (COPD, diabetes, liver disease), vaccine counseling and addressing hesitancy
adult-immunizations.core: Match vaccination to age, prior doses, pregnancy, immune status, and exposure risk; missed series resume without restarting.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **HepB**: all 19–59; ≥60 with risk/request; health worker anti-HBs negative post-series → revaccinate
**HIV any CD4**, liver disease/alcohol, COPD, diabetes, smoking → pneumococcal <50; liver → HepA/HepB
Asplenia → pneumococcal, MenACWY, MenB, Hib; HIV → MenACWY

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Pregnancy: **Tdap each pregnancy at 27–36 wk**; inactivated influenza any trimester
Maternal RSV: Abrysvo at 32–36 wk, September–January; previous pregnancy dose → infant antibody instead
RSV once: all ≥75; ages 50–74 with increased severe-disease risk

rows.label: Test
items: Anti-HBs/anti-HAV/VZV IgG positive → immune, skip; otherwise **do not delay vaccination** for serology
★ Immunocompromised ≥19 → recombinant zoster; HIV CD4 ≥200 permits MMR/varicella if nonimmune
HPV started <15 → two doses; ≥15 or immunocompromised → three

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **No live MMR, varicella, intranasal influenza**: severe immunosuppression, pregnancy (nonimmune → postpartum)
PCV15 → PPSV23: ≥8 weeks immunocompromised; older exams: PPSV23 alone; mild illness/antibiotics: no deferral
Hesitancy → elicit concern; inactivated influenza cannot cause flu, coincidental virus; refusal → document, revisit

table.title: Routine adult schedule
rows: Annual influenza; updated COVID-19 for all adults
Tdap once, then either every 10 years
PCV20/21 alone; PCV15 → PPSV23 after 1 year

airway-management.name: Airway management
airway-management.scope: Indications for endotracheal intubation (GCS <= 8, airway protection, respiratory failure), rapid sequence intubation, bag-valve-mask ventilation, difficult airway
airway-management.core: Secure the airway when oxygenation, ventilation, or protection fails; preparation and rescue oxygenation determine safety.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Facial/neck trauma, burns, angioedema, obesity, limited jaw opening or cervical mobility
Shock, severe hypoxemia, metabolic acidosis increase peri-intubation collapse risk

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **GCS ≤8**, absent protective reflexes, recurrent aspiration, apnea → assess need for definitive airway
Stridor, fatigue, rising CO₂, refractory hypoxemia, inability to handle secretions → impending failure
GCS alone imperfect: reversible intoxication without ventilation/protection failure may permit closely monitored observation
Toxic sore throat, drooling, stridor → epiglottitis: laryngoscopy + intubation in OR before imaging/cultures

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Upper-airway obstruction, depressed drive, or respiratory muscle failure prevents effective gas exchange
Induction/positive pressure reduces sympathetic tone and venous return, worsening hypotension

rows.label: Dx
items: Continuous pulse oximetry, ECG, BP; assess mouth opening, neck anatomy, aspiration risk
★ Confirm tracheal placement with **persistent waveform capnography**, then auscultation and chest radiograph for depth
Do not rely on chest movement, oxygen saturation, or auscultation alone

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Position, suction, **preoxygenate**; prepare BVM, supraglottic device, video laryngoscope, and surgical rescue
Two-person BVM with airway adjunct and oxygen; oral adjunct only without gag reflex
RSI: etomidate/ketamine + rocuronium/succinylcholine; provide immediate postintubation analgesia and sedation
★ Predicted difficult airway → awake intubation strategy; **cannot intubate/cannot oxygenate or shattered midface/mandible → cricothyrotomy**
Avoid succinylcholine: hyperkalemia, denervation, established major burns, neuromuscular disease, malignant hyperthermia risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Esophageal intubation, aspiration, dental injury, hypoxemia, cardiac arrest
Positive-pressure ventilation → barotrauma; prolonged ventilation → pneumonia, laryngeal injury
Right-mainstem tube → occludes right upper lobe bronchus → **alveolar collapse** (atelectasis), not air trapping
Prolonged intubation → **tracheomalacia**: dynamic expiratory collapse, localized wheeze, exertional dyspnea; not asthma

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Optimize **hemodynamics before induction**, use attempt limits and explicit backup plan
Head-of-bed elevation, oral care, daily sedation/ventilator liberation assessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic hyperventilation: preserved oxygenation/protection, respiratory alkalosis
Compensatory Kussmaul breathing: metabolic acidosis; losing minute ventilation can cause abrupt deterioration

airway-management.evidence: Not checked online; established emergency airway principles.

amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.name: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.scope: Upper and lower motor neuron signs, bulbar symptoms, preserved sensation, EMG/NCS findings, noninvasive positive pressure ventilation, riluzole, edaravone, end-of-life planning
amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.core: Progressive weakness with upper and lower motor neuron signs in multiple regions, usually with preserved sensation and sphincter function.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Middle/older adulthood, male sex; mostly sporadic, minority familial
Family history of motor neuron disease or frontotemporal dementia supports inherited susceptibility

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Atrophy, fasciculations + hyperreflexia/spasticity** within affected regions; asymmetric limb onset common
Bulbar disease: dysarthria, dysphagia, tongue wasting; pseudobulbar affect may accompany corticobulbar dysfunction
Orthopnea, morning headache, weak cough → ventilatory weakness; inward abdominal motion on inspiration → **diaphragmatic paralysis**
Ocular movement and sensation usually spared; some patients develop executive or behavioral impairment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Degeneration of corticospinal neurons and anterior horn/bulbar motor neurons; denervation spreads progressively

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical progression + EMG/NCS**: widespread **fibrillation potentials**, sharp waves, chronic denervation; sensory conduction normal
MRI brain/spine to exclude structural mimics; targeted B12, thyroid, CK, and other studies
Assess FVC, inspiratory strength, nocturnal gas exchange, swallow function, nutrition; no single definitive blood test

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Riluzole** modestly prolongs survival; edaravone may slow functional decline in selected patients
★ **Noninvasive ventilation** for symptomatic respiratory weakness improves comfort and survival
Swallow/nutrition support; discuss gastrostomy before severe respiratory decline; cough-assist and secretion management
Baclofen for spasticity, communication devices, physical/occupational support; multidisciplinary specialty care
Early shared planning for ventilation, feeding, advance directives, hospice; discuss choices before communication declines

rows.label: Complications
items: Respiratory failure is usual terminal event; aspiration, malnutrition, falls, immobility
Depression, caregiver burden; frontotemporal impairment may affect decision-making capacity

rows.label: Prevention
items: No primary prevention; aspiration/fall precautions, vaccination, nutritional support, respiratory surveillance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervical myelopathy: sensory level, sphincter changes, compressive MRI lesion
Myasthenia gravis: fatigable ocular weakness, no UMN signs
Multifocal motor neuropathy: conduction block, IVIG response

amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.evidence: Not checked online; established ALS diagnosis and supportive-treatment teaching.

angioedema.name: Angioedema
angioedema.scope: Hereditary angioedema (C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency, C4 level), ACE inhibitor-induced, mast cell-mediated vs bradykinin-mediated, acute airway compromise, C1-INH concentrate, icatibant
angioedema.core: Deep, transient swelling of lips, tongue, airway, or bowel; distinguishing histamine from bradykinin determines which drugs will work.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Allergens, NSAIDs, insect stings → mast cell activation
Hereditary attacks: autosomal dominant history, trauma, dental procedures, estrogen exposure
ACE inhibitors: attacks possible even after years of uneventful use

rows.label: Clues
items: Nonpitting, asymmetric edema; gastrointestinal attacks may cause severe colicky pain, vomiting
★ Hoarseness, stridor, drooling, rapidly progressive tongue swelling → **airway emergency**
Recurrent episodes beginning in childhood support hereditary disease; late onset suggests acquired deficiency

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Histamine increases vascular permeability through mast cell mediator release
C1-INH deficiency/dysfunction or impaired bradykinin breakdown → kallikrein-mediated vascular leakage

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Recurrent nonurticarial attacks → **C4 plus C1-INH level and function**; repeat abnormal results
Low C1-INH quantity → type I; normal/high quantity with low function → type II
Normal C4 does not fully exclude HAE; C1q low in acquired, usually normal in hereditary disease
ACE inhibitor-related disease: clinical diagnosis; complement usually normal

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Secure threatened airway early with expert intubation; prepare surgical airway
Uncertain mechanism with possible anaphylaxis → IM epinephrine immediately; do not await complement testing
★ ACE inhibitor-related: stop drug permanently; airway/supportive care; targeted drug evidence inconsistent
HAE attack: give available on-demand drug early; plasma if specific agents unavailable

rows.label: Complications
items: Asphyxiation, hypovolemia from bowel edema; unnecessary abdominal surgery after misdiagnosis
Recurrence may continue after ACE inhibitor discontinuation

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ HAE: on-demand rescue supply; procedure prophylaxis with C1-INH; avoid ACE inhibitors and estrogen
Frequent HAE attacks → lanadelumab, berotralstat, or scheduled C1-INH; screen first-degree relatives

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cellulitis: persistent warm, tender erythema with infection signs
Contact dermatitis: superficial pruritic, eczematous eruption rather than isolated deep swelling

table.title: Mediator guides treatment
rows: Epinephrine for anaphylaxis; H1 antihistamine adjunct

antepartum-bleeding.name: Antepartum bleeding
antepartum-bleeding.scope: Placenta previa, placental abruption, vasa previa, uterine rupture, transabdominal ultrasound before digital exam, Kleihauer-Betke test, emergent cesarean delivery
antepartum-bleeding.core: Bleeding in later pregnancy requires immediate maternal stabilization and fetal assessment, followed by placental localization before any digital cervical examination.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Previa: prior cesarean, multiparity; abruption: hypertension, cocaine, trauma, prior abruption
Vasa previa: velamentous cord, accessory placental lobe, IVF; rupture: uterine scar, obstructed labor

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Shock may exceed visible blood loss** with concealed abruption or internal hemorrhage
Assess uterine tone, pain, contractions, fetal tracing, membrane status; bleeding volume alone is unreliable

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Maternal placental bleeding versus fetal vessel hemorrhage; vasa previa can rapidly exsanguinate fetus
Placental separation or uterine disruption compromises oxygen delivery independent of maternal external blood loss

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ CBC, type/crossmatch, coagulation studies including fibrinogen; continuous fetal monitoring if viable
★ **Ultrasound before digital examination**; transabdominal first; transvaginal safely clarifies placenta–cervix relationship
Normal ultrasound does not exclude abruption; suspected rupture is a clinical emergency
Rh-negative bleeding/trauma → Kleihauer–Betke or flow cytometry quantifies fetomaternal hemorrhage for anti-D dosing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ ABCs, two large IVs, blood products when needed; **do not delay delivery for imaging if unstable**
Hemorrhage/fetal compromise → emergency cesarean; rupture → laparotomy, uterine repair or hysterectomy
Stable preterm previa → observation, pelvic rest, corticosteroids when eligible; planned cesarean before labor
Abruption: deliver if significant or compromised; vaginal birth possible when stable and imminent or fetal demise
Unsensitized Rh-negative patient → anti-D immunoglobulin; correct abruption-associated coagulopathy

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemorrhagic shock, DIC, AKI, hysterectomy; fetal hypoxia, death, prematurity
Previa plus cesarean scar increases placenta accreta spectrum risk and operative hemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Control BP, avoid cocaine/tobacco; prenatal placental/cord localization and planned high-risk delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bloody show: small mucus-streaked bleeding with cervical change
Cervical lesion: contact bleeding, visible source on speculum examination

table.title: Critical distinctions
rows: Bleeding after rupture; sudden fetal bradycardia
Scarred uterus; sudden pain, lost station, fetal bradycardia

antepartum-bleeding.evidence: Not checked online; established obstetric hemorrhage teaching.

antipsychotics.name: Antipsychotics
antipsychotics.scope: First-generation vs second-generation, extrapyramidal symptoms (acute dystonia, akathisia, parkinsonism, tardive dyskinesia), neuroleptic malignant syndrome, metabolic syndrome, hyperprolactinemia, QTc prolongation
antipsychotics.core: Dopamine-modulating drugs treat psychosis and mania; selection depends on motor, metabolic, endocrine, cardiovascular, and hematologic risks.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ Psychosis, mania, agitation; **SGA first-line**; **clozapine** if resistant or recurrent suicidality
FGA: mainly D2 antagonism; SGA: D2/5-HT2 effects, varying by agent
Quetiapine sedation → switch to aripiprazole; obesity → ziprasidone, not olanzapine/clozapine

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Nigrostriatal blockade → movement disorders; tuberoinfundibular blockade → prolactin elevation
Aripiprazole: partial D2 agonist; haloperidol high-potency FGA, chlorpromazine low-potency FGA
Chronic D2 blockade → receptor supersensitivity → tardive dyskinesia; can worsen after stopping

rows.label: Adverse
items: ★ Fever, **lead-pipe rigidity**, autonomic instability, high CK → NMS; stop drug, supportive ICU care
Severe NMS: dantrolene/bromocriptine; olanzapine/clozapine: weight gain, diabetes, dyslipidemia
Risperidone: ↑prolactin; ziprasidone: ↑QT; clozapine: neutropenia, myocarditis, ileus, seizures

rows.label: Avoid
items: Lewy body/Parkinson disease: severe sensitivity; specialist-selected quetiapine/clozapine if essential
Dementia: ↑mortality, falls; dangerous behavior after safer measures → low-dose **quetiapine**/risperidone, not benzodiazepines

rows.label: Interactions
items: Other QT-prolonging drugs, electrolyte depletion → torsades; sedatives/alcohol increase CNS depression
Metoclopramide, prochlorperazine block dopamine: same EPS, tardive dyskinesia, NMS; avoid after NMS

rows.label: Monitor
items: ★ Weight/BMI, BP, glucose/A1c, lipids; movement examinations; **ANC with clozapine**
ECG for cardiac/QT risks; prolactin when symptomatic; ask about bowel function
Clozapine + ANC <1000 → **hold clozapine**, not dose reduction; ANC 1000–1499 → continue, closer monitoring

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Anticholinergics worsen tardive dyskinesia**; valbenazine/deutetrabenazine are VMAT2 inhibitors
Akathisia can mimic worsening agitation; increasing antipsychotic dose can worsen it
Low-potency FGAs: more orthostasis/anticholinergic effects; high-potency FGAs: more EPS

table.title: Extrapyramidal syndromes
rows: Stop/switch culprit first; benztropine or amantadine

antipsychotics.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [FDA clozapine monitoring update](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/fda-removes-risk-evaluation-and-mitigation-strategy-rems-program-antipsychotic-drug-clozapine); other effects established teaching.

aortic-dissection.name: Aortic dissection
aortic-dissection.core: Sudden maximal chest or back pain with vascular or neurologic deficits suggests aortic dissection, even without widened mediastinum.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Long-standing hypertension → **medial degeneration** in older adults; bicuspid aortic valve, coarctation
Marfan/vascular Ehlers-Danlos, pregnancy, cocaine, aortic instrumentation or aneurysm

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Abrupt severe pain**, pulse/BP asymmetry, syncope, focal neurologic deficit
New aortic regurgitation murmur; limb ischemia or abdominal pain from branch-vessel malperfusion
Hypotension suggests rupture, tamponade, severe regurgitation, or coronary involvement

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Intimal tear → blood separates medial layers, creating false lumen
Propagation compromises branch arteries or ruptures into pericardium/pleura

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Stable → **CTA chest/abdomen/pelvis**; unstable or unable to leave resuscitation → bedside TEE
Chest radiograph may show widened mediastinum but normal film does not exclude dissection
ECG/troponin may mimic MI; high suspicion requires aortic imaging before antithrombotics
Examine bilateral arm pressures, femoral pulses, neurologic status, renal function

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IV esmolol or labetalol** + opioid analgesia; target HR 60–80 and SBP <120 if perfusion maintained
Persistent hypertension after rate control → nicardipine or nitroprusside; avoid vasodilator before beta blockade
★ **Avoid anticoagulation and thrombolysis** when dissection suspected
Tamponade from dissection → immediate surgical team; routine pericardiocentesis can worsen hemorrhage

rows.label: Complications
items: Aortic rupture, hemothorax, tamponade, MI, stroke, paraplegia, mesenteric/renal ischemia
Late aneurysmal dilation or recurrent dissection despite initial successful treatment

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Lifelong **BP control and surveillance CTA/MRA**; beta-blocker-based regimen
Avoid heavy isometric lifting; screen first-degree relatives for familial aortopathy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Acute coronary syndrome: pressure-like pain, no pulse deficit; coexistence possible
PE: pleuritic pain, hypoxemia, right-heart strain
Esophageal rupture: vomiting followed by pain and subcutaneous emphysema

aortic-dissection.evidence: Not checked online; established aortic emergency principles.

appendicitis.name: Appendicitis
appendicitis.scope: Acute appendicitis, clinical presentation, pediatric and pregnancy considerations, imaging (ultrasound, CT), surgical management
appendicitis.core: Periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant, followed by anorexia and nausea, suggests appendiceal inflammation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Adolescents/young adults; luminal obstruction by lymphoid hyperplasia or fecalith
Older adults may have obstructing neoplasm; immunosuppression can blunt findings

rows.label: Clues
items: McBurney tenderness, guarding, fever; Rovsing, psoas, or obturator signs depend on position
★ **Diffuse peritonitis, toxicity, hypotension** → perforation/sepsis until proven otherwise
Young children: nonspecific symptoms and rapid progression; pregnancy: displaced appendix, less reliable examination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Luminal obstruction → distention, venous congestion, bacterial invasion → ischemia/perforation
Visceral midgut pain precedes focal parietal peritoneal irritation

rows.label: Dx
items: CBC, urinalysis, **pregnancy test** in reproductive-age patients; pyuria does not exclude appendicitis
★ Stable nonpregnant adult → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast** when diagnosis uncertain
★ Child/pregnancy → **ultrasound first**; nondiagnostic → MRI without gadolinium, or CT in nonpregnant child
Noncompressible enlarged appendix >6 mm with periappendiceal inflammation supports diagnosis
Clear peritonitis → surgical evaluation; do not delay necessary operation for repeated imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ NPO, **IV fluids, IV opioids, ceftriaxone + metronidazole**, surgical consultation; opioids do not obscure exam
Laparoscopic appendectomy definitive; do not withhold necessary surgery during pregnancy
Selected uncomplicated cases → antibiotics after shared decision; recurrence/failure higher, especially with appendicolith
Localized abscess/phlegmon in stable patient → antibiotics ± image-guided drainage; follow-up based on age/risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Perforation, abscess, peritonitis, sepsis, ileus
Postoperative wound infection, intra-abdominal collection, adhesional obstruction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG, adnexal findings
Ovarian torsion: sudden unilateral pelvic pain; gastroenteritis: diarrhea prominent before diffuse cramping
Mesenteric adenitis: viral prodrome, normal appendix on imaging

appendicitis.evidence: Not checked online; established general-surgery evaluation and treatment principles.

bartholin-gland-cyst-and-abscess.name: Bartholin gland cyst and abscess
bartholin-gland-cyst-and-abscess.scope: Asymptomatic cyst, symptomatic cyst, acute Bartholin abscess, incision and drainage, Word catheter placement, marsupialization, excision for recurrent or older women
bartholin-gland-cyst-and-abscess.core: Obstructed posterior vestibular gland causing a cyst or abscess; durable drainage prevents recurrence, and age determines the need for malignancy assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive age, prior duct obstruction, previous cyst/abscess; usually polymicrobial vaginal/enteric flora
STIs may coexist but most abscesses are not solely gonococcal or chlamydial

rows.label: Clues
items: Cyst: soft fluctuant, often painless; abscess: marked tenderness, erythema, difficulty sitting/walking
Gland location near 4 or 8 o'clock at vaginal opening; usually unilateral
Firm, fixed, irregular, recurrent, or postmenopausal lesion → malignancy concern

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Duct occlusion retains gland secretions; bacterial infection produces purulence
Drainage without an epithelialized outlet allows rapid closure and recurrence

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical vulvar examination**; assess cellulitis, systemic illness, pregnancy, immune status
GC/chlamydia NAAT when sexual risk or cervicitis; culture selected recurrent/severe infections
★ **Biopsy at age ≥40 or suspicious mass**; imaging unnecessary for typical superficial lesion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Management branches below; **Word catheter about 4 weeks** permits an epithelialized drainage tract
★ Avoid **incision alone or needle aspiration**: rapid closure causes recurrence
Antibiotics only for cellulitis, systemic infection, immunocompromise, or confirmed STI; uncomplicated drainage needs none
Persistent recurrence → gland excision after acute inflammation settles

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent abscess, surrounding cellulitis, rare sepsis; early catheter expulsion can compromise tract formation
Excision → bleeding, scarring, dyspareunia; older patients risk missed gland malignancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Complete catheter follow-up, hygiene without irritating products; condoms/STI treatment for exposure-related infection
No proven universal prevention of duct obstruction; return promptly for recurrent pain, fever, or mass

rows.label: Mimics
items: Skene duct cyst: periurethral/anterior location
Epidermal inclusion cyst: superficial skin nodule, possible punctum
Hidradenitis: recurrent multiple intertriginous nodules, sinus tracts

bartholin-gland-cyst-and-abscess.evidence: Not checked online; established gynecologic office-procedure teaching.

benign-breast-conditions.name: Benign breast conditions
benign-breast-conditions.scope: Fibroadenoma, fibrocystic changes, intraductal papilloma, breast cyst, fat necrosis, galactocele, breast abscess
benign-breast-conditions.core: Breast symptoms require age-directed imaging and clinical–radiologic concordance; a benign-appearing examination alone cannot exclude malignancy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive hormonal cycling; milk stasis; breast trauma or prior surgery
Smoking predisposes to recurrent subareolar abscess
**Cracked, excoriated nipples** → main portal of entry for lactational mastitis

rows.label: Clues
items: Galactocele: cystic lactational/postlactational mass, no inflammation, varies with feeds; fat–fluid level on imaging
Mastitis: focal tender erythema, fever, no fluctuance; abscess adds **fluctuance**; often Staphylococcus aureus
★ Spontaneous unilateral **bloody single-duct discharge** → usually **papilloma**; exclude malignancy, persistent → surgical evaluation
Nonbloody discharge only on expression, normal exam → **physiologic**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hormone-responsive stromal/glandular tissue produces cyclic changes; duct obstruction causes retained secretions
Adipose injury causes inflammatory necrosis and calcification that can resemble cancer

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Palpable mass **<30 years → ultrasound**; ≥30 → diagnostic mammography with targeted ultrasound
Suspicious solid lesion or imaging–exam discordance → **core needle biopsy**
Simple cyst: anechoic, thin-walled, posterior enhancement; no solid component
Nonlactational abscess or persistent inflammation after antibiotics → exclude underlying carcinoma
Cyclic bilateral nodularity, no dominant mass → **reexamine after menses**, before imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Painful simple cyst → aspiration; nonbloody fluid + full collapse → benign; bloody fluid/residual mass → **biopsy**
Fibroadenoma → observe when concordant; excise if rapidly enlarging, large or symptomatic
Breast pain, no mass, young, normal exam → **reassurance**; fibrocystic pain → supportive bra, topical/oral NSAID
★ Mastitis → **dicloxacillin/cephalexin**, keep breastfeeding/pumping; abscess → add needle/incision drainage; MRSA → clindamycin
Tender lactating lump, no erythema/fever → **warm compresses**, keep nursing; persistent galactocele → aspiration

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent periductal abscess → fistula; incomplete drainage → persistent infection
Proliferative lesions with atypia increase future cancer risk; simple cysts do not

rows.label: Prevention
items: Effective breast emptying during lactation; smoking cessation for recurrent periductal disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cancer: irregular fixed mass, retraction or suspicious nodes
Phyllodes: rapidly enlarging fibroepithelial mass requiring excision

table.title: Common benign findings
rows: Early postpartum; bilateral tense tender breasts, low fever

benign-breast-conditions.evidence: Not checked online; established breast diagnostic principles.

benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.scope: Lower urinary tract symptoms, medical therapy, urinary retention and obstructive uropathy
benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.core: Aging man with hesitancy, weak stream, incomplete emptying, and nocturia from benign periurethral prostatic enlargement.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, androgen exposure, family history, obesity/metabolic syndrome
Anticholinergics, opioids, and sympathomimetic decongestants can precipitate retention

rows.label: Clues
items: Storage symptoms: urgency, frequency; voiding symptoms: straining, intermittency, terminal dribbling
Smooth, symmetric enlarged prostate; size correlates imperfectly with symptom severity
★ **Painful inability to void** with palpable bladder → acute urinary retention
Renal dysfunction or bilateral hydronephrosis suggests high-pressure obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dihydrotestosterone-driven transition-zone hyperplasia + alpha-adrenergic smooth-muscle tone obstruct bladder outlet

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis**, symptom score, examination; review medications and neurologic disease
Postvoid residual if incomplete emptying suspected; creatinine/renal ultrasound for obstruction or renal impairment
PSA after shared decision-making if result changes management; elevation not specific for cancer

rows.label: Tx
items: Mild, nonbothersome → observation; reduce evening fluids, caffeine, alcohol; timed voiding
★ Acute retention → **urethral catheter**, then alpha-blocker and voiding trial; suprapubic drainage if catheterization fails
★ Refractory symptoms, retention, recurrent UTIs, stones, renal impairment → **TURP or other outlet procedure**
Monitor urine output/electrolytes after relief of prolonged obstruction

rows.label: Complications
items: Overflow incontinence, recurrent infection, bladder stones, postrenal AKI
Postobstructive diuresis; surgery → bleeding, retrograde ejaculation, urethral stricture

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid precipitating drugs; reassess progressive symptoms and residual volume
BPH does not transform into prostate cancer; continue independent cancer-risk discussion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Prostate cancer: hard asymmetric nodule
Prostatitis: tender prostate, fever; neurogenic bladder: neurologic disease, altered bladder sensation

table.title: Medication selection
rows: Large gland; reduce progression over months

bipolar-disorder.name: Bipolar disorder
bipolar-disorder.scope: Bipolar I (manic episode, DIG FAST), bipolar II (hypomania and major depression), cyclothymic disorder, acute mania pharmacotherapy (antipsychotics, lithium, valproate), maintenance therapy
bipolar-disorder.core: Distinct episodes of pathologically increased energy with elevated or irritable mood distinguish bipolar illness from ordinary mood variability.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Strong family history; typical onset adolescence/young adulthood
Sleep deprivation, antidepressants, stimulants, substances can precipitate episodes

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **DIG FAST**: distractibility, impulsivity, grandiosity, flight of ideas, activity, decreased sleep need, talkativeness
≥3 associated symptoms; ≥4 if mood only irritable
Mania: psychosis, marked impairment, risky spending/sex, or hospitalization; reduced sleep without fatigue

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Multifactorial genetic vulnerability with dysregulated mood, reward and circadian systems

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical longitudinal history + collateral**; ask about prior elevated episodes before treating depression
Assess suicidality, pregnancy, substance use; TSH, metabolic panel, toxicology to exclude secondary causes
Hospitalization requirement can establish manic duration criterion even before one week
Major depression ≥2 weeks; hypomania causes no psychosis, marked impairment or hospitalization
Cyclothymia: symptoms ≥half the time; no symptom-free interval >2 months or full mood episodes

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute mania → **antipsychotic** (olanzapine/quetiapine); severe → add lithium/valproate; mixed/rapid cycling → **divalproex**
Unsafe, psychotic, severely agitated, or unable to care for self → hospitalization
Depression → quetiapine, lurasidone, lithium, lamotrigine; urgent/refractory or first-trimester psychotic mania → **ECT**
★ **Avoid antidepressant monotherapy**; lamotrigine does not treat acute mania
Maintenance: lithium, quetiapine, valproate or lamotrigine selected by episode pattern; lithium reduces suicide risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, substance misuse, financial/relationship loss; metabolic adverse effects of antipsychotics
Lithium: renal/thyroid toxicity; valproate/carbamazepine: teratogenicity, avoid in first trimester; lamotrigine: severe rash

rows.label: Prevention
items: Regular sleep, psychoeducation, relapse-sign monitoring, maintenance adherence; avoid stimulants and substance misuse

rows.label: Mimics
items: ADHD: chronic baseline symptoms rather than distinct mood episodes
Borderline personality: brief reactive shifts linked to interpersonal stress
Medication/substance-induced mania: onset after antidepressant, stimulant, steroid → **stop culprit first**
Hyperthyroidism: heat intolerance, tremor, low TSH

table.title: Diagnostic branches
rows: Hypomania ≥4 days + major depression; never mania

bowel-obstruction.name: Bowel obstruction
bowel-obstruction.scope: Small bowel obstruction (adhesions, hernia), large bowel obstruction (volvulus, malignancy), paralytic ileus, NG decompression, surgical management
bowel-obstruction.core: Colicky abdominal pain, vomiting, distention, and obstipation suggest mechanical obstruction; constant pain or systemic toxicity raises concern for strangulation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior abdominal surgery (**adhesions**, leading cause), incarcerated hernia, Crohn strictures → small-bowel obstruction
Colorectal malignancy, chronic constipation, institutionalization → large-bowel obstruction or sigmoid volvulus
Recent surgery, opioids, hypokalemia, severe systemic illness → ileus

rows.label: Clues
items: Early high-pitched sounds may become absent; proximal obstruction causes earlier vomiting, distal disease greater distention
★ **Peritonitis, fever, tachycardia, rising lactate**, or continuous severe pain → ischemia/perforation
Complete → **obstipation**, no flatus; partial may still pass stool/diarrhea, not excluding obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Luminal blockage → upstream dilation, third spacing; closed loop compromises venous then arterial supply
Adynamic ileus reflects impaired motility without an anatomic transition point

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast** defines transition point, cause, and ischemic signs
CBC, electrolytes, creatinine, lactate; normal lactate cannot exclude early ischemia
Radiograph may show dilated loops/air-fluid levels, no rectal gas; CT more definitive if diagnosis uncertain
★ Massive colonic distention + **coffee-bean (inverted-U) loop** on radiograph → sigmoid volvulus
Pregnancy: plain radiograph acceptable first (minimal fetal dose); MRI if unclear; do not delay

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **NPO, IV isotonic fluids, electrolyte correction**; NG decompression for significant vomiting/distention
★ Strangulation, perforation, closed loop, or incarcerated hernia → **urgent surgery** + ceftriaxone/metronidazole
Uncomplicated adhesive SBO → surgical observation, serial examination; water-soluble contrast helps predict resolution
Failure to improve during a short monitored trial, commonly up to 72 h → operation
Ileus → correct trigger, reduce opioids, mobilize; no operation solely for absent sounds

rows.label: Complications
items: Dehydration, AKI, hypokalemic alkalosis; bowel necrosis, perforation, sepsis
Recurrent adhesions; short-bowel syndrome after extensive resection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early postoperative ambulation, opioid-sparing analgesia, electrolyte correction; elective repair of symptomatic hernias

rows.label: Mimics
items: Gastroenteritis: prominent diarrhea, no focal transition point
Mesenteric ischemia: pain out of proportion before peritoneal signs
Ileus: hypoactive/absent sounds, gas throughout bowel including rectum
Diabetic autonomic neuropathy: dysmotility, dilated loops without transition point

table.title: Large-bowel branches
rows: Sigmoidoscopic detorsion, rectal tube → same-admission resection

bowel-obstruction.evidence: Not checked online; established acute surgical management principles.

breast-neoplasia.name: Breast neoplasia
breast-neoplasia.scope: Ductal carcinoma in situ, invasive ductal and lobular carcinoma, receptor status (ER, PR, HER2), metastatic disease (bone, visceral), surgical management, endocrine and chemotherapy
breast-neoplasia.core: A suspicious breast lesion requires core biopsy, assessment of invasion and ER/PR/HER2 status to guide local and systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, BRCA-related syndromes, close-relative family history (distant relative adds little), prior chest irradiation
**Combined estrogen-progestin therapy**, prolonged estrogen, postmenopausal obesity, alcohol; atypical proliferative lesions

rows.label: Clues
items: Painless hard irregular mass, skin/nipple retraction, unilateral bloody discharge or axillary node
★ Peau d’orange, diffuse erythema and edema → **inflammatory breast cancer**, even without discrete mass
Persistent unilateral eczematous nipple lesion → Paget disease; **full-thickness biopsy**, investigate underlying carcinoma

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Invasion through basement membrane enables lymphatic/hematogenous metastasis
ER/PR signaling and HER2 amplification create actionable tumor drivers; triple-negative tumors lack these targets

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Diagnostic mammography + targeted ultrasound** → core biopsy of suspicious lesion; pregnancy → **ultrasound first**
Pathology: invasion, grade, **ER/PR/HER2**; assess regional nodes clinically and with targeted imaging
Clinically node-negative invasive disease, including microinvasion ≤1 mm → sentinel node biopsy during definitive surgery
Distant staging scans for advanced disease or suspicious symptoms; not every small asymptomatic cancer
Axillary node adenocarcinoma, normal mammogram → occult breast primary; breast MRI

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early: lumpectomy + radiation or mastectomy; **positive margins → reexcision** before adjuvant therapy
ER-positive → tamoxifen or postmenopausal aromatase inhibitor; chemotherapy based on stage/biology
★ HER2-positive → **trastuzumab-based** treatment, monitor LVEF; triple-negative → chemotherapy ± pembrolizumab if higher-risk
Locally advanced → neoadjuvant treatment, then surgery/radiation; large residual + palpable nodes → **mastectomy + axillary dissection**
Bone metastases → **zoledronate/denosumab**; systemic treatment by receptors, chemotherapy for visceral crisis

rows.label: Complications
items: Metastases to bone (often **mixed lytic–blastic**), lung, liver, brain; surgery/radiation → lymphedema
Tamoxifen → VTE/endometrial cancer; aromatase inhibitors → bone loss; trastuzumab → cardiomyopathy
Prior cancer + severe hypercalcemia, lytic lesions → recurrence; thiazide/calcium supplements cause only mild elevation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Age/risk-based screening, genetic counseling for suggestive pedigree; selected high-risk patients → chemoprevention
BRCA-related very high risk → discuss risk-reducing surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mastitis: lactation-associated tenderness/fever, improves with antibiotics
Fat necrosis: trauma/surgery history; biopsy if discordant imaging

table.title: Histologic distinctions
rows: Bilateral risk marker; discohesive lobular cells
Surveillance/risk reduction if concordant; later cancer usually ductal

breast-neoplasia.evidence: Not checked online; established breast-oncology management principles.

bronchiectasis.name: Bronchiectasis
bronchiectasis.scope: Cystic fibrosis, post-infectious, high-resolution CT, airway clearance, pseudomonas colonization, acute exacerbation
bronchiectasis.core: Chronic productive cough with recurrent respiratory infections and permanently dilated bronchi on high-resolution CT.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cystic fibrosis, prior severe pneumonia/TB, primary ciliary dyskinesia, aspiration, immunodeficiency
ABPA, rheumatoid arthritis, obstructing endobronchial lesion; some cases remain idiopathic

rows.label: Clues
items: Copious purulent sputum, coarse crackles, recurrent focal infections, hemoptysis, sometimes clubbing
Exacerbation: increased sputum volume/purulence, cough, dyspnea, fatigue; hypoxemia or sepsis → severe disease
Early lifelong infections, sinusitis, infertility, or situs inversus suggest impaired ciliary clearance
Child: chronic cough refractory to bronchodilators, steroids, antibiotics + persistent focal collapse/consolidation → localized bronchiectasis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired mucus clearance → persistent infection and neutrophilic inflammation → irreversible airway wall destruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **High-resolution chest CT**: signet-ring bronchi, absent tapering, airways visible near pleura, cystic spaces ± air-fluid levels
Sputum bacterial and mycobacterial cultures; spirometry measures associated airflow limitation
Quantitative immunoglobulins; total IgE/Aspergillus testing for ABPA; sweat chloride if CF suspected
Localized disease → bronchoscopy for tumor/foreign body; diffuse disease → investigate systemic cause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Daily **airway clearance**, exercise; bronchodilator for obstruction; no routine inhaled steroids or non-CF dornase alfa
★ Exacerbation → sputum culture then antibiotics guided by prior isolates; often **14 days**
Pseudomonas susceptible → ciprofloxacin; severe infection → IV cefepime or piperacillin-tazobactam
★ ≥2 yearly or ≥1 severe exacerbation → azithromycin after NTM exclusion; chronic Pseudomonas → inhaled tobramycin
Massive hemoptysis → airway protection and bronchial artery embolization; focal refractory disease → resection evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic Pseudomonas colonization, resistant infection, respiratory failure, pulmonary hypertension
Antibiotic toxicity/resistance; macrolides can cause QT prolongation and hearing impairment

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, influenza/pneumococcal vaccination, aspiration management, treatment of underlying immunodeficiency
New Pseudomonas isolation → specialist eradication regimen, often ciprofloxacin followed by inhaled antibiotic

rows.label: Mimics
items: Chronic bronchitis: smoking-related sputum without characteristic bronchial dilation
Lung abscess: solitary cavity with air-fluid level; no lifelong productive cough
Pulmonary TB: constitutional illness and compatible imaging; mycobacterial testing confirms

cardiomyopathies.name: Cardiomyopathies
cardiomyopathies.scope: Dilated cardiomyopathy, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, restrictive cardiomyopathy, stress (Takotsubo) cardiomyopathy, viral myocarditis, diagnostic evaluation, management
cardiomyopathies.core: Myocardial disease causes pump failure, impaired filling, dynamic obstruction, or arrhythmias; echocardiography defines the phenotype.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dilated: familial disease, alcohol, anthracyclines, peripartum state, **viral myocarditis**
Hypertrophic: autosomal dominant sarcomeric variants; restrictive: amyloid, hemochromatosis, radiation
Takotsubo: emotional/physical stress; myocarditis: recent viral illness, immune checkpoint inhibitors

rows.label: Clues
items: Exertional dyspnea, edema, elevated JVP; **displaced PMI**, S3 → dilated LV; syncope/ventricular arrhythmia signals danger
★ Obstructive HCM murmur **↑Valsalva/standing**, ↓squatting/handgrip; exertional presyncope
Myocarditis: chest discomfort, tachycardia disproportionate to fever, acute heart failure

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Sarcomere dysfunction or myocardial injury → remodeling; infiltration → reduced ventricular compliance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG, troponin, BNP → transthoracic echo**; assess coronary ischemia when suspected
Cardiac MRI: inflammation, scar, infiltrative patterns; iron studies or monoclonal protein testing when relevant
Endomyocardial biopsy: selected fulminant unexplained failure, malignant arrhythmias, suspected giant-cell myocarditis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ HFrEF: **ARNI, evidence-based beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2 inhibitor**; loop diuretic for congestion
Obstructive HCM: nonvasodilating beta-blocker (propranolol, metoprolol); alternative verapamil/diltiazem
Refractory obstruction → myosin inhibitor, disopyramide, or septal reduction; avoid dehydration and vasodilators
Restrictive disease: cautious diuresis, treat cause; Takotsubo: supportive care after excluding ACS
Myocarditis with shock → ICU, circulatory support; no routine antiviral or immunosuppression

rows.label: Complications
items: Sudden cardiac death, atrial fibrillation, thromboembolism; advanced failure → transplantation evaluation
★ HCM with cardiac arrest or major sudden-death risk → **ICD** consideration

rows.label: Prevention
items: Screen first-degree relatives in inherited disease; avoid cardiotoxins
Myocarditis: restrict strenuous exercise until clinical recovery and reassessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ischemic cardiomyopathy: obstructive coronary disease explains dysfunction
Constrictive pericarditis: pericardial disease, respiratory ventricular interdependence
Aortic stenosis: murmur softer with standing/Valsalva, unlike obstructive HCM

table.title: Echo phenotype
rows: Enlarged ventricles, diffuse hypokinesia, reduced EF
Transient apical ballooning beyond coronary territory

cardiomyopathies.evidence: HCM checked 2026-10-30: [AHA/ACC 2024](https://www.acc.org/latest-in-cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2024/05/06/15/12/2024-hypertrophic-cardiomyopathy-gl); other content established teaching.

carotid-artery-stenosis.name: Carotid artery stenosis
carotid-artery-stenosis.scope: Asymptomatic carotid bruit, carotid duplex ultrasound, medical management, indications for carotid endarterectomy
carotid-artery-stenosis.core: Carotid atherosclerosis causes ipsilateral retinal or cerebral ischemia; intervention depends on symptoms, stenosis severity, and operative risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, smoking, hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia; coronary or peripheral arterial disease
Prior neck radiation increases stenosis and surgical complexity

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Amaurosis fugax** (painless curtain-like monocular vision loss), contralateral weakness, aphasia → symptomatic disease
Bruit may be incidental; loudness does not measure severity, complete occlusion may be silent
Isolated dizziness or syncope rarely represents carotid-territory ischemia

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Plaque rupture → artery-to-artery emboli; critical narrowing can reduce cerebral perfusion
Retinal **Hollenhorst plaque** (cholesterol embolus) → ulcerated ipsilateral carotid plaque

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected stenosis or selected incidental bruit evaluation → **carotid duplex ultrasound**
CTA/MRA confirms anatomy before intervention; brain imaging evaluates neurologic deficits
★ **No routine screening** of asymptomatic general adults; bruit auscultation is an unreliable screen

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ All: **antiplatelet + high-intensity statin**, BP and diabetes control
Symptomatic operative candidates: endarterectomy generally within **2 weeks**, after neurologic stabilization
Classic asymptomatic CEA criteria: ≥70%, life expectancy ≥3–5 years, perioperative stroke/death <3%; individualized decision
CREST-2: asymptomatic stenting benefited selected patients; CEA lacked significant benefit; avoid automatic surgery
Symptomatic older adults: CEA generally preferred to stenting; high surgical-risk anatomy may favor stenting

rows.label: Complications
items: Ischemic stroke, recurrent TIAs; procedure → stroke, MI, cranial nerve injury
Hyperperfusion after revascularization → headache, seizures, brain hemorrhage; driven by **postoperative hypertension**
New deficit after endarterectomy → **noncontrast head CT** first: hemorrhage vs carotid thrombosis; no heparin/tPA beforehand
★ Expanding neck hematoma with stridor → **open wound/emergent neck exploration**; no imaging delay

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, exercise, Mediterranean-style diet; sustained vascular risk reduction
New focal neurologic symptoms → emergency stroke assessment, even after symptom resolution

rows.label: Mimics
items: Aortic stenosis: cardiac murmur radiates to both carotids
Cardioembolism: atrial fibrillation or cardiac thrombus; multiple vascular territories
Migraine aura: gradually spreading positive visual/sensory symptoms
Giant cell arteritis: headache, jaw claudication, ↑ESR; vision loss often persistent

table.title: Symptomatic ipsilateral stenosis
rows: Selected patients: age, sex, comorbidity matter

catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.name: Catheter-related bloodstream infection
catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.scope: Central line infection, organisms, line removal, prevention
catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.core: Fever or rigors in a patient with an intravascular catheter, especially during infusion, raises concern for catheter-related bacteremia.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Long catheter dwell time, femoral placement, parenteral nutrition, immunosuppression, hemodialysis
Poor asepsis, frequent hub manipulation; tunneled devices and ports also susceptible

rows.label: Clues
items: Exit-site erythema or drainage may occur; normal insertion-site appearance does not exclude infection
★ **Hypotension, persistent bacteremia**, new murmur, or embolic signs → complicated infection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Skin flora migrate externally or contaminated hubs seed intraluminal biofilm
Biofilm limits antibiotic penetration; S aureus and Candida frequently seed distant sites

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Before antibiotics: **paired peripheral and catheter blood cultures**, labelled by source
Same organism with catheter culture positive ≥2 h earlier supports catheter source
Culture removed catheter tip when infection suspected; no routine tip culture after elective removal
Repeat blood cultures to document clearance; persistent positivity → endocarditis, infected thrombus, abscess evaluation
S aureus bacteremia → echocardiography, TEE when high risk; assess metastatic foci

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Empiric **IV vancomycin** (MRSA, coagulase-negative staph); sepsis/neutropenia → add cefepime; adjust to cultures
★ **Remove line** for shock, tunnel infection, endocarditis, persistent bacteremia, S aureus, Pseudomonas, or fungi
Candida → echinocandin; MSSA → cefazolin or nafcillin; enterococcal treatment follows susceptibilities
Selected stable long-term line infections with coagulase-negative staphylococci → systemic antibiotics + antibiotic lock
Uncomplicated S aureus bacteremia: ≥14 days after clearance; endocarditis/deep infection usually requires 4–6 weeks

rows.label: Complications
items: Endocarditis, septic thrombophlebitis, osteomyelitis, septic emboli, shock
Unnecessary device retention → relapse; repeated placement → thrombosis and vascular injury
Suppurative thrombophlebitis: fluctuant, purulent vein after line removal → **surgical vein excision**, not compresses

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Hand hygiene, chlorhexidine skin preparation, maximal sterile barrier** during insertion
Scrub hubs, sterile dressings, daily necessity review, prompt removal of unnecessary lines
Avoid routine prophylactic systemic antibiotics or scheduled catheter replacement solely to prevent infection

rows.label: Mimics
items: Contaminated blood culture: single skin-flora isolate without corroborating cultures or illness
Infusate reaction: temporal symptoms without reproducible bacteremia
Catheter thrombosis: swelling, poor flow; cultures negative unless infected
Wound/abdominal source: local findings; benign exam + gram-positive bacteremia → catheter

table.title: Organism pattern
rows: S epidermidis: leading biofilm/port-pocket infection; distinguish contamination
Parenteral nutrition, broad antibiotics; remove catheter

catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.evidence: Not checked online; established catheter-infection management principles.

cerebellar-disorders.name: Cerebellar disorders
cerebellar-disorders.scope: Acute cerebellar ataxia, cerebellar signs, toxic cerebellar degeneration (cytarabine, phenytoin, alcohol), paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration, Friedreich ataxia, imaging
cerebellar-disorders.core: Dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesia, intention tremor, and a broad-based gait localize dysfunction to the cerebellum or its connections.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Recent viral infection in children; chronic alcohol exposure or malnutrition
Phenytoin toxicity, high-dose cytarabine, occult malignancy; inherited recessive disease

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Abrupt ataxia with **headache, vomiting, focal deficits** → posterior circulation emergency
Midline lesions: truncal instability; hemispheric lesions: ipsilateral limb incoordination
Scanning dysarthria, gaze-evoked nystagmus; imbalance persists with eyes open

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired timing and error correction; lateral cerebellum coordinates ipsilateral extremities
Alcohol predominantly damages anterior vermis; paraneoplastic disease causes immune-mediated Purkinje cell loss

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Acute focal or persistent unexplained ataxia → **brain MRI**, especially posterior fossa
Acute vomiting, suspected hemorrhage/mass → **CT first**; negative CT does not exclude cerebellar infarction
Check glucose, toxic exposures, phenytoin level; consider B12, thyroid testing
Subacute progressive course → paraneoplastic antibodies and malignancy search; hereditary pattern → genetic testing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected nutritional deficiency → **IV thiamine** promptly; give glucose immediately if hypoglycemic
★ Toxic **cytarabine/phenytoin** → stop culprit; cytarabine toxicity requires urgent oncology review
Postinfectious acute cerebellar ataxia: observation/support after exclusion of dangerous causes
Paraneoplastic syndrome: treat tumor, consider immunotherapy; rehabilitation for all persistent deficits

rows.label: Complications
items: Falls, aspiration; cerebellar infarction/edema → obstructive hydrocephalus and herniation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Alcohol cessation, nutritional repletion; review anticonvulsant levels and interactions

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sensory ataxia: impaired proprioception, marked worsening with eye closure
Vestibular disease: vertigo predominates, no limb dysmetria

table.title: Progressive syndromes
rows: GAA expansion; areflexia, extensor plantars, cardiomyopathy
Weeks–months; breast/ovarian or small-cell lung cancer

cerebellar-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established neurologic localization and toxicology teaching.

cervical-cancer-screening.name: Cervical Cancer Screening
cervical-cancer-screening.scope: USPSTF guidelines by age (Pap smear alone 21-29, Pap with hrHPV cotesting or hrHPV alone 30-65), screening cessation, post-hysterectomy
cervical-cancer-screening.core: Screen average-risk people with a cervix from age 21; age, prior results, and cervical precancer history determine testing and cessation.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **Average-risk cervix present**; sexual history and HPV vaccination do not alter schedule
HIV, immunosuppression, DES exposure, prior CIN 2+ → separate surveillance pathways
HIV: **cytology annually**; every 3 years only after 3 consecutive normal results

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Stop after 65 only with **adequate negative prior screening** and no high-risk history
Adequate: 3 negative cytology/2 HPV-based tests over 10 years; latest within 5
Total benign hysterectomy, no CIN 2+/cancer → stop; supracervical hysterectomy → continue

rows.label: Test
items: Choose one age-specific strategy below; annual testing increases unnecessary procedures

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ **HPV 16/18 or high-grade cytology → colposcopy**, including pregnancy, <25; others: risk assessment
CIN 2+ even hysterectomy → vaginal-cuff HPV-based testing ≥25 years; older exams: annual Pap

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Postcoital bleeding or visible lesion → diagnostic evaluation**, regardless of screening interval
Under 21: no routine screening; unknown/inadequate history after 65 → continue
USPSTF 2018 final schedule below; later draft self-collection proposals do not replace final guidance

table.title: USPSTF age-based choices
rows: Primary hrHPV or cotest every 5 years

cervical-cancer-screening.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF final recommendation (2018)](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/cervical-cancer-screening); post-treatment surveillance follows established ASCCP teaching.

cervicitis-pid.name: Cervicitis and pelvic inflammatory disease
cervicitis-pid.core: Sexually active patient with mucopurulent discharge or postcoital bleeding; ascending infection adds pelvic pain, sometimes an adnexal abscess.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age <25 (adolescent cervical ectopy → vulnerable columnar epithelium), new/multiple partners, inconsistent condoms, prior STI
IUD-associated PID risk concentrated within first 3 weeks after insertion

rows.label: Clues
items: Cervical friability, easily induced endocervical bleeding; infection sometimes asymptomatic
Dyspareunia, fever; severe unilateral pain/adnexal mass → **tubo-ovarian abscess**
Peritonitis, shock → rupture; RUQ pain → Fitz-Hugh–Curtis perihepatitis
Persistent dysuria, sterile pyuria, negative culture → chlamydial urethritis, not UTI

rows.label: Pathophys
items: GC/CT ascend cervix → endometrium/tubes; PID often polymicrobial, including anaerobes
Chlamydial tubal damage: **host immune response** → scarring, hydrosalpinx

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pregnancy test** first; vaginal/cervical or urine **GC/CT NAAT**; HIV/syphilis testing
★ Pelvic pain + **cervical motion, uterine, OR adnexal tenderness** → presumptive PID; no confirmation delay
Negative cervical NAAT does not exclude upper-tract infection; normal discharge/no vaginal leukocytes argues against PID
**Transvaginal US** for abscess or diagnostic uncertainty; routine laparoscopy unnecessary

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Cervicitis: empiric GC/CT coverage IF high risk/unreliable follow-up; otherwise await NAAT
★ Admit IF **pregnant, abscess, severe illness**, oral intolerance, uncertain surgical diagnosis, or failure by 72 h
Abscess rupture → emergency surgery; persistent abscess after 48–72 h antibiotics → drainage
Pregnant chlamydia → **azithromycin**, avoid doxycycline; retain IUD initially, reassess if no improvement

rows.label: Complications
items: Tubal infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain; abscess → sepsis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Treat partners from prior **60 days**; abstain until courses completed, partners treated, symptoms resolved
Retest GC/CT at 3 months; pregnant chlamydia → test of cure at 4 weeks
Annual GC/CT screening: sexually active women <25, older women with risks; condoms

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG, no confirmed intrauterine pregnancy
Ovarian torsion: abrupt unilateral pain, vomiting; Doppler flow may persist
Appendicitis: migrating RLQ pain, CT appendiceal inflammation

table.title: Antibiotic branches
rows: Ceftriaxone; add CT regimen unless excluded
Oral drugs 14 days; ceftriaxone once IM outpatient

chancroid.name: Chancroid
chancroid.scope: Haemophilus ducreyi, painful genital ulcers with ragged undermined margins, painful fluctuant inguinal lymphadenitis (bubo), azithromycin, ceftriaxone, differentiation from syphilis and herpes
chancroid.core: Painful, friable genital ulcers with ragged undermined edges and tender suppurative inguinal nodes suggest Haemophilus ducreyi infection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual exposure in endemic regions/outbreaks, multiple partners, inconsistent condom use
HIV and lack of circumcision associated with slower healing and treatment failure

rows.label: Clues
items: Nonindurated ulcer base, purulent exudate, easy contact bleeding; often multiple lesions
Buboes commonly unilateral; lymph-node suppuration may cause draining sinus tracts
Systemic symptoms usually limited; generalized rash or neurologic findings suggest another infection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Gram-negative coccobacillus enters mucosal breaks, producing local necrosis and regional lymphatic infection
Ulceration increases HIV acquisition and transmission risk

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical suspicion plus exclusion of **syphilis and HSV**; test all genital ulcers
Ulcer HSV NAAT and syphilis serology; very early negative syphilis result requires repeat testing
H. ducreyi culture needs special media, limited sensitivity; NAAT availability limited
★ Obtain **HIV test**; consider repeat testing/PrEP according to ongoing exposure risk

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Azithromycin orally once** or **ceftriaxone IM once**
Fluctuant buboes → needle aspiration or incision/drainage plus antibiotics
★ Reexamine in **3–7 days**; symptoms should improve before complete ulcer healing
No response → reassess diagnosis, adherence, coinfection, HIV, or antimicrobial resistance

rows.label: Complications
items: Genital scarring, phimosis, fistulas, secondary infection; prolonged open lesions facilitate HIV spread

rows.label: Prevention
items: Condoms, abstain until lesions healed and partners treated
Examine/treat partners exposed during 10 days before symptom onset, even without symptoms

rows.label: Mimics
items: Syphilis: classically painless, indurated chancre with nontender nodes
HSV: grouped vesicles evolve into shallow ulcers; burning prodrome, recurrent episodes
LGV: small transient often painless lesion, later inguinal adenopathy or proctitis

child-abuse-and-neglect.name: Child abuse and neglect
child-abuse-and-neglect.scope: Physical abuse (burn patterns, fractures of different ages, metaphyseal corner fractures), abusive head trauma (shaken baby, subdural hematoma, retinal hemorrhages), neglect, mandatory reporting
child-abuse-and-neglect.core: Reasonable suspicion of child maltreatment requires protective reporting; proof and caregiver permission are unnecessary.

rows.label: Principle
items: Inconsistent history, delayed care, or developmentally impossible mechanism increase suspicion

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Report to child protective services** promptly; urgent danger → emergency protective services
Stabilize; document verbatim statements, findings and photographs; interview caregivers separately
★ Suspected physical abuse age <2 → **skeletal survey**; repeat after approximately 2 weeks

rows.label: Don't
items: Confront or accuse caregivers; promise secrecy; delay reporting for complete diagnostic certainty
Discharge into an unsafe setting; substitute reporting to a supervisor for mandated reporting

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Financial hardship alone ≠ neglect; assess ability to obtain food, shelter and medical care
Consider bleeding disorders, osteogenesis imperfecta and accidental trauma without delaying protection

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Metaphyseal corner/posterior rib fractures**; mixed healing stages → abuse concern
Immersion burns: uniform depth, sharp edges, stocking/glove pattern; nonmobile infants: sentinel bruising
★ Abusive head trauma: acceleration-deceleration tears bridging veins → **subdural, retinal hemorrhages**

table.title: Presentation → evaluation
rows: AST/ALT, lipase, urinalysis; CT if concerning
Growth, nutrition, hygiene, supervision, unmet care needs
Sexual abuse assessment and CPS report

child-abuse-and-neglect.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric safeguarding principles; reporting procedures vary by jurisdiction.

child-growth-and-development.name: Child growth and development
child-growth-and-development.scope: Normal growth velocity, weight doubling and tripling milestones, WHO/CDC growth chart interpretation, developmental surveillance, normal toddler behavioral variants (head banging, temper tantrums)
child-growth-and-development.core: Interpret serial growth and developmental progress against age, family pattern, and corrected gestational age; a trajectory matters more than one percentile.

rows.label: Definition
items: Weight doubles by 4–6 months, triples by 12 months, quadruples near 24 months
Length increases about 25 cm during year 1; prepubertal height velocity about 5–6 cm/year
★ **WHO charts before 2 years; CDC charts from 2 years** in US practice

rows.label: Interpret
