Encephalitis/neonatal CNS concern, **lymphocytic CSF with RBCs** → CSF HSV PCR; early negative may require repeat
Neonate → lesion/surface, blood, CSF testing plus liver enzymes; treat while testing
No routine type-specific serology screening or HSV IgM

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First genital episode → **oral acyclovir or valacyclovir for 7–10 days**; start before results
Recurrence → prompt episodic dosing at prodrome; frequent/distressing episodes → daily suppressive valacyclovir
★ Neonatal, CNS, disseminated disease or severe eczema herpeticum → **IV acyclovir**
Pregnancy: acyclovir/valacyclovir from 36 weeks; labor lesions/prodrome → cesarean; neither → vaginal despite history
Corneal involvement → urgent ophthalmology; avoid unsupervised ocular corticosteroids

rows.label: Complications
items: Encephalitis, aseptic meningitis, urinary retention, keratitis, dissemination; increased HIV acquisition risk
Acyclovir → crystal nephropathy, neurotoxicity with renal impairment; hydrate, adjust dose

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Avoid sex during lesions/prodrome**, condoms, partner disclosure; suppression lowers but never eliminates transmission
Avoid kissing infants with active labialis; cover lesions, hand hygiene

rows.label: Mimics
items: Syphilis: classically painless chancre; chancroid: deep purulent painful ulcer
Aphthae: mucosal ulcers, no preceding vesicles
Zoster: unilateral dermatomal eruption
Felon/paronychia: pus, no vesicles; whitlow → oral acyclovir, **no incision/drainage**

herpes-simplex-virus.evidence: Checked genital disease 2026-10-30: [CDC HSV guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/std/treatment-guidelines/herpes.htm); neonatal/eczema management established teaching.

table.title: Neonatal IV acyclovir duration
rows: ≥21 days; CNS: confirm CSF PCR clearance

hiatal-hernia.name: Hiatal hernia
hiatal-hernia.scope: Sliding hiatal hernia, paraesophageal hiatal hernia, gastric volvulus risk, barium swallow, surgical repair
hiatal-hernia.core: Herniation of stomach through the diaphragmatic hiatus causes reflux or mechanical obstruction; volvulus and ischemia require urgent surgical care.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age-related diaphragmatic laxity, obesity, pregnancy, increased intra-abdominal pressure; connective-tissue weakness
Prior foregut surgery may predispose to recurrent or altered hiatal anatomy

rows.label: Clues
items: Heartburn, regurgitation, positional symptoms; large hernias → dysphagia, early satiety or postprandial chest pressure
Chronic occult blood loss from Cameron erosions → iron-deficiency anemia
★ Severe epigastric pain, **unproductive retching, inability to pass NG tube** → gastric volvulus
Dyspnea or recurrent aspiration can indicate symptomatic large paraesophageal disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hiatal widening permits proximal stomach migration; disrupted antireflux barrier promotes acid exposure
Rotation/entrapment of intrathoracic stomach compromises outflow and potentially perfusion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Barium swallow** defines anatomy and rotation; **refractory reflux or anemia → EGD** for mucosal injury/Barrett
Acute severe symptoms → contrast CT for obstruction, ischemia or perforation
Before elective antireflux surgery → manometry; reflux monitoring when EGD lacks objective GERD evidence
Chest radiograph may show retrocardiac air-fluid level; cannot fully characterize complications

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Reflux-predominant sliding hernia → **PPI**, weight loss, smaller meals, head-of-bed elevation
Persistent objectively confirmed reflux or complications → selected surgical repair/fundoplication
Symptomatic paraesophageal hernia → elective repair after operative-risk assessment
★ Volvulus, strangulation or perforation → resuscitation, decompression and **urgent surgery**
Incidental asymptomatic sliding hernia → **observation**; asymptomatic paraesophageal → shared decision on repair

rows.label: Complications
items: Esophagitis, stricture, Barrett esophagus; mechanical obstruction, gastric necrosis, hemorrhage
Repair → recurrence, dysphagia, gas-bloat syndrome

rows.label: Prevention
items: Weight management, avoid late meals; smoking cessation reduces reflux burden
Known unrepaired paraesophageal hernia → counsel on emergency obstructive symptoms

rows.label: Mimics
items: ACS: ischemic ECG/troponin findings; exclude with suspicious acute chest symptoms
Achalasia: impaired LES relaxation and esophageal retention without primary hiatal migration

hiv-infection.name: HIV infection
hiv-infection.scope: Acute HIV, testing, ART start, opportunistic infection prophylaxis, PrEP/PEP, opportunistic infections (CMV retinitis, toxoplasmosis, PJP)
hiv-infection.core: HIV progressively depletes CD4 cells; early diagnosis and suppressive ART prevent immune failure and sexual transmission.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual exposure, shared injection equipment, perinatal transmission; other STIs increase acquisition risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Acute infection 2–4 weeks post-exposure: fever, rash, sore throat, **mucosal ulcers**, diarrhea, generalized lymphadenopathy
Weight loss, thrush, recurrent candida/herpes, **extensive adult molluscum** → test HIV; dysphagia → candidal esophagitis
Child/teen: chronic fever/diarrhea, poor growth, generalized nodes, splenomegaly, **polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retroviral integration creates lifelong reservoirs; ongoing replication drives immune depletion and inflammation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Fourth-generation Ag/Ab → HIV-1/2 differentiation assay**; discordance → HIV RNA
★ Recent exposure/acute syndrome despite negative screen → **HIV RNA**, before antibodies appear
Baseline viral load, CD4, genotype, renal/liver function, HBV/HCV/TB, pregnancy testing, **cervical cytology**
AIDS: CD4 <200 or AIDS-defining illness regardless of count
Prenatal: opt-out screening; refusal → counsel, re-offer later; never test without consent

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Start **integrase-based ART promptly**, usually bictegravir/TAF/emtricitabine; assess HBV coinfection and interactions
Do not delay routine ART for genotype; cryptococcal/TB meningitis require disease-specific deferred timing
PJP: TMP-SMX; add glucocorticoid if PaO₂ <70 or A–a gradient ≥35
Toxoplasmosis: **pyrimethamine/sulfadiazine/leucovorin**, else TMP-SMX; CMV retinitis: valganciclovir, ophthalmology
Untreated/viremic mother's newborn → **triple ART** ASAP, ideally within 6 h, ≤6 weeks; suppressed mother → zidovudine alone

rows.label: Complications
items: Opportunistic infections, malignancies, wasting, neurocognitive disease, kidney disease
Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome after ART; drug toxicity/interactions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ PJP prophylaxis: **TMP-SMX** with CD4 <200 before/starting ART; on ART, <100 or 100–200 with viremia
Toxoplasma IgG positive + CD4 <100 → prophylaxis; MAC <50 only without immediate effective ART
★ Exposure ≤72 hours → **28-day PEP: dolutegravir + TDF/emtricitabine**; do not delay for laboratory results
PrEP: TDF/emtricitabine, cabotegravir, or lenacapavir; exclude HIV first, continue serial testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: EBV mononucleosis: atypical lymphocytes, heterophile positivity; acute HIV can be heterophile-negative
Primary CNS lymphoma: often solitary lesion; biopsy after failed empiric anti-Toxoplasma treatment, earlier if serology/imaging/CSF PCR disagree
SCID/CVID: low immunoglobulins; SCID lymphopenia, no nodes; perinatal HIV: PJP, thrush, nodes, normal lymphocytes

table.title: Advanced-disease syndromes
rows: Dry cough, hypoxemia, ground-glass; sputum/BAL silver stain
Ring-enhancing mass lesions, edema/mass effect; positive IgG
Cognitive decline; non-enhancing subcortical demyelination, no mass effect

hypercalcemia.name: Hypercalcemia
hypercalcemia.scope: Primary hyperparathyroidism, malignancy-associated hypercalcemia, milk-alkali syndrome, IV saline resuscitation, calcitonin, bisphosphonates
hypercalcemia.core: Elevated calcium causes stones, constipation, polyuria, weakness, and neuropsychiatric changes; PTH distinguishes hormone-driven disease from other causes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Parathyroid adenoma/hyperplasia, malignancy, prolonged immobilization
Thiazides, lithium, excess vitamin D or calcium/absorbable alkali, granulomatous disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Dehydration, nausea, abdominal pain, reduced reflexes; ECG may show shortened QT
★ **Calcium >14 mg/dL**, confusion, arrhythmia, or severe volume depletion → urgent treatment
Primary hyperparathyroidism often asymptomatic; malignancy-associated disease tends to progress rapidly

rows.label: Pathophys
items: PTH promotes bone resorption and renal calcium retention while increasing phosphate excretion
Hypercalcemia impairs renal concentration → dehydration, reduced calcium clearance, self-reinforcing elevation
High filtered calcium exceeds tubular reabsorption → **hypercalciuria** → calcium stones

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm with repeat total/albumin-adjusted or **ionized calcium**, especially with altered proteins or critical illness
★ **Intact PTH first**; elevated or inappropriately normal → PTH-dependent
Suppressed PTH → PTHrP, vitamin D metabolites, malignancy/myeloma evaluation guided by context
Primary disease versus FHH → urine calcium; clearance ratio <0.01 favors FHH, with overlap
Parathyroid imaging localizes before surgery; never establishes biochemical diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe/symptomatic → **IV isotonic saline**, then calcitonin for rapid temporary lowering
★ **Denosumab** (favored, esp renal limitation/refractory) or **IV zoledronic acid/pamidronate** for sustained malignancy control
Calcitriol-mediated disease → glucocorticoids; dialysis for refractory life-threatening elevation or inability to hydrate
Primary disease: surgery for symptoms, age <50, calcium >1 above ULN, osteoporosis/fracture, stones, eGFR <60
Stop causative supplements/drugs; loop diuretic only for fluid overload, not routine calcium elimination

rows.label: Complications
items: Nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis, AKI, osteoporosis/fractures, pancreatitis
Calcitonin tachyphylaxis after 48–72 hours; antiresorptives can cause hypocalcemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hydration, avoid excess calcium/alkali; monitor calcium, renal function, and bone density when observing primary disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: FHH: lifelong mild elevation, family history, hypocalciuria; surgery ineffective
Pseudohypercalcemia: high protein-bound calcium but normal ionized fraction

hypercalcemia.evidence: Not checked online; established calcium evaluation and emergency management.

hyperglycemic-crises.name: Hyperglycemic crises
hyperglycemic-crises.core: Insulin-deficient diabetes with osmotic diuresis: rapid acidotic illness or slowly progressive hyperosmolar encephalopathy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Infection, missed insulin, pump failure, MI; DKA often type 1, HHS often older type 2
Euglycemic triggers: **SGLT2 inhibitors**, pregnancy, fasting

rows.label: Clues
items: Polyuria, thirst, weight loss, dry mucosa, tachycardia
DKA: abdominal pain, vomiting, **Kussmaul (deep) breathing**; HHS: profound dehydration, focal deficits
★ Severe: **hypotension, stupor**, or coma → ICU

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Insulin deficit + counterregulatory hormones → lipolysis, ketogenesis; residual insulin in HHS limits ketosis
Total-body K depleted despite initially normal/high serum K

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Glucose, electrolytes, venous pH, β-hydroxybutyrate**, osmolality; ECG + trigger evaluation
Effective osmolality = 2 × Na + glucose/18; glucose in mg/dL
★ HHS: **effective osmolality >300 OR total >320 mOsm/kg**; substantial ketosis/acidosis → mixed DKA/HHS
DKA resolution: ketones <0.6 mmol/L AND (pH ≥7.3 OR HCO₃ ≥18); urine ketones/anion gap misleading

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IV isotonic crystalloid → K correction → IV regular insulin**; K <3.5 mmol/L → delay insulin
Replace K when <5 mmol/L; glucose checks every 1–2 h, electrolytes/pH/ketones every 4 h
★ Add **dextrose** below glucose 250; euglycemic presentation → immediately; continue insulin until crisis resolves
SC basal insulin overlaps infusion 1–2 h; bicarbonate only consider pH <7.0; HHS: slower osmolar correction

rows.label: Complications
items: AKI, thrombosis; treatment: hypoglycemia, hypokalemic arrhythmias, cerebral edema (Cushing triad), hyperchloremic acidosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Sick-day fluids/ketone checks; continue basal insulin; ensure supplies and early follow-up
Hold SGLT2 inhibitors during acute illness and before surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Alcoholic ketoacidosis: binge then poor intake; usually no diabetes
Starvation ketosis: usually milder acidosis, no marked hyperglycemia
Toxic alcohols: osmolar gap, exposure; absent substantial ketonemia

table.title: Biochemistry; ketones and HCO₃ in mmol/L

hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy.name: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy.scope: Chronic and gestational HTN, preeclampsia, HELLP, eclampsia
hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy.core: Pregnancy-associated hypertension; maternal organ injury or placental dysfunction signals danger even without substantial proteinuria.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior preeclampsia, chronic HTN, CKD, diabetes, SLE/APS, multifetal gestation
Nulliparity, obesity, age ≥35, family history

rows.label: Clues
items: Headache, visual disturbance, RUQ/epigastric pain, dyspnea; edema nonspecific
★ Severe features: **platelets <100,000/µL**, creatinine >1.1 mg/dL or doubled, transaminases ≥2× normal
Other severe features: pulmonary edema, refractory neurologic symptoms
Presentation through **6 weeks postpartum**; eclampsia/HELLP possible without prior HTN

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Abnormal spiral-artery remodeling → placental ischemia → systemic endothelial injury, vasospasm, capillary leak

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **BP ≥140/90**, either component, twice ≥4 h apart; severe ≥160/110 confirmed within minutes
CBC/platelets, creatinine, AST/ALT, urine protein; fetal growth US + antenatal testing
Proteinuria: **≥300 mg/24 h** or protein/creatinine ≥0.3; dipstick 2+ only if quantification unavailable
Chronic HTN + new proteinuria/end-organ injury → superimposed preeclampsia; HELLP: smear, LDH ≥600 IU/L

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Persistent severe BP ≥15 min → **IV labetalol/hydralazine** or immediate-release oral nifedipine within 30–60 min
★ Severe preeclampsia/eclampsia → **magnesium sulfate** through 24 h postpartum; airway before delivery
Chronic HTN ≥140/90 → oral labetalol/extended-release nifedipine; avoid ACE inhibitors/ARBs
Mg toxicity: areflexia/hypoventilation → stop infusion, **IV calcium gluconate**; oliguria → reduce dose

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, abruption, DIC, AKI, hepatic hematoma/rupture; fetal growth restriction, prematurity, death

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ High risk or multiple moderate risks → **aspirin 81 mg/day**, start 12–28 wk, ideally before 16
Postpartum BP review within 72 h if severe, otherwise 7–10 days; long-term cardiovascular follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: TTP: profound thrombocytopenia/hemolysis, persists after delivery
Acute fatty liver: hypoglycemia, jaundice, marked coagulopathy
Epilepsy: established seizure disorder; evaluate alternative causes despite obstetric context

table.title: Classification and delivery
rows: Before 20 wk or persists >12 wk postpartum
After 20 wk + proteinuria OR severe features
Severe BP alone sufficient; <34 stable → betamethasone
Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets
Deliver after stabilization, any gestational age

hyperthyroidism.name: Hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis
hyperthyroidism.scope: Graves disease, toxic multinodular goiter, toxic adenoma, subacute thyroiditis, thyroid storm, beta-blockers, thionamides, radioactive iodine
hyperthyroidism.core: Excess circulating thyroid hormone → heat intolerance, weight loss despite appetite, tremor, and tachycardia; hormone overproduction differs from destructive release.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autoimmune history, female sex; older age favors autonomous nodules
Iodine load, amiodarone, exogenous thyroid hormone; infection/surgery can precipitate storm

rows.label: Clues
items: Hyperreflexia, lid lag, onycholysis, frequent stools, proximal weakness, widened pulse pressure; older adults: apathetic
★ **Thyroid storm**: fever, delirium, severe tachyarrhythmia, vomiting, heart failure; clinical diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased tissue metabolic activity and beta-adrenergic sensitivity explain systemic manifestations
Thionamides block thyroid peroxidase; PTU also reduces peripheral T4 → T3 conversion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TSH first → free T4**, total T3 if T4 normal; suppressed TSH with elevated hormones
TRAb establishes Graves; uncertain cause → **Doppler ultrasound** or radioiodine uptake (not if pregnant/lactating)
Low uptake: thyroiditis/exogenous hormone; low thyroglobulin supports exogenous ingestion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptom control: **propranolol**; caution in asthma or decompensated HF
★ Storm → ICU, cooling/fluids, beta-blockade if tolerated, **PTU → iodine ≥1 hour later**, hydrocortisone
Radioiodine contraindicated during pregnancy/lactation; significant active orbitopathy favors another definitive treatment
Compression/suspicious nodule → thyroidectomy after control; pregnancy: first-trimester PTU, later methimazole

rows.label: Complications
items: AF, embolism, osteoporosis, mild hypercalcemia, cardiomyopathy; radioiodine often → hypothyroidism
★ Thionamides: **fever/sore throat → stop drug, urgent CBC**; PTU → severe hepatotoxicity
Pregnancy: thionamides/TRAb cross placenta → **fetal goiter**, impaired swallowing, polyhydramnios

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor free T4 early during treatment; TSH recovery lags
Smoking cessation for orbitopathy; definitive treatment before planned pregnancy when feasible

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic disorder: episodic symptoms without thyroid biochemical abnormalities
Pheochromocytoma: paroxysmal headache, sweating, severe hypertension
Menopause: hot flashes with menstrual transition, normal thyroid testing
Orbital pseudotumor: involves muscle bellies and tendons; Graves spares tendons

table.title: Etiology determines treatment
rows: Diffuse uptake; bruit, orbitopathy, pretibial myxedema, acropachy (clubbing)
One hot nodule, suppressed surrounding tissue
NSAID; prednisone if severe; no thionamides

hypocalcemia.name: Hypocalcemia
hypocalcemia.scope: Hypoparathyroidism, vitamin D deficiency, post-thyroidectomy, hypomagnesemia
hypocalcemia.core: Low ionized calcium causes neuromuscular irritability and QT prolongation; severe symptoms require IV calcium while the cause is corrected.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Thyroid/parathyroid surgery, autoimmune hypoparathyroidism, DiGeorge syndrome
Vitamin D deficiency from low intake, malabsorption, limited sun; CKD, pancreatitis, massive citrate transfusion
Severe hypomagnesemia from alcoholism, diarrhea, PPIs, diuretics; bisphosphonates/denosumab can precipitate deficiency

rows.label: Clues
items: Perioral tingling, distal paresthesias, muscle cramps, carpopedal spasm
★ **Trousseau sign**: cuff-induced carpal spasm; Chvostek sign is less specific
★ Severe: **seizures, laryngospasm, arrhythmias**; ECG shows prolonged QT
Post-thyroidectomy tingling or stridor requires immediate calcium assessment rather than simple reassurance

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced extracellular calcium lowers nerve excitation threshold; myocardial repolarization is prolonged
Low magnesium impairs both PTH secretion and action, making calcium replacement alone ineffective

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Ionized calcium**, Mg, phosphate, creatinine, PTH, 25-hydroxyvitamin D
Low albumin lowers total calcium, not necessarily ionized; correction formulas unreliable in critical illness
Alkalosis increases albumin binding → symptomatic low ionized calcium despite unchanged total concentration
Interpret PTH relative to calcium: normal PTH can be inappropriately low during hypocalcemia

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic, severe, or ECG changes → **IV calcium gluconate with ECG monitoring**
Mild stable disease → oral calcium; nutritional vitamin D deficiency → cholecalciferol/ergocalciferol
Hypoparathyroidism or advanced CKD → **calcitriol** plus calcium; coordinate phosphate management
★ **Replace magnesium** when deficient; correct underlying cause, avoid overcorrection

rows.label: Complications
items: Tetany, seizures, ventricular arrhythmias; chronic deficiency can cause cataracts and basal ganglia calcification
Overreplacement → hypercalciuria, nephrolithiasis/nephrocalcinosis; monitor serum and urine calcium

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor calcium after neck surgery and antiresorptive treatment; ensure sufficient vitamin D/calcium intake
Chronic hypoparathyroidism: target symptom control with low-normal serum calcium, avoiding renal calcium loading

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hyperventilation syndrome: transient alkalosis-related ionized reduction; assess precipitating illness
Seizure disorder: no biochemical calcium explanation; pseudohypocalcemia: normal ionized level

hypocalcemia.evidence: Not checked online; established endocrine teaching.

hyponatremia.name: Hyponatremia
hyponatremia.scope: Hypovolemic, euvolemic (SIADH, primary polydipsia), hypervolemic, acute vs chronic, hypertonic saline indications
hyponatremia.core: Low serum sodium reflects excess water relative to sodium; symptoms and duration determine urgency before the cause determines maintenance treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Thiazides, SSRIs, carbamazepine/oxcarbazepine, oxytocin; **hypotonic IV D5W**, postoperative state, exercise + excess water
Pulmonary/CNS disease; **small cell lung cancer** (ectopic ADH); heart failure, cirrhosis, renal failure

rows.label: Clues
items: Nausea, headache, gait instability; seizures, coma or marked confusion indicate severe cerebral edema
Orthostasis/dry mucosa suggest depletion; edema/ascites suggest excess extracellular fluid
SIADH: clinically euvolemic with inappropriately concentrated urine despite hypo-osmolality
Massive water intake, often psychiatric illness; urine osmolality below serum still favors polydipsia, even if >100

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hypotonic extracellular fluid drives water into brain; chronic adaptation makes rapid correction dangerous
ADH-mediated water retention or intake exceeding renal dilution capacity lowers sodium concentration
Low effective volume (heart failure, cirrhosis, diarrhea) → baroreceptor ADH release; total-body sodium high in edema

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Serum osmolality first: **<275 mOsm/kg** confirms hypotonicity; assess glucose and volume status
Hyperglycemia → translocational hyponatremia; severe hyperlipidemia/proteinemia → pseudohyponatremia
★ Urine osmolality **<100** → polydipsia/low solute; ≥100 → persistent ADH activity
Urine Na <20–30 suggests low effective arterial volume; >30 suggests renal loss or SIADH
Exclude adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism and renal failure before diagnosing SIADH; diuretics confound urine Na

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe neurologic symptoms → **3% saline bolus**, repeated for initial Na rise 4–6 mEq/L
Hypovolemia → isotonic saline; SIADH → fluid restriction, increased solute, remove trigger
Edematous states → fluid/sodium restriction and loop diuretic; treat heart/liver/kidney disorder
★ Chronic/unknown duration: generally limit rise to **≤8 mEq/L per 24 h**; monitor frequently
Overcorrection → desmopressin plus D5W; avoid routine vaptans in acute symptomatic cases

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute severe hyponatremia → herniation, respiratory arrest
Osmotic demyelination after rapid correction; greatest risk with alcoholism, malnutrition, hypokalemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid hypotonic maintenance fluids during high ADH states; review causative drugs
Monitor for brisk aquaresis after restoring volume or stopping thiazides

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cerebral salt wasting: neurosurgical patient, hypovolemic, high urine Na; SIADH euvolemic
Hyperosmolar hyperglycemia: measured osmolality elevated
Primary psychiatric disease: neurologic change without sodium abnormality

hyponatremia.evidence: Not checked online; established hyponatremia consensus principles.

hypothyroidism.name: Hypothyroidism
hypothyroidism.scope: Hashimoto thyroiditis, subclinical hypothyroidism, myxedema coma, autoimmune associations, levothyroxine dosing, TSH monitoring
hypothyroidism.core: Insufficient thyroid hormone slows metabolism, causing fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, and delayed reflex relaxation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hashimoto autoimmunity, family history of autoimmune disease; thyroid surgery/radioiodine, iodine deficiency/excess
Lithium, amiodarone, postpartum thyroiditis; pituitary surgery/radiation or mass
Congenital primary → **thyroid dysgenesis** most common, not lymphocytic thyroiditis

rows.label: Clues
items: Weight gain, bradycardia, hoarseness, heavy menses, hyperlipidemia; hyponatremia in severe disease
★ **Hypothermia, altered mentation, hypoventilation, hypotension** → myxedema coma
Autoimmune clustering: type 1 diabetes, pernicious anemia, adrenal insufficiency, celiac disease
Infant: macroglossia, umbilical hernia, prolonged jaundice, hypotonia, large fontanelle → **TSH/free T4**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced hormone activity lowers thermogenesis and cardiac output; glycosaminoglycan deposition produces nonpitting edema
Hashimoto: lymphocytic infiltration; firm painless goiter, even if euthyroid; **anti-TPO/antithyroglobulin** antibodies

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TSH and free T4** establish hormone deficiency and localize the level of dysfunction
Positive anti-TPO predicts progression from subclinical disease; ultrasound unnecessary without nodule/goiter concern
Recheck mild isolated TSH elevation after transient illness resolves; exclude medication interference

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Levothyroxine**; healthy young adult approximately 1.6 mcg/kg/day; older/CAD start 12.5–25 mcg/day
Fasting, apart from calcium/iron; TSH at 6–8 weeks; **persistently high → increase dose**, even if asymptomatic
Central disease: titrate using free T4; evaluate/replace cortisol before thyroid hormone
Subclinical, untreated: generally start at TSH ≥10; consider symptoms, antibodies, pregnancy at lower values
★ Myxedema: **IV levothyroxine + IV hydrocortisone**, airway support, cautious fluids/passive warming; treat trigger

rows.label: Complications
items: Dyslipidemia, infertility, pericardial effusion, neuropathy; severe disease → respiratory failure
Excess replacement → AF, angina, bone loss; rapid correction in CAD can precipitate ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Pregnancy: early **TSH monitoring**, usually increase existing replacement promptly; use pregnancy-specific targets
Monitor stable replacement at least annually; address adherence/absorption before escalating doses

rows.label: Mimics
items: Depression, dementia, psychosis: normal TSH; hypothyroidism itself can cause reversible cognitive or psychiatric symptoms
Euthyroid sick syndrome: acute systemic illness, often low T3; avoid routine hormone replacement

hypothyroidism.evidence: Not checked online; established thyroid replacement and endocrine emergency teaching.

impetigo.name: Impetigo
impetigo.scope: Nonbullous impetigo (honey-colored crusts), bullous impetigo, Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes, topical mupirocin, oral cephalexin, poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis risk
impetigo.core: Contagious superficial bacterial infection causes crusted erosions or fragile blisters, usually in children; lesion extent determines topical versus oral treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Preschool age, warm humid weather, crowding, close contact, shared towels
Skin-barrier disruption from eczema, insect bites, minor trauma, scabies; nasal staphylococcal carriage

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Nonbullous: vesicles/pustules rupture → **honey-colored crusts**, often around nose/mouth
★ Bullous: **flaccid superficial bullae**, collarette scale; intertriginous/truncal distribution common
Usually localized with little systemic illness; high fever, toxicity, diffuse tenderness require broader evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Nonbullous disease: S aureus and/or group A streptococci infect superficial epidermis
Bullous disease: staphylococcal exfoliative toxin cleaves desmoglein 1; bacterial growth remains localized

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical lesions → **clinical diagnosis**; no routine blood tests
Culture exudate when recurrent, extensive, treatment-resistant, outbreak-associated, or MRSA suspected
Deep punched-out crusted ulcer → ecthyma, extending into dermis; consider oral treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: Gently cleanse with soap/water, soften crusts; cover lesions and trim nails
★ Few localized lesions → **topical mupirocin for 5 days**
★ Numerous lesions, outbreaks, ecthyma → **oral cephalexin or dicloxacillin for 7 days**
Suspected/confirmed MRSA → culture-directed clindamycin, doxycycline, or TMP-SMX; account for age and streptococcal coverage
Streptococci alone on culture → oral penicillin; reassess spread or failure to improve

rows.label: Complications
items: Cellulitis, lymphangitis, deeper ulceration with scarring; systemic infection uncommon
**Poststreptococcal GN** can follow skin infection; antibiotics do not reliably prevent it
Acute rheumatic fever classically follows streptococcal pharyngitis rather than uncomplicated impetigo

rows.label: Prevention
items: Handwashing, separate towels, avoid scratching, treat underlying eczema/scabies
Avoid contact sports while contagious; repeated infections may prompt household/colonization assessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: HSV: grouped painful vesicles, recurrent distribution; eczema herpeticum: monomorphic punched-out erosions
Contact dermatitis: prominent itch, exposure-shaped rash, no bacterial crust initially
Staphylococcal scalded skin: diffuse tender peeling, systemic toxin effect, often sterile bullae

infectious-mononucleosis.name: Infectious mononucleosis
infectious-mononucleosis.scope: Epstein-Barr virus, triad of fever, pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy, atypical lymphocytes, heterophile antibody test, splenic rupture precautions
infectious-mononucleosis.core: An adolescent or young adult with fever, exudative pharyngitis, posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, and prolonged fatigue likely has EBV mononucleosis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Salivary transmission, close intimate contact, shared drink containers; primary symptomatic infection often in adolescence
Immunocompromised patients face greater risk of EBV-related lymphoproliferative disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Palatal petechiae, generalized nodes, splenomegaly, mild hepatomegaly/transaminase elevation
★ **Atypical lymphocytes** on smear; reactive cells are CD8 T lymphocytes, not infected B cells
★ Diffuse rash after **amoxicillin/ampicillin** supports EBV; not automatically lifelong penicillin allergy
Severe tonsillar enlargement with stridor/drooling → assess airway immediately

rows.label: Pathophys
items: EBV infects B cells via CD21; cytotoxic immune response produces systemic symptoms and lymphocytosis
Reticuloendothelial expansion enlarges spleen and weakens its capsule

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Heterophile antibody test** with CBC in typical presentation
False negatives early in illness and in young children → EBV-specific serology
Acute infection: VCA IgM positive with absent EBNA; EBNA develops later and persists
Mononucleosis-like illness with negative EBV tests → consider CMV and acute HIV testing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Hydration, rest, acetaminophen/NSAID, viscous lidocaine gargle**; gradual activity as symptoms improve
No routine antibiotics, antivirals, or glucocorticoids for uncomplicated disease
Steroids only for threatened airway or severe immune complications, such as hemolysis/thrombocytopenia
Sudden LUQ pain, referred left shoulder pain, syncope → urgent splenic rupture evaluation and resuscitation

rows.label: Complications
items: Splenic rupture, airway obstruction, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia
Hepatitis, prolonged fatigue; rare neurologic involvement; avoid alcohol during significant liver inflammation

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **No athletic activity for first 3 weeks** from onset; then light noncontact activity if recovered
Contact/collision sports and heavy lifting deferred until recovery and individualized clearance; usually ≥3–4 weeks
No routine ultrasound solely to clear athletes; avoid sharing saliva-contaminated objects

rows.label: Mimics
items: Streptococcal pharyngitis: anterior nodes, no typical atypical lymphocytosis or splenic enlargement
CMV: heterophile-negative syndrome, less prominent pharyngitis
Acute HIV: exposure history, rash/mucosal ulcers; antigen/antibody plus RNA testing

infective-endocarditis.name: Infective endocarditis
infective-endocarditis.scope: Native and prosthetic valve endocarditis, Duke criteria, prophylaxis, IV drug use endocarditis, blood culture diagnostic criteria
infective-endocarditis.core: Persistent bacteremia with valve infection causes systemic emboli, valve destruction, and immune-complex injury.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prosthetic valve, prior endocarditis, congenital valve abnormality, intracardiac device
Injection drug use → tricuspid involvement; healthcare exposure, indwelling vascular access

rows.label: Clues
items: Fever, new regurgitant murmur, embolic stroke, splenic infarct, hematuria
Janeway lesions painless; Osler nodes painful; Roth spots retinal; splinter hemorrhages nonspecific
★ **New conduction block** → periannular abscess; right-sided disease → septic pulmonary emboli

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Endothelial injury → platelet-fibrin nidus → microbial adherence and vegetation
Immune complexes → glomerulonephritis; infected fragments disseminate through downstream circulation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Three blood-culture sets before antibiotics**; separate peripheral draws unless resuscitation would be delayed
Major microbiology: **typical organism in ≥2 culture sets**, nontypical in ≥3; specialized serology/PCR also qualifies
★ **TTE → TEE** if prosthesis/high suspicion; major imaging: vegetation, abscess, perforation, new significant regurgitation
Definite clinical Duke: 2 major, 1 major + 3 minor, or 5 minor criteria
Minor: predisposition, fever, vascular phenomena, immunologic phenomena, nondiagnostic microbiology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Empiric **IV vancomycin + cefepime** for acutely ill/healthcare-associated cases; tailor to cultures and setting
MSSA → nafcillin/oxacillin or cefazolin; susceptible viridans streptococci → ceftriaxone
Prolonged pathogen-directed IV antibiotics; prosthetic infections need specialist regimen and early surgical evaluation
Surgery: heart failure, abscess, persistent bacteremia, fungal infection, or selected recurrent/large embolizing vegetations

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute regurgitation, heart failure, mycotic aneurysm, metastatic infection
Antibiotic nephrotoxicity, line infection; hemorrhage into embolic cerebral lesions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Dental **amoxicillin** for prosthetic valve/material, previous IE, selected cyanotic/residual CHD, transplant valvulopathy
Good oral hygiene, sterile access; no routine prophylaxis for GI/GU procedures or isolated MVP

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis: cancer/autoimmune disease, sterile cultures
Atrial myxoma: positional obstruction, intracavitary mass; vasculitis: no infected vegetation

informed-consent-and-capacity.name: Informed consent and capacity
informed-consent-and-capacity.scope: Decision-making capacity, informed consent, emergency exception (implied consent), refusal of treatment, AMA discharge
informed-consent-and-capacity.core: A capable adult may accept or refuse treatment after understanding its benefits, material risks, alternatives, and consequences of refusal.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ Capacity: **understand, appreciate (own case), reason, communicate**; decision-specific, fluctuating
Competence: legal; diagnosis, age, alcohol use, incarceration, disagreement alone ≠ incapacity

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Explain benefits, material risks, alternatives/no treatment; **qualified interpreter and teach-back**
Correct delirium, intoxication, pain, communication barriers; reassess capacity
AMA request: assess capacity, explore barriers, offer safer plan, document discussion and follow-up

rows.label: Don't
items: Capable refusal → respect choice, even if life-saving or pregnant; avoid coercion, abandonment
No valid consent → possible **battery**; signed form alone insufficient
Refusing one therapy (blood) ≠ refusing all; provide other indicated care, including surgery

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Emergency + incapacity + no surrogate/directive/verified refusal → implied consent to treat
★ Parents refuse minor's life-saving transfusion → **treat emergency**; seek court authority if feasible
Incapacity without emergency → authorized surrogate; involve patient to remaining ability

rows.label: Traps
items: Psychiatric illness does not automatically remove capacity; assess the specific decision
Suicide danger may justify protective detention despite expressed desire to leave
New material procedure or changed risk → renewed consent; consent revocable anytime before procedure

table.title: Who decides
rows: Ask whom to involve; facilitate promptly; no override
Minor decides; no parental consent (state law varies)
Parents seek unproven remedy for child
Continue proven therapy; investigate remedy; CPS not first
Close; discuss after waking; no next-of-kin consent
Autonomy ≠ entitlement; physician refuses, explains, offers alternatives

informed-consent-and-capacity.evidence: Not checked online; established consent/capacity ethics; emergency and minor-consent law varies by jurisdiction.

inguinal-hernia.name: Inguinal hernia
inguinal-hernia.scope: Direct inguinal hernia, indirect inguinal hernia, femoral hernia, incarcerated and strangulated hernia, physical exam, elective vs emergent surgical repair
inguinal-hernia.core: A groin bulge enlarging with strain suggests hernia; a painful irreducible mass with obstructive or ischemic signs requires urgent surgical assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Male sex, family history, prematurity, persistent processus vaginalis
Age-related fascial weakness, chronic cough, constipation, heavy strain; femoral hernias more frequent in women

rows.label: Clues
items: Bulge or dragging discomfort with standing/Valsalva, improving supine or after reduction
Incarcerated: contents cannot be reduced; bowel obstruction causes vomiting, distention, obstipation
★ **Severe persistent pain**, tenderness, erythema, toxicity/peritonitis → impaired perfusion; fever may be late

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Abdominal contents protrude through a weak opening; a narrow neck impairs venous then arterial perfusion
Richter hernia traps only bowel-wall segment; ischemia may occur without complete obstruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Standing groin examination with cough/Valsalva**; inspect both sides and assess reducibility
Uncertain occult lesion → dynamic ultrasound; CT if obstruction, complication, or alternative diagnosis suspected
Clinical strangulation → immediate operation; imaging must not delay treatment
Do not rely on surface examination alone to reliably distinguish direct from indirect anatomy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Strangulation → **IV fluids, NPO, analgesia, antibiotics, emergency repair**; resect nonviable bowel
Incarceration without ischemic features → urgent surgeon evaluation; gentle reduction only in selected cases
★ Symptomatic inguinal hernia → **elective mesh repair** in adults; children → herniotomy
Minimally symptomatic men may choose watchful waiting with return precautions
Women and femoral hernias → timely repair because occult femoral disease and strangulation risk are greater

rows.label: Complications
items: Bowel obstruction, ischemic necrosis, perforation, sepsis
Repair → chronic groin pain, recurrence, wound/mesh infection, testicular ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Treat constipation and chronic cough, smoking cessation, weight management; risk reduction cannot close an existing defect
After reduction or observation: urgent return for escalating pain, vomiting, or loss of reducibility

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lymphadenopathy: discrete solid nodes without cough impulse
Hydrocele: transilluminates; confined fluid rather than reducible bowel
Saphena varix: compressible venous swelling; Doppler demonstrates venous flow

table.title: Anatomic distinctions
rows: Below inguinal ligament, medial femoral vein

intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.name: Intrapartum fetal monitoring
intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.scope: Baseline fetal heart rate, variability, early decelerations, late decelerations, variable decelerations, category I II III tracings, intrauterine resuscitation
intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.core: Fetal oxygenation assessment from baseline, variability, and decelerations; persistent category III requires expedited delivery after immediate resuscitation.

rows.label: Definition
items: ★ Normal baseline **110–160/min**; moderate variability **6–25 beats/min**
Bradycardia <110; tachycardia >160; baseline change lasts ≥10 minutes
Tachysystole: >5 contractions/10 minutes over 30 minutes; oxytocin excess → late decelerations

rows.label: Interpret
items: Early: mirrors contraction → head compression; benign
Late: nadir after contraction peak → uteroplacental insufficiency
Variable: abrupt fall → cord compression; prolonged: 2–10 minutes

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Category II: lateral positioning, stop oxytocin, IV fluids; correct hypotension
Persistent tachysystole with concerning tracing → **terbutaline**; recurrent variables → amnioinfusion
★ Bradycardia: exam for cord prolapse; post-epidural → **maternal hypotension**; prepare delivery

rows.label: Compare
items: **Maternal fever** commonest tachycardia, variability kept; hypoxia → low variability, late decelerations
Transient minimal variability, no decelerations → **fetal sleep**, usually <40 minutes
Late decelerations → hypoxemia → **metabolic acidosis**; acute cord compression → respiratory acidosis

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Oxygen only for **maternal hypoxemia**; older routine-oxygen answers conflict with current guidance
Moderate variability or accelerations strongly argues against current metabolic acidemia
Category II alone does not mandate cesarean; reassess response and labor progress

table.title: Three-tier interpretation
rows: Reassuring rate/variability; no late or variable decelerations
Absent variability + recurrent late/variable decelerations or bradycardia
Resuscitate; unresolved → cesarean unless fully dilated
Evaluate severe anemia; expedite if persistent

invasive-fungal-infections.name: Invasive fungal infections
invasive-fungal-infections.scope: Invasive aspergillosis, allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA), mucormycosis, candidemia, amphotericin B, voriconazole, systemic corticosteroids
invasive-fungal-infections.core: Fungal syndromes range from allergic airway disease to lethal tissue invasion; immune status and imaging guide testing and treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prolonged neutropenia/transplant → molds; DKA, glucocorticoids or iron overload → mucormycosis
Central lines, TPN, abdominal surgery, broad antibiotics → invasive Candida
ABPA: asthma or cystic fibrosis; hypersensitivity rather than tissue invasion
Old TB cavity → **aspergilloma**: mobile fungus ball, air crescent, hemoptysis; colonization, not invasion

rows.label: Clues
items: Invasive aspergillosis: fever despite antibiotics, pleuritic pain, hemoptysis, pulmonary nodules
★ **Black nasal/palatal eschar**, facial pain, ophthalmoplegia → rhinocerebral mucormycosis
Candidemia: sepsis, persistent positive blood cultures; metastatic eye, heart or deep-organ infection
ABPA: recurrent wheeze, brown mucus plugs, fleeting pulmonary infiltrates

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Angioinvasive molds cause vascular thrombosis, infarction and necrosis
Candida translocates through damaged gut or colonizes intravascular devices, then disseminates hematogenously

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected mold pneumonia → **chest CT**, bronchoscopy/BAL or tissue biopsy
Aspergillus galactomannan in serum/BAL; β-D-glucan supports several fungi but usually negative in mucormycosis
Necrotic sinus lesion → urgent endoscopic biopsy for histology/culture; do not await blood cultures
Candidemia → repeat blood cultures until clear; assess source and metastatic foci
ABPA: Aspergillus-IgE + total IgE ≥500 IU/mL; two of eosinophilia, Aspergillus-IgG, CT bronchiectasis/infiltrates

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Aspergillosis → **voriconazole** or isavuconazole; evaluate interactions and liver function
★ Mucormycosis → **liposomal amphotericin B + urgent surgical debridement**; correct DKA/immunosuppression
Candidemia → echinocandin such as micafungin; step down to fluconazole when stable, susceptible and cleared
Remove implicated line when feasible; uncomplicated candidemia → ≥14 days after clearance and symptom resolution
ABPA → prednisolone or itraconazole; recurrent flares → both; avoid steroids for untreated invasive disease

rows.label: Complications
items: CNS dissemination, massive hemoptysis, blindness, endocarditis; high mortality if treatment delayed
Amphotericin → AKI, hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia; voriconazole → visual effects, hepatotoxicity

rows.label: Prevention
items: Selected high-risk prolonged neutropenia → posaconazole prophylaxis; line hygiene and antibiotic stewardship

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pseudomonas ecthyma gangrenosum: necrotic skin lesions with bacterial sepsis
Bacterial abscess: pyogenic cultures; malignancy: tissue without invasive organisms

knee-injuries.name: Knee injuries
knee-injuries.scope: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear, posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) tear, collateral ligaments, meniscal tears, knee dislocation, popliteal artery injury, Ottawa knee rules
knee-injuries.core: Knee trauma assessment starts with neurovascular safety and fracture risk, then uses mechanism, effusion timing, and targeted ligament or meniscal tests.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Pivoting/cutting sports, contact trauma, dashboard impact, hyperextension
Older age, osteoporosis, and inability to bear weight increase fracture probability

rows.label: Clues
items: Immediate large effusion suggests hemarthrosis; delayed swelling and catching suggest meniscal injury
★ **Gross deformity or spontaneously reduced dislocation** → popliteal artery injury risk
Cool foot, weak pulses, paresthesia, escalating pain → vascular compromise or compartment syndrome

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Ligament disruption → instability; displaced meniscal fragment → mechanical locking
Knee dislocation may stretch/tear popliteal artery despite restored alignment and initially palpable pulses

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Neurovascular examination before and after reduction**; ABI assesses arterial injury
★ ABI **<0.9, abnormal pulses, or pre-reduction deficit → CT angiography**; hard ischemic signs → vascular intervention
Normal ABI/pulses, no prior deficit → serial vascular checks, not immediate discharge
Ottawa: age ≥55, isolated patellar/fibular-head tenderness, flexion <90°, or inability four-step weight-bearing → radiographs
MRI for soft-tissue injury after fracture evaluation; locked knee → prompt orthopedic assessment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Dislocation → **urgent reduction before angiography**, immobilization, orthopedic/vascular consultation
Initial sprain → ice/compression, analgesia, protected weight bearing then early rehabilitation
Isolated collateral sprain → hinged brace + rehabilitation; many PCL injuries managed nonoperatively
ACL rupture with athletic demands/persistent instability or combined injury → reconstruction discussion
Displaced locked meniscal tear → arthroscopy; degenerative tears without locking usually exercise-based rehabilitation

rows.label: Complications
items: Missed arterial injury → limb loss; peroneal nerve injury → foot drop
Chronic instability, recurrent meniscal injury, posttraumatic osteoarthritis, stiffness

rows.label: Prevention
items: Neuromuscular landing/pivot training, strength and balance rehabilitation before sport return

rows.label: Mimics
items: Patellar dislocation: lateral patellar displacement, often spontaneous reduction
Septic arthritis: atraumatic hot effusion, fever; urgent aspiration
Patellofemoral pain/instability: running, stairs, sitting → anterior pain; crepitus, genu valgum, lax patella; no effusion unless acute dislocation
Osgood-Schlatter: growth-spurt athlete, chronic tibial tubercle pain; traction apophysitis, tendon-insertion microfractures

table.title: Mechanism and examination
rows: Joint-line tenderness; McMurray: click on rotation/extension; Thessaly

knee-injuries.evidence: Not checked online; established orthopedic trauma and Ottawa knee principles.

lactose-intolerance.name: Lactose intolerance
lactose-intolerance.scope: Primary lactase deficiency, secondary lactase deficiency, hydrogen breath test, stool reducing substances, dietary restriction, lactase replacement
lactose-intolerance.core: Bloating, flatulence and watery diarrhea after lactose ingestion reflect carbohydrate malabsorption rather than milk-protein allergy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Primary lactase nonpersistence increases after childhood and varies by ancestry
Secondary brush-border injury: viral gastroenteritis, celiac disease, Crohn disease, giardiasis
Congenital lactase deficiency rare; preterm infants can have transient developmental enzyme deficiency

rows.label: Clues
items: Dose-related cramps and gas within hours after milk/ice cream; symptoms improve without lactose
Stools lack blood; isolated intolerance does not cause fever or systemic inflammation
Infants with secondary malabsorption may develop acidic diarrhea and perianal irritation
Weight loss, anemia, nocturnal diarrhea or persistent symptoms despite restriction suggest another disorder

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Low intestinal lactase prevents lactose cleavage into absorbable glucose/galactose
Unabsorbed sugar retains luminal water; bacterial fermentation produces hydrogen and organic acids

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical symptoms → **lactose elimination and rechallenge**; history often sufficient
★ Uncertain diagnosis → **hydrogen breath test** after lactose; rising hydrogen with symptoms supports intolerance
Stool reducing substances and low pH can support infant carbohydrate malabsorption; limited specificity
Persistent/refractory symptoms → targeted evaluation for celiac disease, giardiasis or other mucosal injury
Distinguish lactose malabsorption on testing from clinically symptomatic intolerance

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Reduce lactose to tolerated amount**; complete lifelong dairy exclusion usually unnecessary
Lactase enzyme with lactose-containing meals or lactose-free dairy; divided portions with food improve tolerance
Yogurt with live cultures and aged hard cheese often tolerated better than milk
★ Maintain **calcium and vitamin D** through tolerated foods, fortified alternatives or supplements
Treat secondary cause; retry lactose after mucosal recovery rather than assuming permanent deficiency

rows.label: Complications
items: Unnecessary dairy restriction → low calcium intake and impaired bone health
Severe infant diarrhea can cause dehydration; uncomplicated adult intolerance does not damage intestinal mucosa

rows.label: Prevention
items: Identify personal threshold; review lactose in foods and maintain nutritionally complete substitutes
Temporary reduced intake after gastroenteritis may help selected persistent cases

rows.label: Mimics
items: Milk-protein allergy: eczema, wheeze, urticaria or bloody infant stools
Celiac disease: nutrient deficiencies and positive tTG-IgA
IBS: broader food/stress triggers, no reproducible lactose-specific pattern

lead-poisoning.name: Lead poisoning
lead-poisoning.scope: Occupational exposure, moonshine, pediatric lead toxicity, basophilic stippling, motor neuropathy (wrist drop, foot drop), encephalopathy, dimercaprol, succimer chelation
lead-poisoning.core: Exposure-related abdominal colic, anemia, and neurologic dysfunction; children may have developmental injury despite appearing well.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Pre-1978 paint dust, contaminated water/soil, imported remedies or pottery; pica increases exposure
Battery manufacture/recycling, construction, firing ranges, moonshine; occupational dust carried home

rows.label: Clues
items: Children: irritability, constipation, learning/behavior problems; severe cases → seizures, encephalopathy
Adults: **motor-predominant neuropathy** with wrist/foot drop, hypertension, renal dysfunction, saturnine gout
Microcytic or normocytic anemia; basophilic stippling supportive but neither sensitive nor specific

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inhibition of ALA dehydratase and ferrochelatase → impaired heme synthesis
Calcium mimicry disrupts neuronal signaling; deposition in bone creates long-lived stores

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Venous blood lead level** confirms elevated capillary screening; do not rely on hair testing
★ Pediatric reference **3.5 µg/dL** triggers exposure intervention; no safe childhood level
CBC, iron studies, renal function; abdominal radiograph for suspected ingested lead objects/paint chips
Developmental assessment; assess siblings and household exposure

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Remove exposure; involve environmental health/toxicology; correct iron deficiency and support calcium intake
Child **45–69 µg/dL**, no encephalopathy → oral succimer with expert supervision
★ Encephalopathy or ≥70 µg/dL → admit; **dimercaprol followed by calcium disodium EDTA**
Radiopaque lead in bowel → polyethylene glycol whole-bowel irrigation when safe
Adults: neuropathy, colic, high level → **calcium disodium EDTA** or succimer; pediatric thresholds don't apply

rows.label: Complications
items: Persistent cognitive deficits despite chelation; CKD, infertility, pregnancy complications
EDTA can injure kidneys; disodium EDTA causes fatal hypocalcemia—use calcium disodium formulation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Certified lead abatement, wet cleaning, occupational protective measures; avoid contaminated products
Medicaid childhood screening at 12 and 24 months; otherwise risk/local screening program

rows.label: Mimics
items: Iron deficiency: low ferritin; can coexist and increase lead absorption
AIP: marked urinary PBG elevation, no characteristic lead anemia

low-back-pain.name: Low back pain
low-back-pain.scope: Lumbosacral strain, herniated disk and radiculopathy, spinal stenosis, red flags, imaging indications, conservative management
low-back-pain.core: Most acute low back pain improves with activity and analgesia; neurologic deficits or systemic red flags change the workup.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Heavy lifting, deconditioning, obesity, prolonged sitting
Cancer, immunosuppression, injection drug use, osteoporosis, chronic glucocorticoids increase serious-pathology risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Mechanical pain varies with movement; isolated axial pain without systemic illness favors benign disease
★ **Urinary retention, saddle anesthesia, bilateral weakness** → cauda equina emergency
Fever, weight loss, night pain, trauma, or progressive weakness → targeted urgent evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Paraspinal injury causes localized pain; degenerative narrowing or disk extrusion compresses neural structures

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ No red flags → **no initial imaging**, including routine radiographs
Focused strength, reflex, sensory, gait examination; straight-leg raise supports lower lumbar radiculopathy
★ Suspected infection, malignancy, cord compression → **MRI**; suspected fracture → radiograph or CT
Persistent symptoms despite about 6 weeks' care → MRI if intervention being considered
Suspected spinal infection → ESR/CRP, blood cultures; normal temperature does not exclude infection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Continue activity**, no heavy lifting until pain resolves, heat, short NSAID course; avoid prolonged bed rest
Physical therapy if pain persists despite NSAIDs; avoid routine opioids and systemic steroids
Progressive motor deficit or cauda equina → urgent surgical decompression
Refractory disabling radicular pain → epidural injection or diskectomy after imaging correlation

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic pain, functional limitation, medication dependence
Untreated compression → permanent bladder, bowel, sexual, or motor dysfunction

rows.label: Prevention
items: Core strengthening, regular exercise, ergonomic lifting, weight management

rows.label: Mimics
items: AAA: abdominal pulsatile mass, vascular risk, hypotension
Renal colic: flank-to-groin pain, hematuria; inflammatory back pain: improves with exercise
Vascular claudication: calf pain, bicycling too; standing still relieves; weak pulses alone don't exclude stenosis

table.title: Mechanical patterns
rows: Leg pain below knee; cough aggravates
Shopping-cart sign; pulses usually preserved; MRI confirms

low-back-pain.evidence: Not checked online; established generalist back-pain evaluation.

lung-cancer.name: Lung cancer
lung-cancer.scope: Non-small cell, small cell, paraneoplastic syndromes, Pancoast, screening
lung-cancer.core: Persistent cough, hemoptysis, weight loss, or a suspicious lung lesion requires tissue diagnosis and staging before treatment selection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, radon, asbestos, occupational carcinogens, prior thoracic radiation; adenocarcinoma also occurs in never-smokers
Leading cause of cancer death in men and women; smoking is the predominant risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Recurrent focal pneumonia, hoarseness, unexplained pleural effusion
★ **Pancoast tumor**: shoulder/ulnar-arm pain + ipsilateral Horner syndrome
SVC obstruction: facial swelling, neck-vein distention; cord compression or airway compromise requires urgent action
Painful long-bone periostitis ± clubbing/joint swelling → **hypertrophic osteoarthropathy**, a lung cancer complication

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Bronchogenic malignant transformation → local invasion, lymphatic spread, hematogenous metastasis
Ectopic hormone production and immune cross-reactivity cause paraneoplastic syndromes
Central endobronchial tumor → bronchial obstruction → **post-obstructive pneumonia**, atelectasis, lobar collapse
Ectopic **ACTH** (polypeptide; cortisol excess secondary) → hyperpigmentation, hypertension, hypokalemic alkalosis, proximal weakness

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious finding → **contrast chest CT**; biopsy easiest site that establishes highest stage
Central lesion/nodes → bronchoscopy/EBUS; peripheral lesion → CT-guided biopsy; effusion → cytology
PET/CT for extracranial staging, brain MRI for selected stages/small-cell disease; pulmonary function before resection
Molecular profiling and PD-L1 guide advanced NSCLC treatment; suspicious nodes often require pathologic staging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early operable NSCLC → **surgical resection + nodal evaluation**; inoperable localized → stereotactic radiation
Locally advanced NSCLC → combined systemic treatment/radiation ± surgery in selected patients
Metastatic NSCLC → biomarker-directed agents or immunotherapy/chemotherapy
★ Small-cell → **platinum + etoposide**, stage-dependent radiation/immunotherapy; surgery rarely used
SVC syndrome from small-cell → urgent **chemotherapy** ± radiation; stent if severe; diuretics not definitive

rows.label: Complications
items: Brain/bone/adrenal/liver metastases, malignant effusion, thrombosis, respiratory failure
Radiation pneumonitis; checkpoint inhibitors → immune pneumonitis/endocrinopathies

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ USPSTF: **annual low-dose CT**, age 50–80, ≥20 pack-years, current smoking or quit <15 years
Stop after 15 quit-years or limited curative candidacy; **ACS omits quit-time restriction**
Smoking cessation and radon mitigation; chest radiographs do not substitute for screening CT

rows.label: Mimics
items: TB/fungal granuloma: microbiologic evidence; PET uptake not specific for cancer
Hamartoma: fat/popcorn calcification; pneumonia: clinical/radiographic response to antibiotics

lung-cancer.evidence: Screening checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF 2021](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/lung-cancer-screening), [ACS 2023 guideline](https://acsjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.3322/caac.21811); treatment: established stage-based framework.

lyme-disease.name: Lyme disease
lyme-disease.scope: Borrelia burgdorferi, erythema migrans, early localized, early disseminated, late Lyme arthritis, doxycycline, ceftriaxone
lyme-disease.core: Ixodes-transmitted Borrelia infection progresses from an expanding skin lesion to neurologic, cardiac, or joint disease when untreated.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Wooded/brush exposure in Northeast, mid-Atlantic, upper Midwest; attached blacklegged tick
Tick exposure may be unnoticed; small-mammal reservoirs sustain transmission

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Erythema migrans**: enlarging lesion >5 cm, days after bite; central clearing not required
Early dissemination: multiple lesions, unilateral/**bilateral facial palsy**, lymphocytic meningitis, fluctuating AV block
Late disease: intermittent large-joint swelling, especially knee; severe pain less prominent than effusion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Spirochete inoculation → local multiplication, hematogenous spread, inflammatory injury
Persistent antibodies can remain after cure and do not prove viable infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical erythema migrans → **clinical diagnosis**, no serology needed
Other compatible disease → two-tier serology: EIA followed by immunoblot or second EIA
Early localized serology may be negative; isolated IgM after >30 days is unreliable
Joint-fluid PCR supports selected arthritis cases; CSF testing for CNS disease; ECG for cardiac symptoms

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized skin disease → **doxycycline 10 days**, or amoxicillin/cefuroxime 14 days
Facial palsy/mild neurologic disease may use oral doxycycline; severe CNS disease → IV ceftriaxone
★ Symptomatic carditis, PR ≥300 ms, higher-degree block → **hospitalize, telemetry, IV ceftriaxone**; pacing if needed
Lyme arthritis → 28-day oral course; persistent objective disease requires reassessment, sometimes IV ceftriaxone
Post-treatment nonspecific fatigue → supportive evaluation; no prolonged antibiotics without objective reinfection/failure

rows.label: Complications
items: Complete heart block, meningoencephalitis, recurrent arthritis, postinfectious joint inflammation
Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction shortly after antibiotics; not necessarily drug allergy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ High-risk Ixodes bite, attachment ≥36 hours, endemic region → **single-dose doxycycline within 72 hours of removal**
Tick checks, permethrin-treated clothing, DEET; remove tick with fine tweezers near skin
No prophylaxis for low-risk bite or routine serologic testing of asymptomatic patients

rows.label: Mimics
items: Immediate bite hypersensitivity: small, itchy, does not progressively enlarge
Septic arthritis: marked pain, toxicity, positive culture; babesiosis: hemolysis and intraerythrocytic parasites
Neurosyphilis: Lyme can falsely react on syphilis serology; tick exposure + facial palsy → Borrelia antibodies

lymphoma.name: Lymphoma
lymphoma.scope: Hodgkin lymphoma (Reed-Sternberg cells, CD15/CD30, B symptoms, mediastinal mass), non-Hodgkin lymphoma (diffuse large B-cell, follicular, Burkitt, mantle cell), Ann Arbor staging, excisional lymph node biopsy
lymphoma.core: Persistent painless lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, or constitutional symptoms require tissue diagnosis; lymphoma subtype determines urgency, staging, and treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: EBV, HIV, transplantation/immunosuppression; autoimmune disease and older age for many NHL subtypes
Hodgkin incidence peaks in young adults and older age

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **B symptoms**: unexplained fever >38 °C, drenching night sweats, >10% weight loss in 6 months
Young adult, persistent painless cervical node + **generalized pruritus** → suspect Hodgkin
Rubbery nodes; NHL often noncontiguous/extranodal
Rapidly enlarging mass, cytopenias, high LDH → aggressive disease; mediastinal disease may obstruct airway/SVC

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Clonal lymphocyte proliferation; most NHLs are B-cell derived
Classical Hodgkin: sparse malignant cells within a reactive inflammatory background

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Excisional lymph-node biopsy** preserves architecture; core if excision unsafe; FNA alone generally insufficient
Histology, immunophenotyping/flow cytometry, selected cytogenetics classify disease; PET/CT stages FDG-avid lymphoma
Ann Arbor: I one region; II same diaphragm side; III both sides; IV disseminated extranodal disease
CBC, CMP, LDH, uric acid; HIV/HBV/HCV testing before systemic treatment
Stable before biopsy → avoid glucocorticoids obscuring histology; life-threatening compression → urgent specialist management

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early classical HL → **ABVD ± involved-site radiation**; advanced disease → nivolumab-AVD among current options
DLBCL → rituximab-based combination, commonly R-CHOP; Burkitt → urgent intensive chemotherapy with CNS-directed treatment
Asymptomatic low-burden follicular disease → observation; symptomatic/bulky disease → anti-CD20-based treatment
★ Assess tumor-lysis risk before cytotoxic treatment; hydration and **urate-lowering prophylaxis** when risk warrants

rows.label: Complications
items: Tumor lysis, marrow failure, infection, cord compression, superior vena cava syndrome
Doxorubicin → cardiomyopathy; bleomycin → lung toxicity; later infertility/secondary cancers

rows.label: Prevention
items: Anti-CD20 plus HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ → entecavir/tenofovir prophylaxis; fertility preservation before chemotherapy
Survivorship care: cardiovascular risk, thyroid/breast surveillance after relevant radiation exposures

rows.label: Mimics
items: Reactive nodes: tender, infection-linked, regress after illness
TB lymphadenitis: granulomatous inflammation; microbiologic confirmation
Leukemia: circulating blasts or marked blood-count abnormalities; marrow evaluation

macrocytic-anemia.name: Macrocytic anemia
macrocytic-anemia.scope: Folate deficiency, vitamin B12 deficiency, pernicious anemia, hypersegmented neutrophils, methylmalonic acid and homocysteine
macrocytic-anemia.core: MCV >100 fL prompts separation of megaloblastic DNA-synthesis failure from alcohol, liver disease, hypothyroidism, reticulocytosis, and marrow disorders.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Vegan diet without supplementation, gastric bypass, ileal disease/resection, metformin, long-term **PPI** → B12 depletion
Alcohol misuse, poor intake, pregnancy, methotrexate, trimethoprim → folate depletion; stores last months, B12 years
Autoimmune gastritis → pernicious anemia; nitrous oxide functionally inactivates cobalamin

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, pallor, glossitis; ineffective erythropoiesis may raise LDH/indirect bilirubin and lower other cell lines
★ **Paresthesias, gait ataxia, impaired vibration/proprioception** → B12 deficiency, even without anemia
Smooth macro-ovalocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils indicate megaloblastic change

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Defective thymidine synthesis delays nuclear maturation relative to cytoplasm
B12-dependent myelin metabolism explains spinal cord/peripheral nerve injury; folate deficiency lacks this syndrome
B12 malabsorption corrected by oral intrinsic factor → **gastric IF loss** (atrophic gastritis), not ileal disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC, smear, reticulocytes, B12**; assess folate, liver tests, TSH, exposures
Borderline B12 → methylmalonic acid; renal impairment can elevate it independently
★ Suspected pernicious anemia → **anti-intrinsic-factor antibodies**; highly specific but not fully sensitive
High reticulocytes → bleeding/hemolysis; unexplained cytopenias/dysplasia → bone marrow evaluation for MDS
Coexisting iron deficiency may normalize MCV; neurologic suspicion still requires B12 evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Replace B12 before or with folate**; folate alone can conceal ongoing neurologic injury
Neurologic/severe deficiency or malabsorption → parenteral B12 initially; irreversible cause requires lifelong replacement
Dietary B12 deficiency may respond to high-dose oral replacement; folate deficiency → oral folic acid
Remove causative drug/exposure where possible; monitor reticulocyte response and count recovery

rows.label: Complications
items: Untreated B12 deficiency → irreversible neurologic disability; severe disease → pancytopenia
Pernicious anemia → increased gastric adenocarcinoma and neuroendocrine tumor risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Reliable B12 supplementation for vegans**; lifelong monitoring/replacement after relevant GI surgery
Folic acid before conception and early pregnancy; improve nutrition and reduce harmful alcohol intake

rows.label: Mimics
items: Alcohol-associated macrocytosis: round macrocytes, no required megaloblastic change
Myelodysplasia: persistent multilineage cytopenia, dysplastic marrow
Reticulocytosis: polychromasia after blood loss or hemolysis

macrocytic-anemia.evidence: Not checked online; established hematology and nutritional teaching.

meningitis.name: Meningitis
meningitis.scope: Bacterial meningitis, viral meningitis, fungal/cryptococcal meningitis, CSF interpretation, empiric antimicrobial therapy, chemoprophylaxis
meningitis.core: Fever, headache and meningeal symptoms require prompt CSF evaluation when safe; suspected bacterial meningitis demands antibiotics without imaging-related delay.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Adults: **S. pneumoniae** most common; seeded by pneumonia, otitis, sinusitis, CSF leak, asplenia
Neonates: GBS, E. coli, Listeria; older adults/immunocompromised: additional Listeria risk
Crowding/asplenia → meningococcus; advanced HIV/transplant/chemotherapy → Cryptococcus

rows.label: Clues
items: Neck stiffness, photophobia, vomiting; infants may show poor feeding, irritability or bulging fontanelle
★ Petechiae/purpura with shock → **meningococcemia**; absence of rash does not exclude
Confusion, seizure or focal deficit raises encephalitis, raised-pressure or complicated infection concern

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Organisms reach meninges hematogenously or through contiguous spread/CSF defect; inflammation increases edema and pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Blood cultures → LP** with opening pressure, cell count, glucose, protein, Gram stain/culture and PCR
CT before LP for focal deficit, papilledema, new seizure, marked consciousness impairment or significant immunocompromise
★ If LP delayed: cultures then **immediate antibiotics**; CT cannot rule out every pressure hazard
Cryptococcus: subacute, high opening pressure ± CN VI palsy, CSF antigen; TB studies if lymphocytic, low glucose

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Adult empiric → **vancomycin + ceftriaxone**; add ampicillin if >50 or immunocompromised
Neonate → ampicillin + cefotaxime; avoid ceftriaxone in neonates
Dexamethasone before/with first antibiotic when pneumococcal meningitis suspected; narrow treatment by organism
Cryptococcal meningitis → liposomal amphotericin B + flucytosine, then fluconazole; serial therapeutic LPs for pressure
Uncomplicated viral meningitis → supportive care; suspected HSV encephalitis → IV acyclovir

rows.label: Complications
items: Hearing loss, seizures, hydrocephalus, stroke, cognitive impairment; meningococcus → DIC/adrenal hemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Meningococcal contacts within 7 days of onset → **rifampin or ceftriaxone**; droplet isolation until 24 hours treated
Hib prophylaxis for qualifying households/childcare; no routine pneumococcal contact antibiotics
Pneumococcal, Hib and meningococcal vaccination; correct recurrent CSF leaks

rows.label: Mimics
items: SAH: thunderclap headache; CT/LP hemorrhagic findings
Encephalitis: parenchymal dysfunction, focal deficits or prominent behavioral change

meningitis.evidence: Contact prophylaxis checked 2026-10-30: [CDC meningococcal guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/surv-manual/php/table-of-contents/chapter-8-meningococcal-disease.html); empiric regimens established teaching.

multiple-myeloma.name: Multiple myeloma
multiple-myeloma.scope: CRAB features (hypercalcemia, renal insufficiency, anemia, bone lytic lesions), SPEP/UPEP M-spike, serum free light chains, bone marrow biopsy (>10% plasma cells), MGUS, smoldering myeloma
multiple-myeloma.core: A clonal plasma-cell malignancy causes monoclonal protein production and organ damage; modern biomarkers can establish treatment-requiring disease before symptoms.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, Black ancestry, male sex, preexisting MGUS; usually no identifiable preventable exposure

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **CRAB**: hypercalcemia, renal impairment, anemia, lytic bone lesions
Back/rib pain, pathologic fracture, recurrent bacterial infection, high total protein, rouleaux
Acute weakness/back pain → cord compression; proteinuria or restrictive cardiomyopathy → consider AL amyloid

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Marrow expansion suppresses blood formation; osteoclast activation without osteoblast response causes bone destruction
Light chains injure renal tubules; low polyclonal immunoglobulins → **encapsulated bacteria**, e.g., pneumococcus

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **SPEP/immunofixation + free light chains**, urine studies; light-chain disease may lack serum spike
★ **Bone marrow biopsy** quantifies clonal plasma cells; whole-body low-dose CT/MRI assesses bone disease
Active disease: ≥10% clonal marrow cells/plasmacytoma plus attributable CRAB or myeloma-defining biomarker
SLiM: marrow ≥60%; involved/uninvolved FLC ratio ≥100 with involved FLC ≥100 mg/L
MRI >1 focal lesion ≥5 mm defines active disease; bone scan may miss lytic lesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Bortezomib-based combination** ± daratumumab/lenalidomide/dexamethasone; selected patients → autologous transplant
Hypercalcemia → saline plus antiresorptive; AKI → hydration, avoid NSAIDs/contrast and rapidly reduce light chains
Cord compression → dexamethasone and urgent MRI/radiation or surgery; treat infections promptly
MGUS/smoldering disease generally monitored; high-risk smoldering disease merits specialist assessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Cast nephropathy, vertebral collapse, hyperviscosity, AL amyloidosis; treatment-related neuropathy, infections and thrombosis
Urine dipstick detects albumin, misses light chains; negative dipstick does not exclude cast nephropathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Vaccines, bisphosphonates; proteasome inhibitors → antiviral prophylaxis; immunomodulators → thromboprophylaxis by risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Metastatic carcinoma: destructive lesions without clonal plasma-cell findings
Waldenström macroglobulinemia: IgM, hyperviscosity/lymphadenopathy, usually no lytic lesions

multiple-myeloma.evidence: Criteria checked 2026-10-30: [IMWG diagnostic criteria](https://www.myeloma.org/newly-diagnosed/multiple-myeloma-diagnostic-criteria); treatment: established generalist teaching.

multiple-sclerosis.name: Multiple sclerosis
multiple-sclerosis.scope: Relapsing-remitting, optic neuritis, transverse myelitis, internuclear ophthalmoplegia (MLF lesion), Uhthoff phenomenon, Lhermitte sign, disease-modifying therapies
multiple-sclerosis.core: Neurologic deficits separated in location and time, often including optic neuritis, suggest inflammatory CNS demyelination.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Young adulthood, female sex, **Northern European ancestry**, family history; EBV, smoking, low vitamin D

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Optic neuritis: **pain with eye movement**, monocular loss, poor color vision, afferent pupillary defect, often normal fundus
Internuclear ophthalmoplegia: **MLF lesion**, impaired ipsilateral adduction, contralateral abducting nystagmus; convergence intact
Uhthoff: old deficits worsen with heat; Lhermitte: neck flexion triggers electric spinal sensation
Transverse myelitis: weakness, sensory level, urinary dysfunction; acute relapse generally lasts >24 hours

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Immune-mediated oligodendrocyte/myelin injury → CNS plaques, conduction block and eventual axonal loss
Relapsing-remitting: attacks with recovery; progressive forms: accumulating disability between or without attacks

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **MRI brain/cord**: periventricular, cortical/juxtacortical, infratentorial, spinal lesions; 2024 criteria add optic nerve
Classic time dissemination: new follow-up lesion or simultaneous enhancing/nonenhancing lesions; exclude better explanation
CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands support diagnosis; revised criteria also accept kappa free-light-chain index
Atypical severe visual loss/long cord lesion → serum AQP4/MOG antibodies; revised criteria permit selected earlier diagnoses
Suspected relapse → exclude fever, UTI and metabolic triggers before escalating immunosuppression

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Disabling relapse/optic neuritis → **high-dose IV methylprednisolone**, not low-dose prednisone; refractory → plasma exchange
★ Relapsing disease → early disease-modifying drug, e.g., **ocrelizumab**, tailored to activity and pregnancy plans
Lower-activity options include interferon-beta or glatiramer; natalizumab requires JC-virus/PML risk assessment
Baclofen for spasticity; rehabilitation, bladder care and treatment of neuropathic pain
Isolated heat/infection-related worsening → treat trigger; not automatically a new inflammatory attack

rows.label: Complications
items: Gait impairment, falls, neurogenic bladder, depression and cognitive dysfunction
Immunosuppressive treatment → infection; some agents carry PML risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, exercise, vaccination; review contraception/pregnancy before disease-modifying drugs

rows.label: Mimics
items: B12 deficiency: symmetric posterior-column dysfunction, macrocytosis
NMOSD: AQP4-positive, often severe attacks; some MS drugs worsen disease
Stroke: abrupt maximal deficit, vascular territory

needlestick-injuries.name: Needlestick injuries and bloodborne pathogen exposure
needlestick-injuries.scope: Hepatitis B postexposure prophylaxis, HIV postexposure prophylaxis, hepatitis C monitoring, tetanus prophylaxis in puncture wounds
needlestick-injuries.core: After blood exposure, wash immediately, report promptly, assess the source and start time-sensitive prophylaxis before results if transmission risk warrants.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Deep hollow-bore injury, visibly bloody device, intravascular needle and viremic source increase transmission risk
Mucosal/nonintact skin blood contact qualifies; intact skin contact alone usually does not

rows.label: Clues
items: Often no acute symptoms; exposure history and source status determine immediate decisions
Acute fever/rash after exposure → evaluate HIV seroconversion; jaundice/transaminitis → hepatitis assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
