BP, lipid profile and **oral glucose tolerance test** assess metabolic risk; adolescent diagnosis avoids ultrasound criteria

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Lifestyle/weight management first for all; modest weight loss can restore ovulation in overweight patients
★ No pregnancy desired → **combined OCP** for cycles/androgen symptoms; cyclic progestin or LNG-IUD protects endometrium
Persistent hirsutism → spironolactone with reliable contraception; allow months for hair response
Metabolic risk/insulin resistance → metformin; less effective than OCP for androgen symptoms
★ Anovulatory infertility → **letrozole first-line**; clomiphene alternative, older exams may expect it; check other factors

rows.label: Complications
items: Endometrial hyperplasia/cancer, infertility, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, OSA and depression
Pregnancy → increased gestational diabetes and hypertensive-disorder risk
Gonadotropin ovulation induction → high multiple-gestation risk, so letrozole/clomiphene first

rows.label: Prevention
items: Regular progestin exposure for prolonged amenorrhea; persistent abnormal bleeding → endometrial assessment
Periodic glycemic/BP/lipid reassessment; preconception metabolic optimization and folate

rows.label: Mimics
items: Androgen-secreting tumor: rapid progression, severe virilization
Nonclassic CAH: elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone
Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea: low estrogen with exercise/energy deficit

polyuria-diabetes-insipidus.name: Polyuria and diabetes insipidus
polyuria-diabetes-insipidus.scope: Central diabetes insipidus, nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (lithium, hypercalcemia), water deprivation test, desmopressin response
polyuria-diabetes-insipidus.core: Large-volume dilute urine requires separation of water diuresis from solute diuresis; impaired thirst or water access makes diabetes insipidus dangerous.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Central: sellar surgery/trauma/infiltration; nephrogenic: lithium, hypercalcemia, hypokalemia or inherited defects
Primary polydipsia: excessive voluntary intake, psychiatric disease; osmotic diuresis: diabetes mellitus, mannitol

rows.label: Clues
items: Polyuria >3 L/day in adults, nocturia, polydipsia; distinguish from frequent small-volume voiding
★ **Hypernatremia with urine osmolality <300 mOsm/kg** suggests inadequate antidiuretic effect
Low/low-normal sodium favors excess drinking; dehydration, weakness or altered mentation signals severe water deficit

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Insufficient vasopressin signaling prevents collecting-duct aquaporin-mediated water reabsorption
Lithium enters collecting-duct cells through ENaC and impairs concentrating ability

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm **24-hour urine volume**; serum Na/osmolality, urine osmolality, glucose, calcium, K, creatinine
Hyperglycemia with concentrated solute-rich urine → osmotic diuresis; no need for water deprivation
★ Stable hypotonic polyuria → **supervised water deprivation followed by desmopressin**, or stimulated copeptin testing
Avoid dehydration testing in existing hypernatremia/volume depletion; partial defects may yield overlapping responses
Established central disease → pituitary MRI and anterior-axis evaluation; check lithium level with exposure

rows.label: Tx
items: Shock → isotonic resuscitation first; then oral/IV free water with serial sodium monitoring
★ Central → **desmopressin**; avoid excess water intake and monitor for hyponatremia
Nephrogenic → remove cause, low-solute diet, thiazide; lithium-associated → amiloride
Lithium toxicity → stop drug, isotonic fluids; severe neurologic effects/impaired clearance → hemodialysis consultation
Primary polydipsia → address cause and supervised intake plan; desmopressin risks water intoxication

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypernatremic encephalopathy, seizures, hypovolemic shock; overly rapid chronic sodium correction → cerebral edema
Desmopressin/excess drinking → hyponatremic seizures; chronic lithium → CKD

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Reliable water access, sick-day plan; lithium renal/electrolyte monitoring and avoidance of volume depletion
Mild lithium DI, intact thirst, normal sodium → **keep drinking**; fluid restriction risks hypernatremic dehydration

rows.label: Mimics
items: Overactive bladder/UTI: frequency without increased total volume
Postobstructive diuresis: follows relief of retention; monitor fluid/electrolyte losses

polyuria-diabetes-insipidus.evidence: Testing update checked 2026-10-30: [Endotext AVP deficiency/resistance, 2026](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279011/); classic testing patterns: established teaching.

post-traumatic-stress-disorder.name: Post-traumatic stress disorder
post-traumatic-stress-disorder.scope: PTSD diagnostic criteria (>1 month: intrusion, avoidance, negative mood/cognition, hyperarousal), acute stress disorder (<1 month), trauma-focused psychotherapy (CBT, EMDR), SSRIs, prazosin for nightmares
post-traumatic-stress-disorder.core: Persistent trauma-linked reexperiencing and avoidance with altered mood and heightened arousal cause functional impairment beyond the immediate stress response.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Exposure to actual/threatened death, serious injury or sexual violence; direct, witnessed, or qualifying indirect exposure
Prior trauma, psychiatric illness, repeated exposure, poor social support

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Intrusion**: nightmares, flashbacks, distress with reminders; avoidance of internal/external cues
Negative beliefs, guilt, detachment or trauma amnesia; hypervigilance, exaggerated startle, sleep disturbance
Dissociative subtype: depersonalization or derealization; severe distress may coexist with suicidality

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Persistent dysregulated threat response and impaired contextual extinction of traumatic fear

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical: ≥1 intrusion, ≥1 avoidance, ≥2 negative mood/cognition, ≥2 arousal symptoms
**>1 month**, impairment, and not better explained by substances or another illness
Assess ongoing danger, self-harm risk, substance use, depression and traumatic brain injury

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First-line **trauma-focused psychotherapy**: prolonged exposure, cognitive processing therapy, or EMDR
★ If medication preferred/needed → **sertraline, paroxetine, or venlafaxine**; premature ejaculation → paroxetine (delays ejaculation)
Prazosin for persistent trauma nightmares; monitor orthostatic hypotension, not an overall PTSD treatment
Avoid benzodiazepines; no established benefit and increased dependence risk
Immediate safety planning and psychiatric hospitalization when imminent self-harm or inability to remain safe

rows.label: Complications
items: Depression, substance use disorders, suicide risk, relationship and occupational impairment

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early practical support, **psychoeducation normalizing trauma reactions**; symptomatic acute stress → trauma-focused CBT
Avoid compulsory single-session psychological debriefing; maintain supportive follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: Adjustment disorder: stress-related distress without required trauma or full PTSD syndrome
Panic disorder: unexpected attacks without obligatory trauma-linked symptoms

table.title: Time course
rows: Full criteria first met ≥6 months later

postpartum-hemorrhage.name: Postpartum hemorrhage
postpartum-hemorrhage.scope: Primary postpartum hemorrhage (uterine atony, lacerations, retained placenta, coagulopathy), secondary postpartum hemorrhage (retained products of conception, endometritis), barrier methods, surgical management
postpartum-hemorrhage.core: Excessive bleeding after delivery demands simultaneous resuscitation and cause-directed control: Tone, Trauma, Tissue and Thrombin.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Uterine overdistention, prolonged/augmented labor, chorioamnionitis, magnesium, prior PPH → atony
Operative delivery → trauma; placenta accreta/retention → tissue; abruption/sepsis → coagulopathy

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Boggy enlarged uterus** → atony; firm uterus with bleeding → laceration or other cause
Jagged/incomplete placenta, vessels to membrane edge (**succenturiate lobe**) → retained tissue; oozing → coagulopathy
Shock exceeding visible loss → concealed hematoma; post-cesarean distention, hematocrit drop → **intra-abdominal hemorrhage**
Delayed bleeding >24 hours to weeks postpartum → retained products, endometritis or subinvolution

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Myometrial contraction compresses placental-bed vessels; failed contraction or disrupted tissue prevents hemostasis
Vulvar hematoma: **pudendal artery** branch, often operative delivery; vaginal/uterine arteries → deep or retroperitoneal

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Quantify blood loss; US definition **≥1000 mL or hypovolemia within 24 hours**, regardless of route
WHO 2025 earlier treatment trigger: ≥500 mL, or ≥300 mL with abnormal hemodynamic signs
Assess uterine tone, inspect birth canal/placenta; CBC, coagulation studies, fibrinogen and crossmatch
Ultrasound for suspected retained products; avoid delaying control in active unstable bleeding
Inversion: round fleshy introitus mass after cord traction, absent abdominal fundus, shock

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Hemorrhage team, two large IVs, warmed balanced blood resuscitation; massage, empty bladder, **oxytocin**
★ **Tranexamic acid within 3 hours** alongside first-response treatment
Refractory atony → **balloon/vacuum**, embolization if stable; compression sutures/arterial ligation or hysterectomy
Laceration → repair; retained tissue → evacuation; inversion → manual replacement before uterotonics
Endometritis → **clindamycin + gentamicin**

rows.label: Complications
items: DIC, AKI, shock, death; severe ischemia → Sheehan syndrome
Transfusion complications and hysterectomy-related fertility loss; delayed anemia impairs recovery

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Prophylactic **oxytocin after delivery**, active third-stage management and antenatal anemia treatment
Risk assessment, blood availability and team readiness; routine prophylactic TXA not recommended for vaginal birth

rows.label: Mimics
items: Amniotic fluid embolism: sudden hypoxia/collapse with DIC
Pulmonary embolism: hypoxia/chest pain without primary uterine blood loss

potassium-disorders.name: Potassium disorders
potassium-disorders.scope: Hyperkalemia, hypokalemia, cardiac membrane stabilization, shift therapy, elimination
potassium-disorders.core: Potassium abnormalities can cause weakness and fatal arrhythmias; stabilize cardiac risk while identifying the cause and correcting total-body balance.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hyperkalemia: AKI/CKD, RAAS blockers, potassium-sparing diuretics, tissue lysis, insulin deficiency
Hypokalemia: GI losses, loop/thiazide diuretics, hyperaldosteronism, insulin/beta-agonists, magnesium depletion

rows.label: Clues
items: Flaccid weakness, paralysis, palpitations; symptoms may be absent despite dangerous levels
★ **K ≥6.5 mmol/L, ECG changes, or rapid rise** → emergency; normal ECG not reassuring
Bradycardia/high-degree AV block with renal failure → suspect hyperkalemia; calcium before pacemaker

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Extracellular K changes alter membrane excitability and cardiac conduction
Acidosis/insulin deficiency shift K outward; intracellular shifts can coexist with severe total-body depletion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG + repeat potassium**, creatinine, glucose, bicarbonate, magnesium; assess drugs and acid-base status
Hemolysis, thrombocytosis/leukocytosis → pseudohyperkalemia; repeat atraumatic draw if clinically compatible
Hypokalemia: urine K distinguishes renal wasting from extrarenal loss; interpret with BP/acid-base pattern
Do not delay treatment for confirmatory blood draw when malignant ECG changes present

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Hyperkalemic ECG changes or dialysis-patient arrest → **IV calcium gluconate/chloride first**; protects myocardium only
★ Shift K inward: **IV insulin + dextrose**, nebulized albuterol; bicarbonate mainly with significant acidosis
Remove K: loop diuretic if urine output, selected binders; urgent dialysis for severe refractory/renal-failure cases
Mild/stable hypokalemia → oral KCl; <2.5, arrhythmia, paralysis, or no oral access → monitored IV replacement
★ **Correct magnesium deficiency** for refractory low K; never give IV potassium push; monitor glucose after insulin

rows.label: Complications
items: Ventricular arrhythmia, cardiac arrest, respiratory muscle failure
Overcorrection, rebound dyskalemia; insulin-induced hypoglycemia; IV potassium extravasation/phlebitis
Diuretic hypokalemia → **digoxin toxicity**, multifocal PVCs; check K first

rows.label: Prevention
items: Review supplements/salt substitutes; monitor K/creatinine after diuretic or RAAS-drug changes
Treat diarrhea/vomiting and underlying mineralocorticoid disorders; replace ongoing losses

rows.label: Mimics
items: Guillain-Barré: ascending areflexic weakness without explanatory electrolyte pattern
Periodic paralysis: episodic shifts, sometimes thyrotoxicosis; avoid excessive replacement causing rebound

table.title: ECG patterns
rows: Peaked T → PR prolongation → wide QRS/sine-wave
Flat T, ST depression, prominent U waves

potassium-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established electrolyte emergency principles.

preterm-labor.name: Preterm labor
preterm-labor.scope: Preterm labor (<37 weeks), cervical insufficiency, tocolysis (indomethacin, nifedipine), antenatal corticosteroids (betamethasone), magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection, GBS chemoprophylaxis
preterm-labor.core: Regular contractions with cervical change before 37 weeks; briefly delay eligible early births to improve neonatal outcomes, without prolonging unsafe pregnancies.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior spontaneous preterm birth, short cervix, multiple gestation, infection, smoking, uterine anomalies
Cervical surgery or prior painless second-trimester loss suggests cervical insufficiency

rows.label: Clues
items: Pelvic pressure, backache, increased discharge, contractions; assess membrane rupture and bleeding
Fever, uterine tenderness, fetal tachycardia → intraamniotic infection; maternal/fetal instability changes delivery timing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Premature inflammatory/uterine activation versus mechanically weak cervix with painless dilation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Sterile speculum examination** for pooling and cervix; ultrasound dates pregnancy and assesses presentation
Transvaginal cervical length; selected symptomatic cases: negative fetal fibronectin predicts low imminent birth risk
Collect GBS culture, urine studies; exclude previa before digital examination with bleeding

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Birth within 7 days, **24–33 6/7 weeks** → betamethasone; selected untreated 34–36 6/7-week pregnancies also eligible
★ Delivery expected <32 weeks → **magnesium sulfate** for neuroprotection, not primary tocolysis
Tocolysis: 48 hours for steroids/transfer; no maintenance; late-preterm steroids avoided with pregestational diabetes
★ **No tocolysis** with infection, significant abruption, severe preeclampsia, or fetal compromise; proceed toward delivery
Intrapartum penicillin for positive/unknown GBS; no routine antibiotics for intact membranes without infection

rows.label: Complications
items: Neonatal RDS, IVH, NEC, sepsis, cerebral palsy; magnesium toxicity → hyporeflexia, respiratory depression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Singleton short cervix ≤20 mm before 24 weeks → vaginal progesterone; consider at 21–25 mm
Cervical insufficiency/prior qualifying loss → cerclage; prior preterm birth + cervix <25 mm before 24 weeks
17-hydroxyprogesterone caproate withdrawn 2023; progesterone without short cervix not routinely recommended
Older exam questions may expect 17-hydroxyprogesterone from 16–20 weeks after prior spontaneous preterm birth

rows.label: Mimics
items: Braxton Hicks: no progressive dilation
Cervical insufficiency: painless dilation, minimal contractions
PPROM: membrane rupture precedes labor; distinct latency-antibiotic pathway

primary-immunodeficiencies.name: Primary immunodeficiencies
primary-immunodeficiencies.scope: Selective IgA deficiency, common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), X-linked agammaglobulinemia, severe combined immunodeficiency, hyper-IgE syndrome, Wiskott-Aldrich, chronic granulomatous disease
primary-immunodeficiencies.core: Recurrent, unusually severe, persistent, or opportunistic infections; organism pattern and age of onset localize the immune defect.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Consanguinity, affected relatives, male relatives dying in infancy; absent family history does not exclude disease

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Failure to thrive, chronic diarrhea, persistent thrush, or infections across multiple organ systems
Deep abscesses suggest phagocyte dysfunction; recurrent encapsulated bacteria suggest impaired antibody function

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Selective IgA deficiency: impaired mucosal defense; respiratory infections, giardiasis, atopy, or no symptoms
Antibody disorders impair opsonization; T-cell defects permit viral, fungal, and protozoal opportunists
DiGeorge: 3rd/4th **pharyngeal pouch** failure → absent thymus, hypocalcemia, conotruncal defects, T-cell infections
ADA deficiency: autosomal recessive SCID; toxic deoxyadenosine destroys T and B cells

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Start **CBC with differential, quantitative immunoglobulins**, HIV testing; assess vaccine antibody responses
Lymphocyte subsets distinguish B-cell and T-cell deficiencies; abnormal results → genetic confirmation
IgA deficiency: isolated IgA <7 mg/dL after age 4 years; normal IgG and IgM
★ Newborn **TREC screen** detects impaired T-cell production before symptomatic SCID

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Profound combined immune failure → isolation, irradiated CMV-negative blood products, urgent **transplant evaluation**
Acute infections: organism-directed antimicrobials; immunoglobulin replacement not useful for isolated IgA deficiency

rows.label: Complications
items: Bronchiectasis, chronic enteropathy, autoimmune disease; CVID additionally increases lymphoma risk
Anti-IgA antibodies can cause anaphylaxis to blood products

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Avoid **live vaccines** in major T-cell defects; immunize household contacts with safe vaccine choices
IgA-related transfusion reactions → washed cellular products or IgA-deficient plasma
CGD: TMP-SMX + itraconazole prophylaxis; genetic counseling for inherited defects

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vertical HIV: bacterial infections + zoster, nodes, maternal opportunistic infection; low CD4, positive virologic testing
Secondary hypogammaglobulinemia: nephrotic protein loss, B-cell malignancy, or rituximab exposure

table.title: Defect fingerprints
rows: Adolescent/adult; low IgG, poor vaccine response
Boy after 6 months; absent tonsils/B cells
Infant; absent thymic shadow, profound lymphopenia
Cold abscesses, eczema, retained teeth, pneumatoceles

primary-immunodeficiencies.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical immunology teaching.

psychotherapy.name: Psychotherapy
psychotherapy.scope: Cognitive behavioral therapy, psychodynamic psychotherapy, interpersonal psychotherapy, dialectical behavior therapy, supportive psychotherapy, family therapy, indications
psychotherapy.core: Match a structured psychological treatment to the patient's main problem, coping capacity, goals, and willingness to participate.

rows.label: Definition
items: Therapeutic alliance, collaborative goals, confidentiality, regular assessment of functioning and safety

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ Identify the **target mechanism** in the vignette before choosing the named approach
Insight-oriented work: psychological mindedness, stability, tolerance of emotional exploration

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ **OCD → exposure/response prevention**; panic → interoceptive exposure; depression → activation
PTSD → trauma-focused CBT, prolonged exposure, cognitive processing, or EMDR
Severe depression/mania/psychosis → add medication; immediate danger → urgent stabilization

rows.label: Compare
items: Motivational interviewing: explore ambivalence, elicit change talk; substance use/adherence problems
Coercive control/ongoing violence → individual safety planning before couples work

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Family participation needs consent**; protect adult confidentiality
Acute grief: validate and support; avoid forcing unconscious-conflict interpretation
Psychotherapy does not replace urgent suicide-risk assessment or protection of an endangered child

table.title: Approach → target → typical use
rows: Restructure maladaptive thoughts; practice new behaviors
Address grief, role transitions, interpersonal disputes
Validation, practical coping, strengthen existing defenses

pubertal-development.name: Pubertal development
pubertal-development.scope: Tanner stages, normal thelarche vs breast mass, premature adrenarche, precocious puberty, constitutional delay of growth and puberty
pubertal-development.core: Interpret sexual maturation by sequence, age, growth velocity, and bone age; isolated benign variants lack progressive gonadal activation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Constitutional delay often familial; chronic illness, undernutrition, excess exercise delay maturation
CNS lesions, gonadal/adrenal hormone excess, exogenous sex steroids can cause early puberty

rows.label: Clues
items: Girls: breast budding precedes peak growth, then menarche about 2–3 years later
Boys: testes enlarge before penile growth; pubic hair reflects adrenarche, not necessarily gonadarche
★ Asymmetric tender **subareolar breast bud** at expected age usually normal; hard eccentric mass needs evaluation
Rapid height acceleration, advancing secondary characteristics, neurologic symptoms → pathologic early maturation concern

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Central puberty: hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility → LH/FSH → gonadal steroids
Adrenarche produces adrenal androgens independently; peripheral hormone excess suppresses pituitary gonadotropins
Immature hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis → irregular anovulatory cycles, normal for 2–3 years after menarche
Virilized boy with **prepubertal testes** → peripheral androgen, usually adrenal; central puberty enlarges testes

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Precocious: secondary sexual development **before 8 years girls or 9 years boys**
★ Delayed: **no breasts by 13**, no testes ≥4 mL by 14; evaluate absent menarche by 15
Growth chart, Tanner examination, bone age; LH/FSH, estradiol/testosterone, TSH selected by pattern
Central precocity → pubertal basal/stimulated LH; brain MRI especially boys, young girls, neurologic signs
Peripheral pattern → targeted adrenal/gonadal tests/imaging; isolated adrenarche requires exclusion of rapid virilization

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Progressive central precocity → **GnRH agonist**; treat CNS cause when present
Peripheral precocity → remove hormone source or treat tumor/adrenal disorder; GnRH agonist alone ineffective
Constitutional delay → reassurance, follow growth; distress → specialist-guided brief sex-steroid course
Benign premature thelarche/adrenarche → observe progression; no automatic hormonal treatment
Pubertal gynecomastia, unilateral or bilateral, smooth subareolar → **reassurance**; no labs/biopsy; carcinoma very rare

rows.label: Complications
items: Early epiphyseal closure → reduced adult height; psychosocial distress
Missed hypogonadism → impaired bone accrual; untreated CNS/tumor cause may progress

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, manage chronic disease, avoid household hormone exposure; serial growth surveillance
Normal puberty + moodiness, mild parent conflict → **puberty education** for child, parents; no drug testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: Primary gonadal failure: high LH/FSH, low sex steroids
Permanent central hypogonadism: absent progression rather than eventual familial catch-up
Familial short stature: short parents, bone age matches chronologic age; constitutional delay: **delayed bone age**

table.title: Tanner staging anchors
rows: Further enlargement; menarche usually within 1–2 years

pubertal-development.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric endocrine timing and Tanner staging.

pulmonary-hypertension.name: Pulmonary hypertension
pulmonary-hypertension.scope: WHO groups 1-5 (PAH, left heart disease, lung disease/hypoxia, CTEPH, multifactorial), cor pulmonale, echocardiography, right heart catheterization, endothelin receptor antagonists, PDE-5 inhibitors
pulmonary-hypertension.core: Progressive exertional dyspnea, syncope or right-heart failure with elevated pulmonary pressures requires hemodynamic classification before vasodilator treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Connective-tissue disease, congenital shunts, portal hypertension, HIV, methamphetamine → PAH
Left-heart disease, chronic lung disease/hypoxia or prior pulmonary embolism are common secondary contexts

rows.label: Clues
items: Loud P2, RV heave, tricuspid regurgitation murmur; exertional chest pain or presyncope
JVD, hepatomegaly and edema → right-heart failure/cor pulmonale
Severe dyspnea with relatively preserved spirometry or low DLCO suggests pulmonary vascular disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pulmonary vascular resistance or elevated left filling pressure increases RV afterload
Sustained pressure overload → RV hypertrophy, dilation, reduced output and systemic venous congestion
Chronic alveolar hypoxia (COPD, OSA) → **pulmonary vasoconstriction** and remodeling → raised vascular resistance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Echocardiography** estimates probability and evaluates RV/left-heart function; not definitive pressure diagnosis
★ **Right-heart catheterization: mean PAP >20 mm Hg** at rest confirms PH
Precapillary: wedge ≤15 mm Hg and **PVR >2 Wood units**; postcapillary: wedge >15
★ **V/Q scan** screens CTEPH; normal perfusion essentially excludes chronic thromboembolic disease
PFT/DLCO, chest CT, sleep evaluation, HIV/autoimmune testing by history; vasoreactivity testing in selected PAH

rows.label: Tx
items: Oxygen for hypoxemia, diuresis for congestion; treat underlying disease and refer confirmed PAH/CTEPH
★ PAH → specialist **endothelin antagonist + PDE-5 inhibitor**; high-risk disease → parenteral prostacyclin
Vasoreactive idiopathic/heritable/drug-associated PAH → selected high-dose calcium-channel blocker; not empiric treatment
CTEPH → lifelong anticoagulation and pulmonary endarterectomy if operable; selected balloon angioplasty or riociguat
Do not routinely use PAH vasodilators for left-heart/lung-disease PH; PDE-5 drugs cannot combine with nitrates/riociguat

rows.label: Complications
items: RV failure, arrhythmia, syncope and death; pregnancy carries substantial maternal risk in PAH
Endothelin antagonists are teratogenic; some require liver monitoring

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid methamphetamine, address thromboembolic risk; vaccination, supervised exercise, pregnancy/contraception counseling

rows.label: Mimics
items: HFpEF: elevated wedge pressure identifies postcapillary cause
Deconditioning/anemia: no catheter-confirmed pulmonary pressure elevation

renin-angiotensin-system-inhibitors.name: Renin-angiotensin system inhibitors
renin-angiotensin-system-inhibitors.scope: ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, direct renin inhibitors, hyperkalemia, angioedema, cough
renin-angiotensin-system-inhibitors.core: ACE inhibitors, ARBs and aliskiren interrupt the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone axis at different steps.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ **ACE inhibitor or ARB**: hypertension with albuminuric CKD; post-MI ventricular dysfunction
HFrEF: ACE inhibitor/ARB when sacubitril-valsartan cannot be used; aliskiren lacks outcome benefits

rows.label: Mechanism
items: ACE cleaves **C-terminal dipeptide** of angiotensin I → angiotensin II; inhibitors block this step
Efferent arteriolar dilation → ↓glomerular filtration pressure; ↓aldosterone → potassium retention

rows.label: Adverse
items: Hypotension, AKI during hypovolemia; modest stable creatinine rise expected
★ **Angioedema → stop ACE inhibitor permanently**, assess/protect airway; possible even after years

rows.label: Avoid
items: ★ **Pregnancy**, bilateral renal artery stenosis, uncontrolled hyperkalemia
Prior ACE angioedema → no ACE inhibitor; subsequent ARB needs individualized assessment

rows.label: Interactions
items: ★ **Never combine ACE inhibitor, ARB, or aliskiren**; additive kidney injury and hyperkalemia
Potassium supplements, spironolactone, trimethoprim → ↑K; NSAID + diuretic → AKI
Sacubitril-valsartan requires **36-hour ACE inhibitor washout**; RAAS blockade can raise lithium

rows.label: Monitor
items: Baseline BP, creatinine, K → repeat within **2–4 weeks** after initiation/dose increase
Creatinine rise >30% → investigate volume depletion, NSAIDs, renovascular disease; reassess drug

rows.label: Traps
items: Advanced CKD alone → no automatic discontinuation; manage reversible hyperkalemia contributors first

research-ethics.name: Research ethics
research-ethics.scope: Institutional review board (IRB), vulnerable populations (prisoners, children), coercion and undue inducement, clinical equipoise, informed consent in research
research-ethics.core: Scientifically valid research requires independent oversight, fair selection, favorable risk-benefit balance, and voluntary informed participation with additional safeguards for vulnerability.

rows.label: Principle
items: Respect for persons, beneficence, justice: autonomy, minimize harm, equitable recruitment
★ **Clinical equipoise**: expert uncertainty about superior treatment; personal doubt insufficient
Vulnerability warrants safeguards, not automatic exclusion from scientifically justified studies

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **IRB approval before recruitment**; disclose conflicts, monitor harms, report unexpected problems
Explain purpose, randomization, risks, uncertain benefits, alternatives, privacy, injury care, contacts
★ **Ongoing consent**: check understanding, answer questions, update risks; withdrawal without penalty

rows.label: Don't
items: Coercion: threaten lost care, employment, grades, liberty for refusal; parole offer to prisoners
Undue influence: incentives distort voluntary judgment; reasonable reimbursement/payment permitted
Placebo causing serious harm by withholding proven care; disguise research as personalized treatment

rows.label: Exceptions
items: IRB waiver: minimal risk, impracticable otherwise, preserved rights/welfare; later disclosure when needed
Identifiable-data waiver: study also impracticable without identifiers
Emergency research: prior regulatory safeguards/approval; treatment emergency exception insufficient

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **IRB approval never replaces informed consent** unless an authorized waiver applies
Capable child's dissent generally respected despite parental permission
Therapeutic misconception: participant assumes every study decision maximizes personal clinical benefit

table.title: Additional safeguards
rows: Parental permission plus developmentally capable child's assent
Permitted research category; prisoner representative on IRB
Legally authorized representative; seek participant assent

retinal-vascular-occlusion.name: Retinal vascular occlusion
retinal-vascular-occlusion.scope: Central retinal artery occlusion (pale retina, cherry-red fovea, ocular massage), branch retinal artery occlusion, central retinal vein occlusion (blood and thunder, optic disc edema), branch retinal vein occlusion
retinal-vascular-occlusion.core: Sudden painless monocular visual loss requires urgent funduscopic localization and immediate assessment for retinal ischemia or venous obstruction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Arterial: carotid atherosclerosis, cardioembolism, giant cell arteritis
Venous: hypertension, diabetes, glaucoma, hyperviscosity; atypical young cases warrant targeted systemic evaluation

rows.label: Clues
items: Severe asymmetric retinal ischemia → relative afferent pupillary defect
Transient monocular blackout may precede permanent arterial occlusion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Arterial inflow obstruction → inner retinal infarction; venous outflow obstruction → hemorrhage and edema

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Dilated fundus examination** urgently; OCT quantifies macular edema
★ Retinal artery occlusion → **stroke-center evaluation**, carotid imaging, ECG and cardiac source assessment
Age >50 with headache, jaw claudication or scalp tenderness → ESR/CRP, CBC for GCA
Fluorescein angiography assesses venous nonperfusion and neovascularization risk

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ CRAO → immediate emergency/stroke referral; selected early cases → **IV thrombolysis consideration**
Suspected arteritic occlusion → immediate high-dose corticosteroids; never wait for temporal artery biopsy
★ **Ocular massage/paracentesis**: historical answers; unproven, potentially harmful, not recommended by AHA
Venous occlusion with vision-limiting macular edema → intravitreal **anti-VEGF** such as aflibercept
Retinal/iris neovascularization → retinal laser; systemic anticoagulation not routine for isolated vein occlusion

rows.label: Complications
items: Arterial occlusion: permanent blindness and future ischemic stroke
Venous occlusion: recurrent macular edema, vitreous hemorrhage, neovascular glaucoma

rows.label: Prevention
items: Control BP, diabetes, lipids, smoking; arterial disease → antiplatelet/statin or anticoagulation according to embolic source
Ophthalmic surveillance after venous occlusion for delayed neovascularization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Retinal detachment: flashes, floaters, curtain-like field loss
Acute angle closure: painful red eye, halos, high IOP

table.title: Fundus pattern
rows: Sectoral retinal whitening; corresponding field defect

rh-alloimmunization.name: Rh alloimmunization
rh-alloimmunization.scope: Rh(D) and other red cell alloimmunization (Kell, Duffy), anti-D immune globulin prophylaxis, indirect Coombs titer monitoring, fetomaternal hemorrhage (Kleihauer-Betke), middle cerebral artery Doppler for fetal anemia
rh-alloimmunization.core: Maternal IgG against fetal red-cell antigens crosses the placenta, causing fetal anemia, hydrops, and neonatal hemolysis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Antigen-negative mother/positive fetus; prior pregnancy, transfusion, bleeding, trauma, invasive procedures
Anti-D, anti-Kell, and anti-Duffy clinically significant; ABO incompatibility usually milder

rows.label: Clues
items: Often asymptomatic mother; fetal ascites, skin edema, placentomegaly, cardiomegaly
Neonate: early jaundice, pallor, reticulocytosis, **positive direct Coombs**; severe disease → cardiovascular collapse

rows.label: Pathophys
items: First exposure sensitizes; subsequent antigen exposure produces an anamnestic response
Kell antibodies additionally suppress erythropoiesis; low titers can still cause severe disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ First prenatal visit: ABO/Rh type + **indirect Coombs**; repeat before routine antenatal prophylaxis
Antibody → **paternal antigen typing**; negative (certain paternity) → no fetal risk; else fetal typing, titers
★ Critical titer, often **1:16**, or previously affected pregnancy → middle cerebral artery Doppler
MCA peak systolic velocity >1.5 MoM → fetal blood sampling; Kell warrants specialist surveillance
Kleihauer-Betke quantifies hemorrhage for dosing: **300 µg covers 30 mL fetal whole blood**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe preterm fetal anemia → **intrauterine transfusion**; near term → delivery
Neonatal hyperbilirubinemia → phototherapy; severe hemolysis → exchange transfusion

rows.label: Complications
items: High-output heart failure, stillbirth, bilirubin encephalopathy, delayed neonatal anemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Unsensitized Rh-negative mother: **anti-D immune globulin** at 28 weeks and within 72 hours postpartum
Sensitizing event → dose now; lasts ~12 weeks, repeat at 28; postpartum only if Rh-positive/unknown infant
★ Established anti-D sensitization → prophylaxis ineffective; no equivalent prophylaxis for Kell/Duffy
ACOG 2024: routine Rh testing/prophylaxis may be forgone for abortion/loss before 12 weeks

rows.label: Mimics
items: Parvovirus: nonimmune hydrops with negative maternal antibody screen
ABO hemolysis: may affect first pregnancy; fetal hydrops uncommon

rh-alloimmunization.evidence: Prophylaxis checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG Rh guidance](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/the-rh-factor-how-it-can-affect-your-pregnancy), [2024 update](https://doi.org/10.1097/AOG.0000000000005733); remaining content established teaching.

rhabdomyolysis.name: Rhabdomyolysis
rhabdomyolysis.scope: Trauma, crush injury, prolonged immobilization, statins, seizures, elevated CK, myoglobinuria (blood on dipstick without RBCs), acute tubular necrosis, aggressive IV saline hydration
rhabdomyolysis.core: Acute skeletal muscle breakdown releases myoglobin and electrolytes; recognize pigment nephropathy early and restore renal perfusion before kidney failure develops.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **Crush injury, prolonged immobilization**, compartment syndrome, ischemia/reperfusion
Seizures, strenuous exercise, heatstroke, cocaine; statins, especially with interacting drugs
Hypokalemia, infections, alcohol intoxication; pressure injury during unconsciousness

rows.label: Clues
items: Muscle pain, weakness, swelling; dark urine possible, but classic triad often incomplete
↑K, ↑phosphate, early ↓Ca; AST may rise from muscle rather than liver
Tense painful compartment, pain with passive stretch, sensory change → concurrent limb emergency

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Myocyte necrosis → pigment-mediated tubular injury and casts, amplified by hypovolemia and aciduria

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CK >5 times upper limit**, often >1,000 U/L; trend until clearly declining
★ Urine dipstick **heme positive with few/no RBCs** → myoglobin; negative result cannot exclude
Electrolytes, creatinine, ECG, urine output; CK magnitude supports risk assessment, not dialysis alone

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early **IV normal saline**; titrate to urine output 1–3 mL/kg/hour, avoiding overload
Stop culprit; treat heatstroke/seizures; compartment syndrome → emergency fasciotomy
Hyperkalemic ECG changes → IV calcium, insulin/dextrose; dialysis for refractory electrolyte/volume/acid-base disturbances
★ **No routine bicarbonate or mannitol** for AKI prevention; anuria → reassess fluids, renal consultation
Asymptomatic hypocalcemia → avoid replacement; symptomatic tetany or arrhythmia → calcium

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute tubular necrosis, dangerous arrhythmias, disseminated intravascular coagulation
Recovery phase → rebound hypercalcemia; excessive fluids with renal failure → pulmonary edema

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hydration and gradual exercise progression; avoid exertion during severe heat or illness
Review statin interactions, especially macrolides/gemfibrozil; pressure relief during prolonged immobilization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hematuria: numerous RBCs on microscopy
Hemolysis: heme-positive urine with anemia, ↑LDH, ↓haptoglobin rather than marked CK elevation
Inflammatory myopathy: subacute proximal weakness without acute toxic/traumatic trigger

rhabdomyolysis.evidence: Fluid targets and bicarbonate guidance checked 2026-10-30: [AAST consensus, 2022](https://tsaco.bmj.com/content/7/1/e000836.full.pdf).

salicylate-toxicity.name: Salicylate toxicity
salicylate-toxicity.scope: Aspirin overdose, mixed respiratory alkalosis and metabolic acidosis, tinnitus, hyperpyrexia, urinary alkalinization, hemodialysis indications
salicylate-toxicity.core: Aspirin exposure with tinnitus, tachypnea, fever, and a mixed respiratory alkalosis–anion-gap metabolic acidosis; normal pH can conceal severe poisoning.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Intentional overdose; chronic excess aspirin or bismuth subsalicylate, especially with renal impairment
Enteric-coated preparations or bezoars → delayed peak concentrations; older adults vulnerable to chronic toxicity

rows.label: Clues
items: Nausea, vomiting, diaphoresis; confusion, seizures, hypoxemia or hyperpyrexia signal severe toxicity
Children may have predominantly metabolic acidosis; chronic exposure may resemble delirium or sepsis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Medullary respiratory stimulation + oxidative phosphorylation uncoupling → hyperventilation, organic acids, heat generation
Acidemia increases nonionized salicylate → CNS entry; glucose utilization rises despite normal serum glucose

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Serial salicylate levels**, ABG/VBG, electrolytes/anion gap, glucose, creatinine; check acetaminophen co-ingestion
Repeat concentrations until declining with clinical improvement; one early low level cannot exclude poisoning
★ **Severity overrides the level**; falling serum concentration with worsening acidemia can reflect tissue redistribution

rows.label: Tx
items: Airway assessment, IV fluids, potassium correction; activated charcoal early if airway protected
★ **IV sodium bicarbonate** → serum/urine alkalinization; target urine pH 7.5–8; maintain potassium
★ **Hemodialysis**: altered mentation, oxygen-requiring lung injury, failed alkalinization, or pH ≤7.20
Dialyze if level >100 mg/dL; >90 mg/dL with impaired renal function; chronic toxicity needs lower thresholds
★ Intubation only if essential; **maintain hyperventilation**; neuroglycopenia → dextrose despite normal blood glucose

rows.label: Complications
items: Noncardiogenic pulmonary edema, cerebral edema, renal failure, hypoglycemia, death
Sedation or inadequate ventilation → rapid acidemia and cardiovascular collapse

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid aspirin for childhood viral illness; secure medications; reconcile OTC salicylate-containing products
Intentional ingestion → psychiatric assessment and suicide safety planning after medical stabilization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sepsis: infectious source; may share respiratory alkalosis and lactic acidosis
DKA: marked ketonemia and insulin deficiency; absent salicylate exposure
Toxic alcohols: osmolar gap early; methanol visual injury or ethylene glycol oxalate nephropathy

salicylate-toxicity.evidence: Dialysis thresholds checked 2026-10-30: [EXTRIP salicylate recommendations](https://www.extrip-workgroup.org/salicylates); other management: established toxicology teaching.

sarcoidosis.name: Sarcoidosis
sarcoidosis.scope: Noncaseating granulomas, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, pulmonary infiltrates, hypercalcemia, extrapulmonary manifestations (uveitis, erythema nodosum, neurosarcoidosis, cardiac), systemic corticosteroids
sarcoidosis.core: Multisystem granulomatous disease, classically a young adult with bilateral hilar adenopathy; treat threatened organ function rather than an abnormal radiograph alone.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Young or middle-aged adults; higher prevalence and disease burden among Black Americans
Familial predisposition; environmental antigen exposure suspected, without one established infectious cause

rows.label: Clues
items: Dry cough, exertional dyspnea; restrictive physiology and ↓DLCO; upper-lung interstitial infiltrates
★ **Löfgren syndrome**: erythema nodosum + ankle arthritis + hilar adenopathy; usually favorable prognosis
Uveitis, lupus pernio, parotid enlargement; facial palsy, hypothalamic dysfunction suggest neurosarcoidosis
★ Unexplained **AV block, ventricular arrhythmia, syncope** → cardiac involvement

rows.label: Pathophys
items: CD4-mediated granulomas; macrophage 1α-hydroxylase → ↑calcitriol, hypercalcemia/hypercalciuria, suppressed PTH

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Chest radiograph**, PFTs; baseline calcium, creatinine, liver tests, ECG and eye examination
Compatible presentation + **noncaseating granulomas** + exclusion of TB/fungi/beryllium exposure
Sample accessible lesion or EBUS-guided hilar/mediastinal node; classic Löfgren presentation may avoid biopsy
ACE level neither sensitive nor specific; cardiac symptoms/ECG abnormalities → cardiac MRI ± FDG-PET

rows.label: Tx
items: Asymptomatic stage I disease, preserved function → observation with clinical/PFT follow-up
★ **Prednisone** for progressive symptomatic pulmonary disease, significant hypercalcemia, cardiac or neurologic disease
Uveitis → urgent ophthalmology, topical or systemic corticosteroids according to severity
Steroid-dependent disease → methotrexate; refractory organ-threatening disease → specialist-directed infliximab
Hypercalcemia → hydration; restrict excess calcium/vitamin D and sunlight exposure

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary fibrosis, pulmonary hypertension, respiratory failure; nephrolithiasis and kidney injury
Cardiomyopathy, sudden death; visual loss; chronic steroids → infection, osteoporosis, diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: No established primary prevention; smoking cessation and vaccination reduce respiratory morbidity
Monitor treatment toxicity and bone health; individualize vitamin D replacement because calcitriol may already be elevated

rows.label: Mimics
items: TB/fungal infection: organisms or positive microbiology; exclude before immunosuppression
Berylliosis: aerospace/industrial exposure, positive beryllium lymphocyte proliferation test
Lymphoma: malignant tissue, constitutional symptoms; granulomas alone do not exclude concurrent cancer

schizophrenia-spectrum-disorders.name: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders
schizophrenia-spectrum-disorders.scope: Brief psychotic disorder, schizophreniform disorder, schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, mesolimbic dopamine
schizophrenia-spectrum-disorders.core: Psychosis with impaired reality testing: distinguish schizophrenia-spectrum disorders by duration, functional decline, and the relationship between mood episodes and psychosis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, neurodevelopmental vulnerability; adolescent cannabis exposure increases risk
Typical onset late adolescence/early adulthood; exclude stimulant, hallucinogen, medication, and neurologic causes

rows.label: Clues
items: Delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech/behavior; negative symptoms: avolition, alogia, flat affect
★ At least **two core symptoms**, including delusions, hallucinations, or disorganized speech, for active-phase diagnosis
Suicidality, dangerous commands or inability to eat → urgent safety assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **↑Mesolimbic dopamine** → positive symptoms; mesocortical → negative symptoms, early working-memory deficits
D2 blockade reduces psychosis but nigrostriatal/tuberoinfundibular effects cause EPS and hyperprolactinemia
Structural correlate: **enlarged lateral and third ventricles**, reduced cortical volume

rows.label: Dx
items: Clinical history, collateral information, mental status; assess mood timeline and substance exposure
First episode → CBC/CMP, TSH, toxicology; HIV/syphilis or neuroimaging for relevant risks/atypical neurologic findings
★ **Schizoaffective**: ≥2 weeks psychosis without mood episode; mood episodes occupy most illness duration

rows.label: Tx
items: Safety crisis → hospitalization; acute agitation → de-escalation, then medication if needed
★ **Risperidone, aripiprazole or olanzapine** + coordinated specialty care, family education, CBT, supported employment
Schizoaffective depressive/bipolar subtype → add antidepressant or mood stabilizer according to mood syndrome
★ Failure of two adequate antipsychotic trials or persistent substantial suicide risk → **clozapine**
Adherence difficulty → long-acting injectable (haloperidol decanoate); catatonia → lorazepam, then ECT if refractory

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, homelessness, substance use, cardiometabolic disease; antipsychotics → metabolic syndrome, tardive dyskinesia, NMS
Clozapine → neutropenia, myocarditis, severe constipation; monitor ANC and symptoms

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid cannabis/stimulants; maintenance medication, relapse planning reduce recurrence
Monitor weight, BP, glucose, lipids; address tobacco use and cardiovascular risk
**High expressed emotion** (family criticism, hostility) → relapse; family therapy reduces recurrence

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mood disorder with psychosis: psychosis occurs exclusively during mood episodes
Delirium: fluctuating attention/awareness and acute medical cause
Delusional disorder: ≥1 month delusions with otherwise relatively preserved function, limited other psychotic symptoms
Substance/medication-induced psychosis: recent stimulants (mydriasis, tremor) or corticosteroids, intact orientation

scrotal-masses.name: Scrotal masses
scrotal-masses.scope: Varicocele, hydrocele, spermatocele, testicular cancer differential, physical examination, scrotal Doppler ultrasound
scrotal-masses.core: Painless scrotal swelling requires localization: solid intratesticular lesions are malignant until proven otherwise; many extratesticular lesions are benign.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Testicular cancer: cryptorchidism, prior cancer, family history, younger adult age
Hydrocele: infancy/patent processus vaginalis, trauma, infection; varicocele from venous drainage anatomy

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Firm nontransilluminating intratesticular mass** → urgent malignancy assessment
Dull ache/heaviness may occur without acute inflammation; gynecomastia suggests hormone-secreting germ-cell tumor
New isolated right-sided varicocele or failure to decompress supine → evaluate retroperitoneal obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Patent processus vaginalis permits peritoneal-scrotal communication; epididymal duct obstruction forms retention cysts
Pampiniform venous reflux raises local temperature, potentially impairing spermatogenesis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Nonclassic or possibly solid mass → **scrotal Doppler ultrasound**: intra-/extratesticular location, blood flow
Classic left varicocele on examination → clinical diagnosis; **no imaging**
Examine standing/supine, with Valsalva; determine whether testis separately palpable and mass transilluminates
Suspected tumor → AFP, beta-hCG, LDH before surgery; staging CT chest/abdomen/pelvis as needed
Normal markers do not exclude malignancy; AFP elevation excludes pure seminoma

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspicious testicular mass → **radical inguinal orchiectomy**; avoid transscrotal biopsy
Offer sperm banking before cancer treatment; subsequent surveillance/chemotherapy/radiation depends on histology/stage
Newborn transilluminating hydrocele → routine follow-up, usually resolves within 12 months; no aspiration or imaging
Small asymptomatic hydrocele/spermatocele → observe; persistent symptomatic → elective repair
★ Varicocele with **infertility and abnormal semen**, pain, or adolescent testicular atrophy → consider repair

rows.label: Complications
items: Infertility, testicular atrophy; cancer metastasis to retroperitoneal nodes/lungs
Hydrocele may obscure tumor; treatment can impair fertility or endocrine function

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Orchiopexy for undescended testis** reduces infertility risk and facilitates examination; cancer risk persists
No routine population ultrasound or tumor-marker screening; promptly evaluate any new mass

rows.label: Mimics
items: Torsion: sudden severe pain, high-riding testis, absent cremasteric reflex → urgent exploration
Inguinal hernia: reducible groin-continuous swelling, cough impulse
Epididymitis: tender posterior swelling, urinary/STI findings, increased Doppler flow

table.title: Benign examination patterns
rows: Bag of worms; enlarges standing/Valsalva, decompresses supine
Cyst above/behind testis; separate, often transilluminates

scrotal-masses.evidence: Not checked online; established urologic localization and cancer-evaluation principles.

shock.name: Shock
shock.scope: Hypovolemic, cardiogenic, distributive (septic, anaphylactic, neurogenic), obstructive, fluid resuscitation, vasopressors
shock.core: Circulatory failure causing tissue hypoperfusion; normal blood pressure does not exclude early shock.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hemorrhage, GI losses, MI, infection, allergen exposure, spinal injury, thromboembolism
Recent surgery, immunosuppression, indwelling devices increase occult infection risk
Procedure bleeding: thoracentesis → intercostal artery, hemothorax; splenectomy → hemoperitoneum, left shoulder pain

rows.label: Clues
items: Tachycardia, altered mentation, oliguria, cool mottled skin; distributive forms may initially feel warm
★ **Anaphylaxis**: rapid airway swelling, wheezing, hypotension; skin findings may be absent
Neurogenic: **lost sympathetic tone** → hypotension, bradycardia or no tachycardia, warm skin after spinal cord injury

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Oxygen delivery falls below demand → anaerobic metabolism, lactate accumulation
Distributive vasodilation → relative hypovolemia despite normal total body fluid
Warm sepsis: high output, **high mixed venous O2**; pump failure: low contractility, congestion; hypovolemia: low preload

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Bedside ultrasound**: cardiac function, pericardial fluid, RV dilation, lung sliding, volume assessment
**Serial lactate**: hypoperfusion, best predicts course and mortality; trend with capillary refill, urine output
Septic shock: vasopressors for MAP ≥65 plus lactate >2 despite volume resuscitation
CBC, chemistry, ECG, troponin; cultures if infection suspected

rows.label: Tx
items: Airway, IV access; **isotonic crystalloid** (balanced, 0.9% saline) before imaging; restrict with pulmonary congestion
★ Hemorrhage → **control bleeding + blood products** (emergency O-negative); crystalloid as bridge; no vasopressors
★ Septic shock → antibiotics within 1 hour, drainage/debridement; crystalloid 30 mL/kg within 3 hours
★ Persistent septic hypotension → **norepinephrine**, MAP ≥65; add vasopressin, then epinephrine; refractory → hydrocortisone
Pulmonary edema after fluids → stop boluses, **inotrope**; children: epinephrine preferred, older exams may expect dopamine

rows.label: Complications
items: AKI, ischemic hepatitis, DIC, ARDS, bowel ischemia, multiorgan failure
Excess fluids → edema; vasopressors → digital/mesenteric ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early infection treatment, catheter hygiene, VTE prophylaxis, hemorrhage control
After anaphylaxis: trigger avoidance, epinephrine autoinjector, allergy referral

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vasovagal syncope: transient bradycardia, rapid recovery supine
Hypoglycemia: low bedside glucose, improvement with dextrose
Isolated head injury: hypertension + bradycardia (Cushing); trauma hypotension + tachycardia → assume hemorrhage

table.title: Hemodynamics and cause-directed rescue
rows: Decompress pneumothorax; drain tamponade; reperfuse PE

spinal-cord-compression.name: Spinal cord compression
spinal-cord-compression.scope: Neoplastic spinal cord compression (epidural metastases, dexamethasone, emergent MRI), spinal epidural abscess (fever, IV drug use, empiric antibiotics), cauda equina syndrome, surgical decompression
spinal-cord-compression.core: Back pain with new weakness, sensory changes or sphincter dysfunction requires urgent MRI to identify reversible neural compression.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Known breast, prostate, lung, renal cancer or myeloma → epidural metastases
IV drug use, bacteremia, diabetes, spinal procedure or immunosuppression → epidural abscess
Large lumbar disc herniation, trauma or spinal stenosis → cauda equina compression
Anticoagulation + epidural catheter placement/removal → **spinal epidural hematoma**: acute paraplegia, incontinence

rows.label: Clues
items: Progressive nocturnal pain, pain with cough/strain, radicular symptoms; deficits may be initially subtle
Cord lesion: sensory level, spastic weakness, hyperreflexia below lesion after acute phase
★ Cauda equina: **saddle anesthesia, urinary retention**, reduced anal tone, asymmetric flaccid leg weakness
Epidural abscess: fever/back pain ± deficit; classic triad often incomplete

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Epidural tumor, infection or disc material compresses neural tissue and impairs blood supply
Longstanding compression produces irreversible ischemic injury; bladder dysfunction signals advanced disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urgent contrast MRI** of suspected region; whole spine for suspected metastatic compression
Postvoid residual supports retention assessment but normal result does not exclude early cauda equina syndrome
Suspected abscess → blood cultures, CBC, ESR/CRP; image before LP
MRI unavailable/contraindicated → CT myelography; ordinary radiographs cannot exclude epidural pathology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Malignant compression with deficit → **dexamethasone immediately**, urgent neurosurgery/radiation consultation
Tumor → decompression/stabilization ± radiotherapy; choice depends on stability, neurologic function and prognosis
★ Epidural abscess → **vancomycin + cefepime**, cultures; urgent decompression for deficits or instability
Cauda equina syndrome → emergency spinal surgical assessment and **decompression**
Immobilize if instability suspected; bladder drainage and analgesia during definitive treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Permanent paralysis, bowel/bladder dysfunction, sexual dysfunction, pressure injuries and VTE
Abscess → sepsis; steroids can worsen uncontrolled infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Rapid assessment of cancer-associated new back pain; sterile procedures and prompt bacteremia treatment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mechanical strain: normal neurologic exam, no sphincter symptoms
Transverse myelitis: intrinsic cord lesion without external compression
Peripheral neuropathy: distal symmetric findings without sensory level

spinal-cord-compression.evidence: Not checked online; established neurologic and oncologic emergency principles.

spondyloarthritis.name: Spondyloarthritis
spondyloarthritis.scope: Ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis, reactive arthritis, enteropathic arthritis, HLA-B27, sacroiliitis
spondyloarthritis.core: Seronegative inflammatory arthritis characterized by axial pain, enthesitis, or asymmetric peripheral arthritis; identify associated skin, eye, bowel, and genitourinary disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Onset usually before age 45; family history and **HLA-B27** association, strongest in axial disease
Immune-mediated predisposition; preceding Chlamydia or enteric infection can trigger reactive arthritis

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Morning stiffness >30 minutes**, nocturnal back pain, improvement with exercise rather than rest
Alternating buttock pain, reduced spinal mobility/chest expansion; Achilles/plantar enthesitis, dactylitis
★ Painful photophobic red eye → **anterior uveitis**, urgent ophthalmology

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflammation at entheses and sacroiliac joints → erosions followed by new bone formation/ankylosis
TNF and IL-17 pathways drive disease; RF/anti-CCP usually absent

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pelvic radiograph** for sacroiliitis; persistent suspicion with normal radiograph → **MRI sacroiliac joints**
ESR/CRP support activity but may be normal; HLA-B27 neither confirms nor excludes disease
Effusion → aspirate if infection/crystals possible; reactive arthritis → exposure-directed Chlamydia NAAT

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Exercise/physical therapy + NSAID**, e.g., naproxen; avoid prolonged immobilization
Persistent active axial disease → TNF inhibitor, e.g., adalimumab, or IL-17 inhibitor, e.g., secukinumab
Peripheral arthritis → methotrexate/sulfasalazine, ineffective for purely axial disease; avoid chronic systemic steroids
Active IBD/recurrent uveitis → monoclonal TNF inhibitor preferred; avoid IL-17 blockade in active IBD
Treat active Chlamydia and partners; antibiotics do not routinely resolve established postinfectious arthritis

rows.label: Complications
items: Spinal fusion, osteoporosis and unstable vertebral fracture after minor trauma
Aortic regurgitation/conduction disease in longstanding axial disease; biologics → serious infection/TB reactivation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, posture and extension exercises; fall precautions when spine ankylosed
Before biologics: TB/HBV testing and vaccination; sexual barrier protection reduces Chlamydia-associated episodes

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mechanical back pain: worse with activity, improved with rest, minimal morning stiffness
Rheumatoid arthritis: symmetric small-joint synovitis, usually no sacroiliitis; anti-CCP often positive
DISH: older adults, flowing anterior ligament ossification, preserved sacroiliac joints

table.title: Phenotypes
rows: Psoriasis, nail pitting, DIP arthritis; pencil-in-cup
Postinfection oligoarthritis; urethritis, conjunctivitis may coexist
Crohn/UC; peripheral arthritis often tracks bowel activity

stable-ischemic-heart-disease.name: Stable ischemic heart disease
stable-ischemic-heart-disease.scope: Stable angina pectoris, exercise stress testing, stress echocardiography, antianginal pharmacotherapy, invasive coronary angiography indications
stable-ischemic-heart-disease.core: Predictable exertional chest pressure relieved by rest reflects myocardial oxygen supply–demand mismatch; new rest symptoms require acute coronary syndrome evaluation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CKD, older age, family history of premature CAD
Anemia, tachycardia, and uncontrolled blood pressure can worsen ischemic symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: Substernal squeezing, arm/jaw radiation; dyspnea or exertional indigestion may be anginal equivalents
Normal resting ECG does not exclude CAD; examination often normal between episodes
★ **Crescendo symptoms, prolonged pain, rest pain**, instability → ECG/troponins and ACS pathway

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Flow-limiting coronary atherosclerosis restricts supply when demand rises
Microvascular dysfunction can produce ischemia despite absence of obstructive epicardial disease

rows.label: Dx
items: Resting ECG, lipid profile, HbA1c, renal function; estimate clinical likelihood before choosing testing
★ Selected intermediate-risk suspected CAD → **CCTA or stress testing**, based on suitability
★ **Coronary angiography** for high-risk noninvasive findings, refractory limiting symptoms, or suspected high-risk anatomy
Stable on medical therapy, low-risk ischemia → no repeat testing or mandatory catheterization; respect informed refusal
Sedentary, risk factors, starting vigorous exercise: no routine stress test; older exam questions may expect exercise ECG

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Relief → **sublingual nitroglycerin**; avoid with recent PDE-5 inhibitor use or hypotension
★ Prevention → **aspirin + high-intensity statin**; manage BP/diabetes, lifestyle and exercise
Antianginal first-line: beta blocker or calcium-channel blocker; persistent symptoms → long-acting nitrate or ranolazine
Beta blockers improve outcomes for selected recent MI/reduced EF indications, not all stable CAD indefinitely
Refractory symptoms → revascularization; CABG improves survival in left-main/selected complex multivessel disease

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, heart failure, malignant arrhythmia, sudden death
Nitrates → headache/hypotension; combining beta blocker with verapamil/diltiazem can cause bradycardia/heart block

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, Mediterranean-style diet, habitual activity; cardiac rehabilitation when eligible
ACE inhibitor/ARB when hypertension, diabetes, CKD, or reduced EF; adherence and lipid follow-up
Drug-eluting stent → **aspirin + clopidogrel**, not anticoagulant; stable CAD 6 months; older exam questions may expect 12

rows.label: Mimics
items: GERD: meal/recumbency association, regurgitation
Aortic stenosis: exertional symptoms with systolic murmur
Costochondritis: reproducible focal chest-wall tenderness
Variant (Prinzmetal) vasospasm: rest/nocturnal pain, **transient ST elevation**, nitrate relief, normal angiography → calcium-channel blocker

table.title: Functional test selection
rows: Exercise stress echocardiography or perfusion imaging

stable-ischemic-heart-disease.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACC chronic coronary disease guideline summary (2023)](https://www.acc.org/latest-in-cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2023/07/17/19/06/2023-guideline-for-chronic-coronary-disease-gl-ccd/).

study-designs.name: Study designs
study-designs.scope: Case-control, cohort, cross-sectional, RCT, control selection, bias, internal and external validity
study-designs.core: Study design determines how participants are selected, when exposure/outcome are measured, and which associations can be estimated without avoidable bias.

rows.label: Definition
items: Internal validity: credible within-study inference; external validity: applicability elsewhere
**Selection/ascertainment bias**: institutional or already-ill sample misrepresents target population
Subjective scoring by different raters → **interobserver variability**; standardize criteria

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **Randomization balances confounders on average**; concealed allocation prevents enrollment bias
Blinding reduces behavior/assessment bias; intention-to-treat retains original randomized groups
Loss to follow-up can bias estimates when related to exposure and outcome

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Case-control controls → **same source population** that produced cases, independent of exposure
Prospective measurement improves temporality but does not eliminate confounding in observational research
Life table: poorest 1-year survival → steepest interval drop, not lowest cumulative point

rows.label: Compare
items: Confounding: third-variable distortion; randomize, restrict, match, stratify, or adjust
Effect modification: association differs across strata; report rather than remove it
Clinician-chosen treatment → **selection bias/confounding by indication**; randomization prevents it

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Case-control sampling cannot directly estimate incidence or risk** without additional population data
★ Cross-sectional data lack reliable **temporal sequence**; prevalent cases favor longer survivors
Random selection supports generalizability; random assignment supports causal inference

study-designs.evidence: Established epidemiologic definitions; no clinical guideline involved.

substance-use-disorders.name: Substance use disorders
substance-use-disorders.scope: Diagnostic criteria (mild, moderate, severe), cocaine use disorder, amphetamine use disorder, cannabis use disorder, motivational interviewing, cognitive behavioral therapy, 12-step programs
substance-use-disorders.core: A problematic pattern causing impaired control, risky use, social impairment or physiologic adaptation defines substance use disorder; severity follows criterion count.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, trauma, psychiatric comorbidity, early exposure, unstable housing and peer availability
Persistent psychosocial stress and limited treatment access worsen trajectory

rows.label: Clues
items: Tolerance/withdrawal not required; physiologic adaptation during prescribed use alone does not establish disorder
Stimulant withdrawal: fatigue, hypersomnia, depression and craving; assess suicide risk
Cannabis withdrawal: irritability, anxiety, insomnia and reduced appetite after sustained use
Caffeine withdrawal: diffuse headache 12–48 h after stopping intake, including NPO surgery; normal neurologic exam

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reward learning and neuroadaptation strengthen cue-driven behavior while impairing control
Cocaine blocks monoamine reuptake; amphetamines increase release; cannabinoids act mainly at CB1 receptors
THC lipophilic, adipose-stored: urine positive for weeks in chronic use; other drugs clear in days

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **≥2 of 11 DSM-5 criteria in 12 months**; severity **mild 2–3, moderate 4–5, severe ≥6**
Control/social: larger/longer use, failed cutdown, time spent, craving, role failure, social problems, abandoned activities
Risk/pharmacologic: hazardous use, continued despite physical/psychological harm, tolerance, withdrawal
Clinical interview establishes disorder; urine drug testing documents exposure, not severity or current impairment
Screen co-occurring depression, psychosis, HIV/hepatitis risk and polysubstance use; confirm unexpected immunoassay positives

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Motivational interviewing**: explore ambivalence, elicit personal goals, support autonomy; avoid confrontation
★ Stimulant disorder → **contingency management**, CBT/community reinforcement; no FDA-approved maintenance drug
Cannabis disorder → motivational enhancement, CBT and contingency management; no established approved medication
Peer/12-step programs as adjuncts; tailor outpatient versus residential intensity to safety/support and impairment
Stimulant agitation → benzodiazepines/cooling; uncomplicated cannabis intoxication, mild paranoia → observe, no drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Cocaine/amphetamine → MI, stroke, arrhythmia, psychosis; chronic methamphetamine → cardiomyopathy and dental injury
Cannabis → impaired driving, hyperemesis (cessation, fluids, capsaicin/haloperidol), anxiety or psychosis
Stimulant crash can precipitate severe depression/suicidality; withdrawal usually lacks alcohol-like autonomic danger
Older adults: new benzodiazepine (temazepam) → subacute ataxia, dysarthria, confusion, falls

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Harm reduction: **naloxone** for possible opioid contamination, avoid using alone, offer fentanyl testing access
Treat comorbid illness, relapse planning, overdose education and regular follow-up; recurrence prompts reassessment
Adolescent experimentation without impairment → counsel teen and family; no formal treatment program

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bipolar mania: episodes persist independently of intoxication
Primary psychosis: symptoms outside substance exposure periods
ADHD: longstanding childhood-onset pattern, not episodic intoxication

substance-use-disorders.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ASAM/AAAP stimulant guideline 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11105801/); DSM-5 criteria established definitions.

table.title: Intoxication by substance
rows: Mydriasis, hypertension, hyperreflexia, paranoia, pressured speech
Violent agitation, hyperthermia; formication with excoriations; MDMA empathic
Red conjunctivae, dry mouth, tachycardia, hunger, slowed time
**Nystagmus**, analgesia, hypertension, myoclonus; violent-catatonic fluctuation, mutism
Perioral/perinasal rash, solvent odor, ataxia/slurring; clears <1 hour
Coma, apnea, hypotension, bradycardia, sluggish pupils

surgical-wound-complications.name: Surgical wound complications
surgical-wound-complications.scope: Superficial wound separation, fascial dehiscence (profuse serosanguineous drainage, emergent reclosure), evisceration (sterile saline dressings, emergency surgery), wound hematoma, wound seroma, surgical site infection
surgical-wound-complications.core: Postoperative wound drainage or separation requires determining whether fascia is intact; fascial failure is a surgical emergency even without exposed bowel.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, diabetes, malnutrition, smoking, glucocorticoids, wound infection, emergency/contaminated surgery
Vomiting, coughing, ileus or strenuous activity increase abdominal pressure on healing closure

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Sudden profuse serosanguineous drainage**, popping sensation, or new bulge → suspect deep disruption
Erythema, warmth, worsening pain, purulence → infection; systemic toxicity may precede visible skin changes
★ Pain out of proportion, crepitus, bullae, rapid progression → **necrotizing infection**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Early wound tensile strength depends on sutures; collagen remodeling later restores tissue support
Dead space permits fluid/blood accumulation; infection and poor perfusion impair collagen deposition

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Inspect/probe separated incision gently using sterile technique to assess **fascial integrity**
CBC, culture purulent drainage; systemic illness → blood cultures/lactate
Uncertain deep collection, stable patient → ultrasound/CT; obvious emergency → surgery without imaging delay

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Evisceration: sterile saline-moistened dressing**, supine, NPO, IV fluids, antibiotics, emergency operating room
Never force exposed bowel back through wound; surgical exploration determines viability and closure
Cellulitis alone → cefazolin/cephalexin; purulence → drainage, add antibiotics for cellulitis/systemic illness
Polymicrobial deep infection → piperacillin-tazobactam; add vancomycin for MRSA risk
Necrotizing infection → immediate debridement + broad IV antibiotics; antibiotics alone insufficient

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess, sepsis, bowel ischemia, incisional hernia; delayed healing and recurrent separation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Preincision antibiotic prophylaxis, sterile technique, glucose control, smoking cessation, adequate protein/calories

rows.label: Mimics
items: Contact dermatitis: pruritic geometric rash matching adhesive, no purulent drainage
Normal healing ridge: firm linear swelling without progressive pain, erythema, or systemic illness

table.title: Stable localized findings
rows: Observe; aspirate/drain if symptomatic or persistent
Small stable: observe; expanding: evacuate, control bleeding
Open/drain if needed, dressings, secondary closure/healing

surgical-wound-complications.evidence: Not checked online; established postoperative wound and emergency surgical management.

syncope.name: Syncope
syncope.scope: Vasovagal / neurocardiogenic syncope, orthostatic syncope, situational syncope, cardiogenic syncope, breath-holding spells, cerebral hypoperfusion workup
syncope.core: Brief loss of consciousness from global cerebral hypoperfusion with rapid spontaneous recovery; identify cardiac danger before labeling an episode reflex-mediated.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dehydration, blood loss, autonomic dysfunction, diuretics, nitrates, alpha-1 blockers; prolonged standing, heat, fear
Structural heart disease, conduction disease, arrhythmias, family history of sudden death

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Exertional or supine syncope**, palpitations, absent prodrome, cardiac murmur → high-risk cause
Reflex prodrome: nausea, warmth, diaphoresis, tunnel vision; may include brief myoclonic jerks
Situational triggers: urination, coughing, defecation; breath-holding spells follow crying/pain in young children
Shaving, tight collar, head turning + bradycardia → **carotid sinus hypersensitivity**; confirm with carotid sinus massage

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Vasodilation/bradycardia, failed postural compensation, or low cardiac output transiently limits cerebral flow

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Initial **history, examination, orthostatic BP, ECG**; bedside glucose and targeted pregnancy/bleeding evaluation
Orthostasis: systolic fall ≥20 or diastolic ≥10 mm Hg within 3 minutes standing
High-risk → admission/monitoring; suspected structural disease → echo; intermittent arrhythmia → ambulatory ECG
Tilt-table testing for recurrent unexplained reflex/orthostatic cases; no routine head CT, EEG, carotid ultrasound
Typical breath-holding spells: normal development, awake trigger, rapid recovery; CBC/ferritin and ECG when evaluating

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Reflex event → supine, legs elevated; **hydration, counterpressure maneuvers**, trigger recognition
Orthostatic cause → replace volume, review drugs, rise slowly, compression; refractory neurogenic cases → midodrine
★ Cardiac cause → **treat rhythm/obstruction**, restrict unsafe activity pending evaluation
Breath-holding: reassure caregivers, safe positioning, treat iron deficiency; no antiseizure drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Falls, fractures, driving injury; underlying cardiac disease carries sudden-death risk
Recurrent episodes → activity limitation, anxiety; pressor drugs can cause supine hypertension

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid dehydration and prolonged immobility; individualized driving/activity restrictions after unexplained or cardiac events

rows.label: Mimics
items: Seizure: prolonged postictal confusion, lateral tongue biting; incontinence occurs in both
Hypoglycemia: persistent altered state until glucose corrected
TIA: focal deficit; isolated transient unconsciousness unusual

syncope.evidence: Not checked online; established syncope evaluation teaching.

systemic-lupus-erythematosus.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
systemic-lupus-erythematosus.scope: Diagnostic criteria (serositis, arthritis, lupus nephritis), neonatal lupus (congenital AV block), autoantibodies (ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith), pharmacotherapy (hydroxychloroquine, glucocorticoids)
systemic-lupus-erythematosus.core: Multisystem autoimmunity combining inflammatory joint, skin, serosal, renal, hematologic, or neurologic disease; flares often lower complement.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive-age women; family history; UV exposure, infections, estrogen-related triggers

rows.label: Clues
items: Photosensitive malar rash sparing nasolabial folds; painless oral ulcers; nonscarring alopecia
Symmetric nonerosive arthritis, pleuritic pain, pericarditis; leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, hemolysis
★ **Proteinuria, RBC casts**, edema or hypertension → renal involvement
Neonatal lupus: maternal anti-Ro/SSA or anti-La/SSB; congenital AV block may be permanent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Immune-complex deposition activates **classical complement**, consuming C3/C4; autoantibody-mediated blood-cell destruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ANA** sensitive entry test; anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm more specific
Anti-dsDNA titers, C3/C4, CBC, urinalysis, urine protein/creatinine, creatinine assess activity
★ Proteinuria **>0.5 g/g** or unexplained renal dysfunction → kidney biopsy
Classification: ANA ≥1:80, weighted score ≥10 with clinical criterion; clinical diagnosis remains contextual

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Hydroxychloroquine** broadly; NSAIDs for mild arthritis/serositis, glucocorticoids for flares
Organ-threatening flare → IV methylprednisolone; nephritis → mycophenolate plus belimumab/calcineurin inhibitor
Cyclophosphamide alternative for severe renal/CNS disease; taper glucocorticoids after disease control
Pregnancy → continue hydroxychloroquine; avoid mycophenolate, methotrexate, cyclophosphamide

rows.label: Complications
items: Accelerated atherosclerosis, infection, CKD; antiphospholipid antibodies → thrombosis or pregnancy loss
Hydroxychloroquine retinal toxicity; chronic steroid osteoporosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Sun protection; vaccines, cardiovascular risk control, retinal monitoring
Plan pregnancy during quiescence; anti-Ro/La positivity → fetal cardiac surveillance discussion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Drug-induced lupus: antihistone antibodies, usually no renal/CNS disease
Rheumatoid arthritis: erosions; fibromyalgia: pain without inflammatory findings

systemic-vasculitis.name: Systemic vasculitis
systemic-vasculitis.scope: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (c-ANCA/PR3), microscopic polyangiitis (p-ANCA/MPO), eosinophilic GPA, polyarteritis nodosa, giant cell arteritis, Takayasu arteritis, immunosuppressive therapy
systemic-vasculitis.core: Vessel inflammation presenting as unexplained multisystem ischemia: vessel size, organ pattern, antibodies and tissue distinguish the syndromes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autoimmune predisposition; hydralazine/propylthiouracil can induce ANCA disease

rows.label: Clues
